000020.text: Dongwha Pharm is Korea's first pharmaceutical company, founded in 1897 and listed in 1976. It makes and sells prescription and raw-material drugs, quasi-drugs, medical supplies and health supplements, and runs a pharmaceutical distribution chain. Its acquisition of TS Care in 2023 extended that distribution chain overseas, and it maintains the market positions of its main product brands.

000040.text: KR Motors is a motorcycle manufacturer listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It is the only Korean maker with large-displacement engines of 250cc to 700cc, selling mainly models of 125cc or less at home and 250cc or more abroad. In 2023 it signed an exclusive distribution deal with Taiwan's SYM, and it has launched electric two- and three-wheelers, including the E-LUTION.

000050.text: Kyungbang was founded in 1919 to make and sell cotton yarn and textiles, and listed on the KOSPI in 1956. Its textile division spins combed yarn and recycled-polyester blended yarn at a plant in Vietnam with 154,352 spindles and yarn-dyeing facilities. Its real estate division runs a shopping mall, a department store and a hotel under management contracts, and it has two subsidiaries.

000070.text: Samyang Holdings, founded in 1924, is the holding company of its group, with 6 subsidiaries. Its consolidated businesses span food (sugar, starch sugars, flour), chemicals (engineering plastics, semiconductor polymers), IT services and pharmaceutical R&D. It set up US and Japan units in 2025 and is building dedicated plants for allulose and prebiotics while developing eco-friendly materials.

000080.text: Hite Jinro is an alcoholic beverage company with 20 affiliates, including beverage and industrial subsidiaries. It sells soju and beer under several brands in Korea, and its bottled water brand has won a first-brand award for 18 consecutive years. It is also broadening its range of non-alcoholic drinks.

000100.text: Yuhan, founded in 1926 and listed on the KOSPI in 1962, makes and sells pharmaceuticals, chemicals, industrial and veterinary drugs, and household goods. Its drug business includes a non-small cell lung cancer treatment, its healthcare unit sells household products, and its overseas unit exports active ingredients for HIV and hepatitis C drugs. It has two main subsidiaries.

000120.text: CJ Logistics, founded in 1930, is an integrated logistics company operating 92 entities in 33 countries. It provides warehousing and distribution, port and heavy cargo services using Korea's largest port infrastructure, and parcel delivery using automated sorting facilities. It also offers air and sea forwarding and cross-border e-commerce logistics, and runs a construction arm that operates logistics centers and a golf course.

000140.text: Hitejinro Holdings was founded in 1933, listed on the KOSPI in 1973 and became a holding company in 2008. It oversees subsidiaries that sell soju, beer, bottled water and imported alcohol under several well-known brands. The company manages the group's brands and trademarks and provides funding and business support to its subsidiaries.

000150.text: Doosan, founded in 1933, controls a number of group affiliates. Its own businesses are an electronics unit that supplies copper clad laminate (CCL), a key PCB material, for AI and semiconductor uses, and a digital innovation unit that provides IT infrastructure, AI and cloud services. It is expanding CCL for AI accelerators and data centers and developing PFC for EV batteries.

000180.text: Sungchang Enterprise Holdings traces its roots to a rice-milling business started in 1916 and reorganised in 1931 after acquiring a timber company. It is now a holding company whose subsidiaries make plywood, particleboard and wood chips. The group is focused on reworking manufacturing processes, strengthening sales, and stabilising raw material supply to improve price and quality competitiveness.

0001A0.text: Deokyang Energen is a hydrogen purification company spun off in 2020 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026. It takes by-product hydrogen from chlor-alkali and petrochemical processes and refines it into high-purity industrial hydrogen of 99.99% (4N grade). It recently raised its stake in a logistics company to make it a subsidiary.

000210.text: DL Holdings, founded in 1939, became a holding company in 2021 after splitting off its construction and petrochemical businesses. It earns brand royalties, dividends and rental income and has 60 subsidiaries. Its segments cover manufacturing (petrochemicals, materials, auto parts), energy (independent power producer stakes and generation), and hotels, golf courses and property leasing, with manufacturing providing 84.9% of revenue.

000220.text: Yuyu Pharma, founded in 1941, makes and sells pharmaceuticals and health supplements at its own plant in Korea. It supplies prescription drugs to Korean hospitals and clinics, provides contract drug manufacturing, and exports finished drugs to Southeast Asia and South America. Its subsidiaries include YUYU VENTURES, YUYU BIO and MERVYNS PETCARE.

000230.text: Ildong Holdings was founded in 1941 and became a holding company in 2016; it has 8 subsidiaries. It earns income from investments, brand fees, management advisory and leasing, while its subsidiaries make and sell drugs and medical devices. Through its pharmaceutical subsidiary it pursues new drug development and overseas markets, and it also offers MIDD-based drug development consulting and IoT businesses.

000240.text: Hankook, founded in 1941 and listed in 1968, became a holding company in 2012 when its tire business was split off. After a 2021 merger with an affiliate, it created an energy solutions division and now makes and sells automotive and industrial batteries, including through US and German units. It also earns management advisory fees, trademark royalties, rent and equity-method income.

000250.text: Sam Chun Dang Pharm was founded in 1943 to make and sell pharmaceuticals and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2000. In 2013 it acquired Korea's largest maker of single-use eye drops, building a position in ophthalmic treatments. Its subsidiaries handle eye drops and other ophthalmic products, North American export approvals, and drug wholesaling in Japan.

000270.text: Kia, founded in 1944, makes and sells vehicles and belongs to a large Korean automotive group. It has 27 consolidated subsidiaries and runs plants in Korea as well as in the US, Slovakia, Mexico, India and China. Its line-up covers passenger cars, RVs including the EV6 and EV9, and commercial vehicles such as trucks and large buses.

000300.text: Dhautonex is an auto parts maker founded in 1967 that joined its current business group in 2024. It entered the auto parts business in 1998 with LPG fuel tanks and now mainly produces fuel storage systems and thermal management parts using welding and pressing technology. It supplies Korean carmakers and a major parts company, and is developing parts for electric and hydrogen vehicles, including liquid hydrogen storage tanks.

000320.text: Noroo Holdings, founded in 1945, became a holding company in 2006 and, although no longer classed as one under competition law since 2025, still earns holding, brand royalty and rental income. It has 26 subsidiaries in Korea and abroad, covering architectural and industrial paints, automotive paints, PCM coatings and agricultural life sciences. Its paint subsidiary produces tens of thousands of products and runs joint research on eco-friendly coatings.

000370.text: Hanwha General Insurance was founded in 1946 as a non-life insurer and listed on the KOSPI in 1975. It sells fire, marine, auto and long-term non-life insurance, and owns an Indonesian non-life insurer. It holds financial strength ratings of A or higher and an AA claims-paying rating, and is expanding in long-term insurance and digital channels.

000390.text: SP Samhwa, founded in 1946 and listed on the KOSPI in 1993, is a paint manufacturer with 17 affiliates in countries including China and Vietnam. It produces architectural and industrial paints, including powder, automotive and PCM coatings. Its 14 subsidiaries also cover IT services, freight forwarding, overseas property development and finance.

000400.text: Lotte Non-Life Insurance was founded in 1946 as a non-life insurer and listed on the Korea Exchange in 1971. It sells fire, marine, auto, specialty and long-term insurance as well as personal and retirement pensions. It is working to improve its product mix and underwriting, and has launched the ALICE and wonder digital platforms.

000430.text: Daewon Kang Up is an auto parts maker founded in 1946, with 4 plants in Korea and 9 sites across 6 countries. It is Korea's only full-line spring maker, producing suspension springs and car seats for Korean and global carmakers. It has set up an electrification research center and is developing motor cores and lighter, higher-performance springs and seats.

000440.text: Joong Ang Enervis was founded in 1946 to sell petroleum products and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1993. It buys gasoline, diesel and LPG from a refiner under contract and operates 7 gas stations, 1 LPG station and 1 oil depot in the Seoul metropolitan area. With electric vehicles threatening fuel retail, it is shifting toward real estate platforms and digital content.

000480.text: CR Holdings, founded in 1947 and listed in 1978, became a holding company through a 2023 spin-off. It earns trademark fees, dividends and management advisory income, while its subsidiaries make refractories and industrial furnaces and run golf course and real estate businesses. It acts as the group's control tower, looking for new businesses and strengthening its subsidiaries.

000490.text: Daedong is a farm machinery maker founded in 1947 and listed in 1975, with 14 subsidiaries in several countries. It makes tractors, combines and other farm equipment, cast products such as cylinder heads, and mobility products. It is developing smart farm machinery and aims to become an agtech and mobility platform company.

0004V0.text: NBR Motion makes rolling elements used in rotating parts of vehicles and industrial machinery, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026 as a technology growth company. About 90% of its main products go into roller and ball bearings, tying it closely to global markets. It has localised precision roller elements that were previously imported and plans to make ceramic balls for EVs from 2026.

0004Y0.text: DB Finance No.14 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

000500.text: Gaon Cable, founded in 1947, is one of Korea's three major wire and cable makers, producing power and communication cables. It runs 4 divisions: power, communications, special cables and wooden drums. It has 10 subsidiaries and recently took full ownership of a US unit to expand in North America and other global markets.

000520.text: Samil Pharmaceutical, founded in 1947 and listed in 1985, is a mid-sized drugmaker with subsidiaries in Vietnam and North America. It focuses on prescription drugs for eye, liver and digestive conditions, combining licensed-in products, generics, improved new drugs and exclusive imports. It holds Korean rights to Aramchol for NASH and Lorecivivint for osteoarthritis, and runs an ophthalmic CDMO plant in Vietnam.

000540.text: Heungkuk Fire & Marine Insurance was founded in 1948, listed on the KOSPI in 1974, joined its current group in 2006 and took its present name in 2009. It sells fire, marine and specialty insurance along with auto and long-term non-life insurance. It uses chatbots and RPA to improve customer service and pursues ESG management.

000590.text: CS Holdings was founded in 1949 to make and sell welding materials and split into a holding company and two operating companies in 2010. As the holding company it handles investment, with subsidiaries in welding materials, logistics and overseas operations. It uses the holding structure to give each business faster, more specialised decision-making.

000640.text: Dong-A Socio Holdings, founded in 1949 and listed on the KOSPI in 1970, is a holding company approved as such under competition law in 2014. It has several pharmaceutical subsidiaries and recently set up Dong-A Pharm (Hainan). Through its subsidiaries it covers drug manufacturing and sales, biosimilars, logistics, packaging containers and bottled water.

000650.text: Chunil Express, founded in 1949 and listed on the KOSPI in 1977, is an express bus passenger transport company. It is one of 8 express bus operators in Korea, running 120 routes nationwide. It also leases space in buildings it owns.

000660.text: SK Hynix, founded in 1949, is a semiconductor company headquartered in Korea, with 4 production sites, 3 R&D entities and sales units in the US, China, Singapore and elsewhere. Its main products are memory chips, centered on DRAM and NAND Flash, and it also runs a foundry business. It has 57 subsidiaries, including Solidigm Inc.

000670.text: Youngpoong is a non-ferrous metal smelter that began in 1949 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. The parent company refines zinc ingots, sulfuric acid and other non-ferrous products, while subsidiaries make PCBs and FPCBs and provide semiconductor packaging. Its electronics unit supplies HDI boards for smartphones and memory modules, and its package substrate unit is moving into higher-value products.

000680.text: LS Networks was founded in 1949 to make and sell footwear, clothing and outdoor and sports goods, and is the consumer goods arm of its business group. It runs brand, asset management and international trading businesses. Its main subsidiaries include a Toyota and Lexus dealership, the operator of the mont-bell outdoor brand, and an online brokerage.

000700.text: Eusu Holdings began in 1949 as a shipping corporation, listed on the KOSPI in 1956 and adopted its current name in 2014. It functions as a holding company, although it does not meet the legal requirements to be classed as one. Its subsidiaries develop software for shipping, ports and logistics and provide freight forwarding and contract logistics.

000720.text: Hyundai Engineering & Construction was founded in 1950 for civil engineering and building work and listed on the KOSPI in 1984. It operates in civil works, buildings and housing, plants and new energy (petrochemicals, gas processing, nuclear, renewables), and real estate development and resort operation. It has 48 subsidiaries, including an engineering company and a steel structures maker.

000760.text: Rifa was founded in 1950 to make and sell dyes, absorbed a chemical intermediates maker in 1982 and listed on the KOSPI in 1994. Its main business is domestic and overseas wholesale and retail of goods, organised into dyes, distribution of food and industrial additives and solvents, and property leasing. Its main subsidiaries are two real estate leasing companies.

0007C0.text: Acryl, founded in 2011, is an AI infrastructure company that listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025. It develops deep learning technology for NLP, AI platforms including a medical AI platform, and its own LLM, with the goal of specialising in affective computing. It also has GPU optimisation and resource virtualisation technology and carries out government-backed medical AI projects.

0007J0.text: Inventera was founded in 2018 to develop nanomedicines based on a nanostructure platform, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026. It is commercialising disease-specific nano-MRI contrast agents built on its Invinity platform, with pipelines for musculoskeletal, lymphatic and pancreatobiliary conditions. It plans to earn revenue from product sales and from global licensing and co-development deals.

000810.text: Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance, founded in 1952, is Korea's largest non-life insurer, with 3 domestic and 6 overseas subsidiaries. It sells general, long-term and auto insurance along with personal and retirement pensions and trust products. It also invests its roughly 108.4 trillion won of managed assets as an institutional investor in the capital markets.

000850.text: Hwacheon Machine Tool was established in 1945 to make metal-cutting machine tools such as CNC lathes and machining centers, and listed on the Korea Exchange in 1999. Its machinery business produces and sells in 6 regions in Korea and abroad, while its materials business serves Korea and Japan. It is developing high-speed, high-precision products and intelligent machining systems, and markets them in the US, Europe, India and emerging countries.

000860.text: Kangnam Jevisco was founded in 1952 to make and sell paints and pigments, and listed on the Korea Exchange in 1975. It has 3 divisions: paints for buildings, ships, cars and steel pipes; synthetic resins for electronic materials, shipbuilding and food packaging; and composite molding materials for auto parts and office supplies. It is pursuing air-purifying and antibacterial products, food packaging adhesives, polyurea and overseas markets.

000880.text: Hanwha, founded in 1952 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, grew out of explosives manufacturing. Its businesses span defence, shipbuilding, offshore, energy and finance. The explosives side covers industrial explosives, defence products and aircraft engines, while the financial side includes life insurance, non-life insurance and investment services.

000890.text: Bohae Brewery was founded in 1952 to make and sell alcoholic beverages and listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in 1988. It produces soju, fruit wines, liqueurs, rice wine, distilled spirits and whisky under several brands. Its food and beverage business centers on health drinks and household products made from plum extract.

0008Z0.text: S & SYS makes marine equipment and was set up in 2017 as an independent, employee-owned company; it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025. It supplies core ship systems, including power and eco solutions, and offers total solutions for shipbuilding and offshore. It consolidated SNSYS SINGAPORE PTE. LTD. to improve after-sales service in Southeast Asia and set up S&SYS(NANTONG) CO.,LTD. to grow in China.

000910.text: Union was founded in 1964, took its current name in 1977 and listed on the KOSPI in 1996. It is Korea's only producer of white cement, making white and tile cement at one plant and alumina and specialty cements at another. Its subsidiaries make ceramic components and ferrites, including in Vietnam, and wholesale interchangeable tools.

000950.text: Chonbang was founded in 1953 to make and sell cotton, wool and synthetic yarns and clothing, and listed in 1968. Its main business is textiles: it imports raw cotton and spins cotton yarn that it supplies to apparel, household goods and other industries. It is diversifying raw materials, improving production efficiency and quality, and developing new materials and markets.

000970.text: Korea Castiron Pipe IND, founded in 1953 and listed on the KOSPI in 1969, makes ductile iron pipes and coated steel water pipes at two plants, supplying public procurement agencies among others. It has 6 consolidated subsidiaries. They produce construction materials such as galvanised steel pipes and square tubes, and one runs a cosmetics business.

000990.text: DB HiTek, founded in 1953 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975, is a pure-play 8-inch foundry. It manufactures wafers on contract, focusing on higher-value specialty products such as power semiconductors, sensors and display driver chips. It is developing SiC, GaN and silicon capacitor products.

0009K0.text: Aimed Bio, founded in 2018 as a hospital spin-off, is a biotech developing antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) cancer drugs and is listed on the KOSDAQ as a technology growth company. It discovers antibodies using patient-derived models and has its own linker-payload technology covering the full ADC development cycle. It has licensed out AMB302 and signed agreements with partners including Boehringer Ingelheim.

001000.text: SillaTextile, founded in 1976 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994, belongs to a business group with 24 affiliates, 16 in Korea and 8 overseas. Its main businesses are property leasing and mobile phone sales. Its leasing business operates the largest used-car trading complex in its local area.

001020.text: PaperCorea was founded in 1944 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It makes industrial paper and newsprint at two mills and holds the top domestic market share in kraft paper. It is expanding production of eco-friendly materials and developing its former factory site in stages.

001040.text: CJ, founded in 1953, is a holding company with stakes in 8 subsidiaries. The group operates in 4 areas: food, biotechnology, logistics and entertainment, covering the global expansion of Korean food, amino acids, parcel delivery and content production and distribution. It has named Culture, Platform, Wellness and Sustainability as its future growth engines.

001060.text: JW Pharmaceutical began in 1945, was incorporated in 1953 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It researches, develops, makes and sells drugs, supplying original prescription medicines as well as over-the-counter drugs and healthcare products. In 2019 it acquired 100% of Euvipharm in Vietnam to expand into emerging markets.

001070.text: Taihan Textile was founded in 1953 for cotton spinning and weaving and listed on the KOSPI in 1973. Its yarn division imports and sells cotton, blended and specialty yarns and handles garment sales, while its fabric division dyes and finishes fabrics and sells fabrics and finished goods online. It has a trading subsidiary in China.

001080.text: Manho Rope & Wire was founded in 1953 to make wire rope, special steel wire and fiber rope, and listed in 1977. It has about 70 years of history and holds domestic market shares of about 20% in steel products and 25% in fiber products. In 2026 it acquired 100% of two companies that make robot controllers and electrical components.

0010F0.text: Bowon Chemical, founded in 1994 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026, processes plastics such as PVC, TPO and PU through surface treatment and bonding. Its products include surface materials for car interiors, flooring and wall materials, non-slip pads for display manufacturing, and EVA encapsulant sheets for solar panels. It runs joint R&D and exclusive production arrangements with its main customers.

0010S0.text: Wise Planet, founded in 2013, provides performance-based digital marketing services to advertisers across industries. It also runs brands itself, handling consumer data analysis, brand planning, product development, marketing, its own online stores and CRM. Its model is built on direct-to-consumer sales and its own WAPL work management system, and it is expanding its brands and moving into global markets.

0010V0.text: JPI Healthcare, founded in 1980 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025, develops and makes X-ray imaging components and diagnostic imaging equipment. Its main product is the X-ray grid, an essential part for sharp diagnostic images, which it supplies to about 300 global companies including GE, Siemens and Philips. It has 3 subsidiaries.

001120.text: LX International, founded in 1953, is a general trading company with 102 subsidiaries. It operates in resources, trading and new growth businesses, and logistics, with 4 domestic divisions, 7 overseas trading entities and 17 overseas branches. In 2024 it acquired a 60% stake in an Indonesian nickel mine, and it is expanding in eco-friendly power and IT components.

001130.text: Daehan Flour Mill is a flour milling company listed on the KOSPI in 1970, with 15 unlisted affiliates. It makes and sells wheat flour and animal feed, and is also active in forage, cargo handling and storage, pet products and food and beverages. Under its flour brand it produces flour, premixes, noodles and pasta, and it makes feed for poultry, pigs, cattle, fish and dogs.

0011A0.text: Axbis, founded in 2009, makes intelligent optical equipment that combines optics and software, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026. It supplies high-power laser solutions for manufacturing in EV/HEV, autonomous vehicle and UAM industries as well as batteries, camera modules and robotics. It is a small and venture business certified as a materials, parts and equipment specialist.

0011T0.text: Chaevi, founded in 2016, builds EV charging infrastructure and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026 under a special track for companies not yet profitable. It develops, makes, installs, operates and services chargers, with charging station operation and charger sales as its main businesses. It holds the top domestic market share in fast and ultra-fast charging, with chargers from 7kW to 400kW.

001200.text: Eugene Investment & Securities was founded in 1954, listed on the KOSPI in 1987 and took its current name after joining its business group in 2007. It reports 6 segments, including brokerage, proprietary trading, derivatives, futures brokerage and asset management. It also offers underwriting, M&A advisory, corporate finance, asset securitisation and project financing, and its main subsidiaries are an asset manager and a futures firm.

001210.text: Kumho Electric, founded in 1935 and listed on the KOSPI in 1973, makes lighting products. Its business is split into general lighting and LED lighting, with products such as fluorescent lamps, LED fixtures, flat panel lights, sensor lights, floodlights and streetlights. It has 5 affiliates, including units in Vietnam and China.

001230.text: Dongkuk Holdings was founded in 1954 as a steelmaker and became a holding company after a three-way split in 2023. Its main subsidiaries make and sell steel or provide transport and cargo handling, and its income comes from trademark fees, dividends and management advisory fees. It coordinates the group and seeks new businesses, while its subsidiaries pursue greener steel, smart logistics and overseas growth.

001250.text: GS Global, founded in 1954, has been a trading company under the GS group since its largest shareholder changed in 2009. It runs 4 businesses spanning steel, petrochemicals, energy distribution, imported-car PDI, special vehicle manufacturing and logistics, offshore wind foundations and EV mobility. It works through a network of 25 overseas locations and is expanding in eco-friendly businesses.

001260.text: Namkwang Engineering & Construction was founded in 1947 and went public in 1976. It carries out civil works such as railways, roads and bridges, and building work such as apartments and mixed-use complexes, for clients in Korea and abroad. It has 15 affiliates, 1 listed and 14 unlisted, and has completed about 38 overseas projects in countries including the Philippines, Angola and Vietnam.

001270.text: Bookook Securities was founded in 1954 as a securities firm and listed on the KOSPI in 1988. It trades and brokers securities, futures and options, sells financial products and loans, and covers investment dealing, brokerage, collective investment, advisory, discretionary management and trust business. Its subsidiaries include an asset manager and a specialised credit finance company set up in 2023.

001290.text: Sangsangin Investment & Securities was founded in 1954 and changed its name in 2019 when its largest shareholder changed. It is licensed for investment dealing, brokerage, trust, advisory and discretionary management. Its retail unit handles brokerage, its wholesale unit trades securities and derivatives, and its IB unit handles underwriting, M&A advisory, asset securitisation and project finance.

001340.text: PKC was founded in 1954 to make, sell, import and export chemicals, and listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in 1976. It makes inorganic chemicals, specialty gases and food additives used in petrochemicals, textiles, paper, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, displays, secondary batteries and food. It runs a consolidated subsidiary based in China to grow global sales.

001360.text: Samsung Pharmaceutical was founded in 1929 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975; it belongs to a group of 13 affiliates that includes its largest shareholder. It sells drugs and health foods, marketing prescription drugs through contract sales organisations and distributing over-the-counter drugs through an exclusive supply agreement. It has licensed GV1001 for pancreatic cancer and Alzheimer's disease and is developing it as a new drug.

001380.text: SG Global, founded in 1954 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, is an auto parts maker with a production subsidiary in Vietnam. It makes and sells seat covers and seats, manufactures and processes display parts, and leases property. It joins carmakers early in new-model development and is working on lighter seats, eco-friendly materials and smart seats.

001390.text: KG Chemical was founded in 1954 as Korea's first private fertilizer company and listed on the KOSPI in 1989. It is a holding company with 34 subsidiaries, including a carmaker, and runs 11 segments. These span chemicals such as construction materials, eco-friendly farm inputs and bio heavy oil, as well as steel, electronic payment services, car manufacturing and a coffee franchise.

0013V0.text: Samjinfood, founded in 2015, is a food company based on fish protein that integrated production, distribution and sales through a merger. It carries on a fish cake business that began in 1953 and has created a fish cake bakery category aimed at the premium market. It sells through bakery-style stores, directly run shops, online channels and exports.

001420.text: Taewon Mulsan was founded in 1955 under a different name, took its current name in 1968 and listed in 1975. It runs intellectual property, food and auto parts businesses. Its IP business holds character licensing deals with global entertainment companies and makes and distributes character toys and merchandise and hosts interactive exhibitions.

001430.text: SeAH Besteel Holdings was founded in 1955 to make and sell special steel, listed on the KOSPI in 1991 and joined its current group in 2003. After spinning off its operating business in 2022, it became a pure holding company. Its main subsidiaries make carbon and alloy special steels, stainless steel wire rods, bars and pipes, and high-strength aluminum alloys for aerospace and defence.

001440.text: Taihan Cable & Solution traces its roots to Korea's first cable company in 1941 and was established as a general cable maker in 1955. It makes and sells extra-high-voltage and power cables and is expanding overseas. In 2025 it acquired a submarine cable-laying vessel and an installation company, and it offers turnkey 500kV underground cable projects and holds international certification for 525kV HVDC cable.

001450.text: Hyundai Marine & Fire Insurance was founded in 1955 as a marine insurer and listed on the KOSPI in 1989. It provides non-life and third-sector insurance, along with building management, loss adjustment, IT services and asset management. It has 47 subsidiaries and is refining data-based claims and underwriting, investing in digital services and expanding overseas.

001460.text: BYC, founded in 1955 and listed on the KOSPI, makes knitted underwear and related products, both in its own plants and through outsourcing. It also runs construction and leases the property it owns. It produces from fabric to finished goods, holds ISO 9001 certification, and has an Indonesian unit and an advertising subsidiary.

001470.text: Sambu Construction was founded in 1948, received Korea's first civil and building construction license in 1965, and went public in 1976. It operates domestic construction, overseas construction and other businesses, with the domestic segment making up 99.87% of revenue. It has 10 subsidiaries, including one in Pakistan, and sold its steel division in 2024.

001500.text: Hyundai Motor Securities, founded in 1955 and listed on the KOSPI in 1990, is the only brokerage in its automotive business group. It provides investment dealing, brokerage, collective investment and trust services, along with foreign exchange brokerage, retirement pensions and MyData services. Its business spans brokerage and financial products, investment banking and asset management, and it holds an AA- corporate credit rating.

001510.text: SK Securities, founded in 1955 and listed on the KOSPI in 1986, is a financial investment company with 57 unlisted subsidiaries. It is licensed for investment dealing, brokerage, advisory, discretionary management and trust business. Its investment banking unit handles underwriting, M&A advisory and corporate fundraising advice.

001520.text: Tongyang was founded in 1955 as a cement company, went public in 1976 and has 11 unlisted subsidiaries. It operates in ready-mixed concrete and building materials, apartment construction, acrylic yarn and nonwoven textiles, and industrial blower plants. It runs 17 ready-mixed concrete plants nationwide and 3 aggregate sites.

001530.text: Di Dong IL was founded in 1955 to make textile products and listed on the KOSPI in 1964. It makes and distributes textile materials, aluminum foil for secondary batteries and food and pharmaceutical packaging, heat exchangers, gas filters and pollution control equipment. It has 10 consolidated subsidiaries, including production bases in Indonesia and Vietnam and aluminum affiliates such as one in India.

001540.text: Ahn-gook Pharmaceutical, founded in 1959 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2000, makes and sells pharmaceuticals and healthcare products. It runs a GMP-certified plant in Korea and moved its R&D center to a new headquarters in 2024. Its portfolio includes a number of cardiovascular drugs and cough and expectorant medicines.

001550.text: Chobi, founded in 1955 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, makes and sells fertilizers. It holds production licenses for about 675 products, including eco-friendly custom blends and Korea's first slow-release fertilizer, and produces about 280 compound fertilizers sold through agricultural cooperatives and dealers. It is developing eco-friendly fertilizers and replacing low-margin products with higher-value ones.

001560.text: Cheil Grinding Wheel IND was established in 1955 to make industrial grinding wheels, incorporated in 1974 and listed in 2005. It makes conventional grinding wheels and high-speed CBN grinding wheels used in steel, automotive, machinery and shipbuilding. Its affiliates include PT.CHEIL ABRASIVE INDONESIA and CHEIL VINA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY.

001570.text: Kumyang, founded in 1955 and listed in 1976, is a fine chemicals company that holds 11 companies, 10 of them overseas. Its main product is blowing agents used in car interiors, sneakers and insulation, and it also makes lithium secondary batteries and mills lithium hydroxide. It is pursuing lithium projects in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Mongolia and developing eco-friendly blowing agents and hydrogen fuel cells.

0015G0.text: Green Optics, founded in 1999, develops and makes ultra-precision optical systems and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025 as a technology growth company. It has Korea's largest engineering workforce and production facilities in its field, covering design through testing and evaluation. Its products are precision optical systems and zinc sulfide (ZnS) optical materials for defence, display, semiconductor and aerospace uses.

0015N0.text: Aromatica, founded in 2001, adopted its current name in 2014 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025. It is a clean beauty brand that makes and sells 100% vegan cosmetics based on essential oils, covering skincare, hair, body and home care. In 2026 it set up AROMATICA USA INC. to expand overseas.

0015S0.text: Fescaro was founded in 2016 as Korea's first automotive cybersecurity company. It develops and supplies security solutions such as FAST-HSM and FAST-SGW, starting with cars and extending to other mobility fields. Using its software capabilities, it has built BCM and ZCU capabilities needed for software-defined vehicles, and in 2026 it acquired stakes in two companies to expand.

001620.text: Kbi Dongkook IND was incorporated in 1955, listed on the KOSPI in 1990 and switched to auto parts in 1996. It makes car interior and exterior parts using plastic injection and blow molding, as a tier-1 supplier to Korean carmakers. Abroad it supplies Volkswagen, Audi, BMW and GM, and it has major subsidiaries in China, Germany and Mexico.

001630.text: Chongkundang Holdings began in 1941, was incorporated in 1956 and became a holding company in 2013 when its drug business was split off. It has 9 subsidiaries under competition law, and its income comes mainly from management advisory fees and dividends. Its subsidiaries make prescription and over-the-counter drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished medicines.

001680.text: Daesang was founded in 1956 to make seasonings and food additives and began exporting plants overseas in 1973. Its food business sells fermented sauces, seasonings, convenience foods and kimchi under its own brands. Its materials business produces starch sugars and amino acids such as MSG and lysine, and it is expanding overseas manufacturing and R&D.

001720.text: Shinyoung Securities, founded in 1956, is a financial investment firm with unlisted affiliates in asset management and real estate trust. It is licensed for investment dealing, brokerage, advisory, discretionary management, trust and collective investment. It offers MMFs, RPs, equity and bond funds, ELS, wrap accounts and retirement pensions, along with wealth management and HTS and MTS trading platforms.

001740.text: SKNetworks, founded in 1956 and listed on the KOSPI in 1977, has 30 consolidated subsidiaries. Its businesses include mobile phone and telecom distribution, network infrastructure management, global trading, car maintenance and parts distribution, home appliance rental, hotels and resorts, and data services. In the first half of 2026 it acquired two companies to strengthen its digital marketing business.

001750.text: Hanyang Securities, founded in 1956 and listed on the KOSPI in 1988, is a financial investment company. It is licensed for investment dealing, brokerage, collective investment, discretionary management, advisory and trust business. Its segments cover brokerage, proprietary trading and corporate finance, including underwriting, M&A advisory, asset securitisation and project finance.

001770.text: Shin Hwa Dynamics, founded in 1956, makes tinplate and other surface-treated steel; it listed in 1988 and took its current name in 2021. It also processes and trades steel sheet and leases property, and it is one of 3 companies serving the domestic market. It sells a butane can material co-developed with a steelmaker to the world's largest butane gas company, and secures captive demand through a stake in a can maker.

001780.text: Aluko, founded in 1956, is Korea's only specialised aluminum materials company, handling everything from molds to installation. It makes EV battery cases, mobile and display frames, solar module frames, auto and rail car parts, windows and curtain walls. It has 12 subsidiaries, including HYUNDAI VINA, and makes aluminum extrusions through a US unit.

001790.text: TS, founded in 1956 and listed on the KOSPI in 1968, is a mid-sized company with 14 consolidated subsidiaries. Its revenue comes from food (48.1%), livestock distribution (28.8%), feed (18.5%) and other businesses (4.6%). In 2026 it set up TS USA, INC. and SSJ Housing LLC, and through subsidiaries it has expanded into food ingredient distribution and contract catering.

0017J0.text: SEMI Total Solution, founded in 2014, specialises in automated material handling systems (AMHS) for semiconductor plants and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026. It develops, produces and operates clean conveyor systems and nitrogen purge systems. It has 2 unlisted subsidiaries and runs overseas business through a unit in China.

001800.text: Orion Holdings was founded in 1956 and in 2017 split into an investment holding company and a separate food company. Its main business is managing and investing in subsidiaries, with income from brand fees, rent and dividends. It has 18 consolidated subsidiaries, 2 listed and 16 unlisted, spanning confectionery, media and other businesses.

001810.text: Moorim SP, founded in 1956 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1999, makes printing paper in many grades in small batches, including woodfree paper, art paper and CCP. Its CCP premium packaging paper holds a 100% share of the domestic market. It sells through paper wholesalers and large publishers and owns a logistics warehousing subsidiary.

001820.text: Samwha Capacitor, founded in 1956 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, is Korea's only full-line capacitor maker. It produces almost every type of capacitor except electrolytic ones, including multilayer, film and single-layer ceramic capacitors. Exports make up about 70% of sales, spread across the Americas, Europe, Southeast Asia and Greater China.

001840.text: Eehwa Construction, founded in 1956 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994, is a general construction company. It initially focused on national infrastructure such as railways and roads. It now takes on building projects such as apartments, offices and pharmaceutical facilities, and civil works such as bridges and railways, mostly through joint contracts.

001940.text: KISCO Holdings was founded in 1957 as a steel company and became a holding company in 2008 when its operating business was split off. It controls subsidiaries through share ownership and earns dividends and management service fees. The group operates in holding activities, steel manufacturing, leasing and textile sales.

002020.text: Kolon was founded in 1957 as Korea's first nylon fiber producer and became a pure holding company in 2009 after spinning off its industrial business. It has 19 subsidiaries. It manages and supports its subsidiaries and also earns income from brand licensing, property leasing and management advisory services.

002030.text: Asia Holdings was founded in 1957 to make and sell cement and became a holding company in 2013, with cement and paper companies as subsidiaries. Its subsidiaries also run venture capital, recycled materials processing, farming, property leasing and park management. It focuses on accountable management at each subsidiary and on group-wide strategy.

002070.text: Vivien was founded in 1957 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, and is Korea's largest women's lingerie company. It makes women's foundation garments, lingerie and stockings under a range of brands. It has several subsidiaries, including two in China.

002100.text: Kyungnong was founded in 1957 to make and sell pesticides and listed on the KOSPI in 1977. Together with its subsidiaries it operates in crop protection, fertilizers, smart farming, insects, seeds and greenhouse construction. It owns 54.56% of a fertilizer maker, and the national agricultural cooperative is its main customer, accounting for 51.74% of sales.

002140.text: Korea Industrial was founded in 1957 as a construction company and listed on the KOSPI in 1991. Its main business is making and selling compound livestock feed, using corn, soybean meal and other ingredients imported from the US and South America at two domestic sites. It has 6 subsidiaries, and belongs to a business group led by another company.

002150.text: Dohwa Engineering, founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 2010, is an engineering company covering all areas of social infrastructure. It provides design and construction management for public infrastructure, EPC and O&M for renewable energy, and infrastructure maintenance. It also sells solar power in Vietnam, runs ESS projects in Korea, and is moving into investment development and PMC work.

002170.text: SYTS is a leather tanning company listed on the KOSPI in 1989. It imports raw hides and processes them into leather, selling both at home and abroad, with car seat leather as its main product. It has a subsidiary in China and also leases property in Korea.

002200.text: Korea Export Packaging Industrial was founded in 1957 to make corrugated containerboard and boxes, and listed on the KOSPI in 1974. It runs four plants with integrated production from base paper to finished boxes. Its box-making subsidiary buys all its corrugated board from the company and supplies boxes to customers.

002210.text: Dongsung Pharmaceutical, founded in 1957 and listed on the KOSPI in 1990, is a mid-sized company operating 13 sites nationwide, including a plant and research centers. It has 3 divisions: pharmaceuticals, hair dyes and cosmetics. It holds patents including a photo-immune cancer therapy and a cognitive health supplement, and is developing medical and functional cosmetics.

002220.text: Hanil Iron & Steel was founded in 1957 to make steel sheets and pipes, and split off its pipe business into a new company in 2003. Its main business is making and selling steel products, and it has diversified into warehousing, sea freight and leasing and sales of construction equipment. It has unlisted affiliates in shipping and in China.

002230.text: PS Tec, founded in 1957 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1990, makes power equipment. It develops and supplies electricity, gas, water and hot-water meters, heat meters, AMR remote meter-reading systems and energy management systems such as ZEMS. It acquired a new plant in 2024 for eco-friendly switchgear, set up a unit in Ghana in 2025, and has a solar power subsidiary.

002240.text: Kiswire was founded in 1945 to make wire rope, hard-drawn wire and other special wire products, and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It operates a rope segment, a wire segment producing hard-drawn and bead wire, and a leasing segment. Its products go to the auto, mining, shipping and fishing, and machinery industries, and it has 24 unlisted subsidiaries.

002290.text: Samil Enterprise, founded in 1958 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1992, is a general construction company. It builds projects for US forces in Korea, public and private buildings, and civil works such as roads, ports, bridges and site preparation. It has also carried out precision plant work in industrial complexes and leases part of its headquarters building.

002310.text: Asia Paper Manufacturing was founded in 1958, moved into industrial paper and listed on the KOSPI in 1988; it is a subsidiary of a larger group company. It makes and sells industrial paper such as containerboard, and through subsidiaries makes corrugated board and boxes and collects recycled materials. It is vertically integrated and is expanding eco-friendly and air quality businesses.

002320.text: Hanjin Logistics, founded in 1958, is an integrated logistics company with 27 consolidated subsidiaries. It provides B2C and B2B parcel delivery, global logistics, trucking, port handling, shipping and logistics center operations, and has expanded into countries such as Thailand, Russia and Singapore since 2024. It is also growing digital platforms, including the SWOOP fashion platform, as well as EV charging and solar power.

002350.text: Nexen Tire, founded in 1958 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, is a global tire company with 4 production bases, two in Korea and one each in China and the Czech Republic. It is expanding its European plant in a second phase to build out its global production capacity. It makes, sells and rents tires, and through subsidiaries also makes molds and runs a bakery business.

002360.text: SH Energy & Chemical was founded in 1958 to make and sell synthetic resins and plastics. It produces EPS resin and Nylon-12 fine powder, develops shale gas, and provides investment and management consulting. In 2008 it set up SH Energy USA for natural gas development in the US, and it has acquired a stake in a real estate asset manager.

002380.text: KCC was founded in 1958, took its current name in 2005 and is Korea's largest building materials and fine chemicals company. It operates in building materials, paints and silicones, and strengthened its silicone business by acquiring Momentive Performance Materials in the US in 2019. It is developing eco-friendly products, supplying materials for power systems used in AI, and expanding capacity in Vietnam.

002390.text: Handok was founded in 1954 to repackage, make and sell pharmaceuticals and chemicals, and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It makes and sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs, sells medical devices and diagnostic reagents, provides contract manufacturing and QC services, and leases property. It has 5 unlisted subsidiaries.

002410.text: Bumyang Construction, founded in 1958 and listed on the KOSPI in 1988, has 8 subsidiaries. It builds apartments and officetels, roads and tunnels, runs cold-storage logistics, makes modular housing and develops property. It is also running corporate rental housing projects.

002420.text: Wooyang P&L, founded in 1958 and listed on the KOSPI in 1968, completed a merger with its grandparent company in 2026. It runs petroleum sales, culture and leisure, and leasing divisions, having closed its cinema business in 2024. The petroleum division operates 7 gas stations, the leisure division runs a character IP business, and the leasing division hosts immersive performances.

002450.text: Samick Musical Instruments, founded in 1958 and listed on the KOSPI in 1988, is Korea's largest musical instrument company. It makes and sells upright, grand and digital pianos, guitars, violins and other instruments through 15 overseas production and sales units in countries including Indonesia, the US, China and Germany. A subsidiary also runs a district energy business supplying heating and cooling to households.

002460.text: HS Hwasung was founded in 1958 as a regional civil engineering company and listed on the KOSPI in 1988. It ranks 48th in the 2026 construction capability rankings and, after selling its former retail business, focuses on construction. Its segments cover building, civil works and property sales, including public facilities, commercial buildings and apartments.

002600.text: Choheung was founded in 1959 to make basic chemicals and now makes food and food additives. Cheese accounts for 60.5% of revenue and food and food additives for 39.5%. Its subsidiary, set up in 2010, makes mozzarella and other cheeses.

002620.text: Jeil Pharma Holdings was founded in 1959, listed in 1988 and became a holding company in 2017. It owns 49.2% of its listed pharmaceutical subsidiary, 92.4% of an unlisted health science company and 100% of another unlisted company. It earns investment income, brand fees and advisory fees, while its subsidiaries make and sell prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

002630.text: Orientbio was founded in 1959 as a watchmaker and became a life sciences R&D company after a merger in 2003. It produces biological research materials under an exclusive technology partnership with Charles River Laboratories of the US, and develops medical and laboratory equipment and hair growth treatments. It has 15 affiliates and runs ORIENTCAM in Cambodia.

002680.text: Hantop, founded in 1959 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1995, makes and sells wheat flour and compound animal feed. It runs a flour mill and a feed plant in Korea. Its subsidiaries work in medical devices, protective tape (CHOICE PRO-TECH), car repair, livestock farming, venture capital and food processing.

002690.text: Dong IL Steel MFG was founded in 1959 to make wire rods and steel strand, and listed on the KOSPI in 2015. Its businesses are wire products, drawn bars and aluminum bars, including PC strand for infrastructure projects and hard-drawn wire for cars and industrial machinery. It is expanding its semiconductor-related sales and adding production capacity.

002700.text: Shinil Electronics, founded in 1959 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975, makes small home appliances. Its range includes summer products such as fans, dehumidifiers and portable air conditioners, heating products for winter, and general household appliances. It focuses on higher-value models to set itself apart from low-priced Chinese products, and sells through large discount stores and dealers nationwide.

002710.text: TCC Steel was founded in 1959 to make surface-treated steel sheet and listed on the KOSPI in 1984. It produces tinplate and electrolytic chromium-coated steel, with the stated aim of adding value to steel through eco-friendly materials. It has 7 consolidated subsidiaries, including TCC America Corp.

002720.text: Kukje Pharma, founded in 1959 and listed in 1975, makes and sells pharmaceuticals. It sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs and quasi-drugs, including eye drops, through a nationwide sales network. It has 2 new drugs and 2 improved new drugs in research, holds 10 patents, and owns a subsidiary that sells and rents medical devices and welfare aids.

002760.text: Bolak, founded in 1959 and listed on the KOSPI in 1989, is a small company operating from a single site in Korea. It makes and sells food additives and active pharmaceutical ingredients, including food flavors, herbal ingredients, functional food materials and natural cosmetic ingredients. It focuses on natural food additives in response to demand for natural ingredients.

002780.text: Chinhung International was founded in 1959 for civil and building construction and housing, and listed on the KOSPI in 1977. Since joining its current group in 2008 it has built up its housing business and now markets apartments under a joint brand with its parent company. It works in civil engineering, building and housing, and plants, for both public and private clients.

002790.text: Amorepacific Holdings, founded in 1959, is a pure holding company that transferred its cosmetics, household goods and food businesses to a new operating company in 2006. It has 8 subsidiaries, and cosmetics account for 95% of revenue, with other businesses making up 5%. Its subsidiaries run luxury and premium cosmetics brands and hair and beauty brands.

002800.text: Sinsin Pharmaceutical was founded in 1959 to make and sell pharmaceuticals and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. It specialises in pain relief patches, liquid and spray products, and makes and sells about 100 over-the-counter drugs. It runs sales branches nationwide, deals directly with retail pharmacies, and is expanding exports to Southeast Asia, Asia and Europe.

002810.text: Samyung Trading was founded in 1959 as an import-export and trade agency business. Its main businesses are selling industrial chemicals and plastic eyeglass lenses, while its subsidiaries make car interior and exterior parts. It works with domestic and overseas chemical makers for stable supply and is developing eco-friendly patterns and paints and automating processes.

002820.text: SUN & L, founded in 1959 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, added household goods in 2021 by merging with a subsidiary. Its wood division processes plywood and distributes timber, its interior division makes, sells and installs doors, furniture and interiors, and its household goods division makes pump dispensers and cosmetic containers. It has 12 consolidated subsidiaries.

002840.text: Miwon Commercial was founded in 1959 around sulfuric acid and powdered sulfur and listed on the KOSPI in 1989; it now makes advanced chemical products. Its household chemicals unit supplies surfactants and conditioning polymers, and its electronic materials unit supplies process chemicals for OLED, TFT-LCD and chip packaging, as well as photoresist raw materials. A subsidiary sells surfactants, paint additives and photoinitiators in China.

002870.text: Shinpoong, founded in 1960 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976, distributes paper and has 3 subsidiaries. After halting production at its factory in 2019, it moved from manufacturing to distribution, buying paper from domestic and overseas mills and brokering sales through a customer network built over about 60 years. It has installed converting equipment to broaden the products it sells.

002880.text: Dya, founded in 1960 and listed on the KOSPI in 1977, is an auto parts maker. Its two seat divisions supply car seats for a range of SUV, sedan and EV models to Korean carmakers. It has won orders for seats in new models and is expanding the business.

002900.text: TYM was founded in 1951 and listed in 1973. It runs farm machinery and cigarette filter businesses, with farm machinery making up 93% of sales and tractors about 78% of that. It has passed a national type test for autonomous driving and is expanding in North America, Europe and Southeast Asia; its subsidiaries include TYM North America and TYMICT.

002920.text: Yoosung Enterprise makes parts for internal combustion engines, including piston rings, cylinder liners and camshafts, which it supplies to Korean carmakers and a construction equipment maker and exports worldwide. Founded in 1960, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988. It has 4 affiliates, among them a joint venture with Japan's TPR, a wholly owned subsidiary, a unit in China and an electric vehicle powertrain company.

002960.text: Hankook Shell Oil produces lubricants and greases for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, industry and ships. Set up in 1960 to make and sell lubricants, it formed a joint venture with Shell in 1969 and is part of the Shell plc group, the world's largest lubricant supplier by market share. It is widening its premium and eco-friendly product lines and has introduced Midel, an eco-friendly electrical insulating fluid, for the power and utility sectors.

002990.text: Kumho Engineering & Construction works across the construction sector, including building, housing, civil engineering, plant and environmental projects, and sells homes under its ARTERA brand. Founded in 1960 under a different name, it expanded into all areas of construction through an acquisition in 1967 and took its current name in 2021. It has 3 domestic and 2 overseas consolidated subsidiaries.

003000.text: Bukwang Pharmaceutical IND is a drugmaker founded in 1960 whose business covers medicines, health functional foods and quasi-drugs. It has 4 subsidiaries, including Contera Pharma, and pursues new drug development through open innovation. Contera Pharma is running clinical trials of CP-012, a Parkinson's disease treatment, and the company also has research collaborations on RNA therapies.

003010.text: Haein is an energy, power and construction machinery group that supplies engines, generator sets and construction equipment under dealership agreements with global brands such as Caterpillar, Jungheinrich and Vermeer. It also provides maintenance services at its first plant, equipment rental, used equipment trading and a renewable energy business. Founded in 1960, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988.

003030.text: SeAH Steel Holdings is a pure holding company that was founded in 1960 as a steel pipe maker and became a holding company through a spin-off in 2018. It has 19 subsidiaries including overseas affiliates, most of which make and sell steel products. Its pipe business produces piping, oil country and structural pipes, and its sheet business makes color-coated, galvanized and pickled steel sheets.

003060.text: Aprogen Biologics makes and sells pharmaceuticals and has been listed since 1984. Founded in 1960, it added a biopharmaceutical division in 2022 by merging with an affiliate that had biologics production facilities and technology. Its pharmaceutical division makes generic drugs such as circulatory and central nervous system treatments, while the bio division produces biologics using perfusion technology.

003070.text: Kolon Global runs a construction business covering housing, civil engineering and renewable energy, and a trading business dealing in steel, defense goods and other products. Founded in 1960 and listed in 1978, it took its current name in 2011 after a merger. In 2025 it absorbed two companies to expand its leisure and AM businesses.

003080.text: Sbsungbo makes and sells crop protection products, including fungicides, herbicides and insecticides, selling to wholesalers and retailers through regional offices and a nationwide sales network. It was founded in 1961 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It has two subsidiaries that are agricultural companies.

003090.text: Daewoong is a holding company founded in 1961 that adopted its holding structure in 2002 and has 36 subsidiaries. Its main subsidiary is a drugmaker whose products include a botulinum toxin, while other units make active pharmaceutical ingredients and develop biologic drugs. The company itself invests in digital healthcare and new drug development.

0030R0.text: Daishin Value REIT is a real estate investment company listed on the KOSPI. It invests in property and pays shareholders dividends from the income, rather than running an operating business.

003100.text: Sun Kwang is a logistics company founded in 1948 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1999, with 3 subsidiaries. It unloads, stores and transports grain using silos at two ports and operates a container terminal at a new port. It uses automated and eco-friendly systems and equipment such as STS and ARMGC.

003120.text: Ilsung IS makes and sells medicines, developing and producing treatments including antibiotics, bone disease drugs and anesthetics. It began its drug business in 1954, was formally launched under a former name in 1961 and listed on the stock exchange in 1985. It invests in biotech ventures and pursues global partnerships.

003160.text: Di was founded in 1961 to make and sell semiconductor test equipment and listed on the KOSPI in 1996. Its businesses include semiconductor equipment, electronic components such as EMC shielding, and importing and selling overseas high-end audio brands. It has 8 subsidiaries, including D.I Japan Corporation.

003200.text: Ilshin Spinning makes textile materials such as cotton, blended and synthetic yarns, and also runs real estate leasing and logistics warehouse businesses for stable income. It began in 1951, relaunched under its current name in 1961 and listed on the KOSPI in 1973. It has 10 affiliates, including a Vietnamese unit and a venture capital firm.

003220.text: Daewon Pharmaceutical is a mid-sized drugmaker that started in 1958 and incorporated in 1961. Alongside prescription drugs, contract manufacturing (CMO), exports and over-the-counter medicines, the group also covers cosmetics, health functional foods and medical devices. Having launched Korea's 12th domestically developed new drug, it is expanding its pipeline of novel and improved drugs.

003230.text: Samyang Foods is a food manufacturer founded in 1961 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975. It launched Korea's first ramen and makes noodles, snacks, sauces and frozen foods at three domestic plants. It has 15 subsidiaries and sales units in the Americas, Japan, China, Southeast Asia and Europe, and it is building a production facility in China.

003240.text: Taekwang Industrial is a petrochemical and textile company founded in 1961 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975. Its petrochemical division produces PTA, AN and propylene, its textile division makes nylon and modacrylic, and it also has a leasing business and a broadcasting and telecom business through subsidiaries. Its business group has 39 affiliates including the company.

003280.text: Heung-a Shipping mainly carries liquid petrochemical products by sea within Asia and also leases real estate. Founded in 1961, it listed on the KOSPI in 1976 and has 5 consolidated subsidiaries. Its affiliates include a ship management company, a Korea-China car ferry operator, a logistics firm, a Korea-Russia freight brokerage and a Singapore unit.

003300.text: Hanil Holdings was founded in 1961 to make and sell cement and split into a holding company and a cement company in 2018. Through its subsidiaries it makes and sells cement, dry mortar and ready-mixed concrete, and it also runs a theme park, trading and construction businesses.

003310.text: Daejoo was founded in 1962 to make and sell compound animal feed and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1992. It produces feed by animal type, making livestock feed for chickens, cattle and pigs at one plant and pet food at another. Its subsidiary makes veterinary medicines.

003350.text: Hankook Cosmetics Manufacturing is an OEM and ODM cosmetics maker that produces about 1,600 types of skincare and color cosmetics. Founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1978, it holds CGMP and ISO 22716 certification. It has 96 domestic and 9 overseas patents and functional cosmetics certification for about 622 items.

003380.text: Harim Holdings is a pure holding company that aims to be a global food and agribusiness group, earning dividends, trademark fees and rental income from its subsidiaries. Founded in 1950 under a different name, it became a holding company through a spin-off in 2011 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. In May 2026 its group was designated a business group subject to cross-shareholding restrictions.

003460.text: Yuhwa Securities is a financial investment company founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1987. Licensed for dealing, brokerage and discretionary investment management, it trades securities for its own account and for clients, underwrites securities, extends credit and trades repurchase agreements.

003470.text: Yuanta Securities Korea is a securities firm founded in 1962 that took its current name in 2014 and belongs to Taiwan's Yuanta financial group, which gives it a network in China, Taiwan and Hong Kong. It seeks diverse revenue from retail, wholesale, strategic investment and corporate finance businesses and also invests in ventures. It is developing trading and wealth management services using AI and big data.

003480.text: Hanjin Heavy IND. & Const. Holdings is a pure holding company whose income comes from subsidiary dividends, trademark fees and property leasing. Its roots go back to a shipbuilder established in 1937; it was set up as a shipbuilding corporation in 1962 and became a holding company after spinning off its operating businesses in 2007. It has three main subsidiaries.

003490.text: Korean Air Lines carries passengers and cargo with a fleet of 165 aircraft, serving 10 domestic destinations and 106 cities in 38 countries, and also runs an aerospace business. Established in 1962 as a public corporation and privatized in 1969, it had 28 consolidated subsidiaries at the end of June 2026, including airlines, ground handling and IT service affiliates.

003520.text: Yungjin Pharm was founded in 1962 to make and sell medicines and listed on the KOSPI in 1973. A core affiliate of the KT&G group, it leads the group's bio and pharmaceutical business. It sells prescription products such as an enteral nutrition product and a pulmonary fibrosis treatment, and exports cephalosporin antibiotic ingredients and injectables.

003530.text: Hanwha Investment & Securities is a financial investment company organized into WM, Trading, Wholesale and IB divisions. Founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1986, it is part of its group's financial network offering one-stop services. It expanded in Southeast Asia by buying stakes in an Indonesian brokerage in 2024 and an Indonesian asset manager in 2025.

003540.text: Daishin Securities is a financial investment company founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975. It runs retail, corporate finance, CM and institutional sales businesses, and wholly owns affiliates in asset management, savings banking and economic research, among others. It has overseas units in Singapore, the United States and Japan.

003550.text: LG is a pure holding company founded in 1947 that became Korea's first holding company in 2003 through the merger of LGCI and LGEI. Its income comes mainly from subsidiary dividends, LG brand royalties and rent. Its main subsidiaries are in telecom and broadcasting equipment, petrochemicals, rechargeable batteries and wired and wireless telecom, and it pursues research in AI, robotics and cloud technology.

003570.text: SNT Dynamics has a transport equipment business, making defense transmissions, guns and vehicle parts, and a machinery business making machine tools, with customers including Korea's defense procurement agency, defense companies and a truck maker. Founded in 1959, it listed on the KOSPI in 1976 and took its current name in 2023. It is supplying weapon programs such as a 120mm self-propelled mortar and developing electrified products and next-generation weapon systems.

003580.text: HLB Global, founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1990, operates media commerce, food, beverage and cosmetics businesses through subsidiaries. The parent runs a direct-to-consumer business built on media content, while its subsidiaries make jams and syrups, kombucha drinks and cosmetics. It sells mainly through its own online stores and uses customer data for performance marketing.

003610.text: Pangrim is a mid-sized cotton textile maker founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1989. It produces dyed and printed fabrics at its domestic plant and, with a wholly owned Vietnamese subsidiary, runs an integrated process from spinning and weaving to finishing. In 2026 it sold all its shares in a subsidiary to reduce financial risk.

003620.text: KG Mobility makes and sells vehicles and parts, producing passenger models, electric models and electric buses at one plant and gasoline and diesel engines at another. Founded in 1962 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975, it adopted its current name in 2023 and has 4 unlisted subsidiaries.

003650.text: Michang Oil IND is a mid-sized maker of industrial lubricants, founded in 1962 and listed on the Korea Exchange in 1989. It produces automotive, marine and industrial lubricants as well as electrical insulating oil, rubber process oil and liquid paraffin, with technical cooperation from ENEOS CORPORATION. It ranks in the upper-middle tier of Korean lubricant makers by capacity and sales and is strong in factory-fill automotive lubricants.

003670.text: POSCO Future M was founded in 1971 to make refractories and maintain industrial furnaces. It acquired an anode materials business in 2010 and merged with a group company in 2019, becoming the only company in Korea producing both anode and cathode materials. As part of the POSCO Group, it has built a full value chain for battery materials and is expanding its global production sites.

003680.text: Hansung Enterprise was founded in 1963 for fishing and seafood processing and listed on the KOSPI in 1989. It began North Pacific fishing in 1969, started producing and exporting pollock fillets in 1972 and entered the US market with imitation crab in 1982. Overseas it sells its catch, imports, handles intermediary trade and exports processed seafood, and its food division makes a range of foods.

003690.text: Korean Reinsurance, founded in 1963, is Korea's only dedicated reinsurer, covering both non-life and life reinsurance. Its lines include fire, marine, liability, engineering, motor, overseas general and long-term non-life insurance, and it also handles overseas business and asset management. Its ratings include an upgraded A+ from S&P and a new A1 from Moody's.

003720.text: Samyoung is a mid-sized company founded in 1959 that makes capacitor films used in AI data centers and eco-friendly vehicles. It is the only producer of these films in Korea and the world's third-largest, and it also runs a shipbuilding equipment business. It is developing ultra-thin, high-heat-resistant films, and its affiliates include SAMYOUNG CHEMICAL VIETNAM.

003780.text: Chin Yang Industry makes foamed plastic products and was founded in 1963 and listed on the KOSPI in 1973. Its main product, polyurethane foam, is supplied as an intermediate material for car interiors, shoes, bedding and electronics, with a domestic market share of about 20%. It focuses on high-value specialty products, sources its main raw materials domestically and has 3 subsidiaries, including a Vietnamese unit.

0037T0.text: KB No.32 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

003800.text: AceBed makes and sells beds and furniture and also buys, sells and leases real estate. It started in 1963, incorporated in 1977 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1996. It set up the industry's first bed engineering research institute and runs a mobile sleep engineering lab, using ongoing research and development to manage quality.

003830.text: Daehan Synthetic Fibrer makes polyester yarn and PAR and leases land and buildings at three of its plant sites. Founded in 1963, it listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in 1985 and belongs to a group of 39 affiliates. Polyester is cheap to produce and blends well, and it is used in industrial materials such as car interiors and hygiene products as well as in medical applications.

003850.text: Boryung makes and sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs, focusing on chronic metabolic diseases and oncology. Founded in 1963, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988. In 2025 it acquired the rights to a drug business from Sanofi and bought Distribution Solutions Kft., which it renamed Boryung Europe Kft. and made a subsidiary.

003920.text: Namyang Dairy Products is a dairy processor founded in 1964 and listed on the KOSPI in 1978, with 3 subsidiaries. It makes milk powder, milk, fermented milk and cheese as well as cafe mixes and beverages. It is investing in research and facilities for functional premium dairy products and is developing export markets for milk powder in China and Southeast Asia.

003960.text: Sajodaerim makes surimi products and edible oil and sells canned tuna, ham, sausages, laver and fermented sauces, with operations divided into food, livestock, seafood and food service. Founded in 1964 and listed in 1976, it joined its current group in 2006 and merged with a group food company in 2019. In 2024 two group companies were added, expanding it into starch sugar and food service and ingredient distribution.

0039P0.text: Madup is an AI marketing company founded in 2015 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026. Its marketing division provides advertising agency services using its AI solution LEVER Xpert, its solutions division sells AI marketing software, and its brand build-up unit develops the '1950' and 'Latib' brands. It also owns MADUP Global, Inc.

004000.text: Lotte Fine Chemical is a specialty chemicals maker founded in 1964 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. Its chemicals division produces ECH, caustic soda and ammonia and has the largest ammonia storage facilities in Korea. Its green materials division makes high-value cellulose-based products, including construction additives, paint additives and pharmaceutical coatings.

004020.text: Hyundai Steel produces flat steel as well as bars and sections, supplying the construction, automotive and shipbuilding industries. Founded in 1953 and listed on the KOSPI in 1987, it became Korea's second blast-furnace steelmaker when its integrated steelworks started operating in 2010. Its subsidiaries include steel product makers and steel service centers in 9 countries.

004060.text: SG makes and sells apparel and luxury leather goods, was founded in 1964 and listed in 1976, and has 9 consolidated subsidiaries. Its export arm supplies large US buyers such as the GAP group and MACY'S on an OEM basis, producing woven garments at its main factory in Vietnam (SSV) and partner factories. Its fashion arm owns 5 brands in menswear, womenswear and luxury leather goods, sold through department stores, outlets and agencies.

004080.text: Shinhung makes and distributes dental equipment and materials, including unit chairs, dental alloys, air compressors and crowns, and also sells consumer goods and leases property. Founded in 1964, it listed on the KOSPI in 1991. It has 5 subsidiaries, including an implant maker, a lender to dental professionals and an equipment repair company.

004090.text: Korea Petroleum Industries was founded in 1964 to process and sell asphalt and listed on the KOSPI in 1977. It has 8 subsidiaries and operates 4 segments: asphalt, synthetic resins, chemicals and other. It produces asphalt and waterproofing sheets at two plants, and its resin segment handles PE and PP as well as BLOW and PAIL products.

004100.text: Taeyang Metal Industrial makes cold-forged products for automotive, machinery, electrical and electronic parts, supplying major Korean automakers, auto parts makers and LG E&S. It began in 1954, incorporated under its current name in 1964 and listed in 1976. It has 7 affiliates, including units in China and Taeyang Metal India.

004140.text: Dongbang Transport & Logistics is an integrated logistics company founded in 1957 and listed in 1988. Built on port stevedoring and land and sea transport, it offers a range of logistics services through a network of major ports and logistics bases nationwide. It recently added 3 subsidiaries, including a port logistics center, and is expanding its fleet to strengthen its shipping business.

004150.text: Hansol Holdings is a pure holding company earning income from Hansol brand fees, management consulting and dividends. Founded in 1965 and listed in 1972, it spun off its paper business into a new company in 2015 and became a holding company. After buying more shares in a group electronics company, it had 31 consolidated subsidiaries, whose main businesses are paper, IT services and electronic components.

004170.text: Shinsegae is a retailer that runs 13 department stores. Founded in 1955 as a department store under a different name, it listed on the KOSPI in 1985. Through subsidiaries it also operates wholesale and retail, real estate and bus terminals, hotels and duty-free shops, and in 2024 it took over a bus terminal business and acquired another company.

0041B0.text: Kyobo 18 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

0041J0.text: LS Special Purpose Acquisition No1 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

0041L0.text: Hana 35 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

004250.text: National Plastic makes injection-molded plastic products, including industrial containers, beverage and liquor crates and boxes for farm and fishery products, and is the largest such maker in Korea. Founded in 1965 and listed in 1969, it has 24 unlisted subsidiaries. With online shopping and logistics growing, it focuses on eco-friendly insulated boxes and reusable boxes.

004270.text: Namsung exports digital electronics and automotive electronics, including mobile audio and video devices, GPS receivers and smart keys. Founded in 1965 and listed on the KOSPI in 1989, it sells under its own brands such as 'Dual' to the United States and Canada, and its main customers include Wal-Mart. It has a domestic subsidiary and the overseas unit Namsung America, Inc.
