004310.text: Hyundai Pharmaceutical makes and sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs, foods, cosmetics and medical devices for hospitals, clinics, pharmacies and wholesalers. Founded in 1965, it began with medicines and health drinks and listed on the KOSPI in 1978. Its prescription drugs include dementia treatments and a dyslipidemia treatment, and it is focusing on a few over-the-counter brands.

004360.text: Sebang was founded in 1965 for port stevedoring and trucking and listed on the KOSPI in 1977. It provides integrated logistics, including port handling of import and export cargo, room-temperature and cold-chain warehousing, land and sea transport, heavy cargo transport and installation, third-party logistics and e-commerce fulfillment. It has 42 affiliates.

004370.text: Nongshim makes and sells instant noodles, snacks and beverages, exports to about 100 countries and runs local plants in China and the United States. Founded in 1965, it listed in 1976 and took its current name in 1978. Its group has 44 affiliates, including two other listed companies, and in 2026 it set up NONGSHIM RUS LLC in Russia.

004380.text: Samick THK was founded in 1965 to make hand files, later added machinery such as LM systems, and listed on the KOSPI in 1989. Through a joint venture with Japan's THK, it localized production of LM system products for the automation parts market. It is expanding overseas sales channels, building an AI-based AX platform and developing smart factory solutions using autonomous robots.

004410.text: Seoul Food IND runs bakery and environmental businesses. Its bakery products include frozen dough, snacks, packaged bread and breadcrumbs, and its environmental unit makes food waste dryers and manages facilities for local governments. Founded in 1955 and listed on the KOSPI in 1973, it is automating frozen dough and pizza production and seeking exports to markets such as Japan and Taiwan.

004430.text: Songwon Industrial makes polymer stabilizers, fuel and lubricant additives and PVC stabilizers for industries such as packaging, automotive, construction and agriculture. Founded in 1965 and listed on the KOSPI in 1977, it operates 15 entities and 2 branches. It is the world's second-largest polymer stabilizer maker with about 22% of the market, and it relies on vertical integration for cost competitiveness.

004440.text: Samil C&S was founded in 1965 and makes high-strength concrete piles, precast concrete and steel structures at three plants. Its concrete division produces PHC piles and off-site construction products, its wind division makes offshore wind transition pieces and steel bridge structures, and its aggregates division supplies sand and gravel. It is developing PHC piles using Nano-CSH and large, ultra-high-strength piles.

004450.text: Samhwa Crown & Closure was founded in 1965 to make bottle caps and listed in 1976. Its cap division makes metal and non-metal caps for domestic beverage companies and exports to about 10 countries, while its plastic container division develops cosmetics containers with an integrated production system. It runs a research institute and has technology ties with overseas firms.

004490.text: Sebang Global Battery makes lead-acid batteries for vehicles, industrial uses and two-wheelers, as well as lithium battery modules and auxiliary battery packs, supplying vehicle makers and ESS companies. It was founded in 1952 and listed on the KOSPI in 1987. Its subsidiaries include makers of lead-acid battery materials and a lithium module and pack maker, and it has set up a US unit for the North American market.

0044K0.text: Samsung Special Purpose Acquisition 10 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

004540.text: KleanNara makes white board packaging and household products such as toilet paper, facial tissue, diapers, sanitary pads and wet wipes. Founded in 1966 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975, it has three subsidiaries. It is investing in eco-friendly facilities toward carbon neutrality by 2050, adding new product categories and entering pet healthcare.

004560.text: Hyundai BNG Steel, founded in 1966, was Korea's first maker of cold-rolled stainless steel sheets and listed on the KOSPI in 1987. Stainless sheets make up about 99% of its sales and are used in home appliances, transport equipment, construction and electrical equipment. It also has an auto parts business.

004590.text: Korea Furniture was founded in 1966 to make and sell furniture and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1993. It began with high-end classic furniture and now imports and sells foreign furniture brands such as Roche Bobois, Kartell, MDF and Flou. It wholly owns a food wholesaler and owns 50% of a furniture distributor.

004650.text: Changhae Ethanol mainly produces ethanol for spirits and took its current name in 2004. Founded in 1966, it has 4 subsidiaries, including PT ORGANIC FEED INDONESIA and a unit in Vietnam. Its energy business supplies steam from incineration waste heat, its engineering business designs and builds ethanol plants, and its trading business buys and sells tapioca chips.

004690.text: Samchully mainly supplies city gas, buying gas wholesale and delivering it to consumers in its licensed areas. It began in 1955 as a briquette business, incorporated in 1966 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It runs various businesses through 27 subsidiaries, and in February 2026 it bought 100% of a seasoned laver maker.

004700.text: Chokwang Leather makes and sells leather for car seats and steering wheels as well as leather for furniture. Founded in 1936, it listed on the KOSPI in 1977. It imports most of its raw materials, so its profitability depends on global raw material prices, and it produces and inspects goods to customer orders.

004710.text: Hansol Technics makes electronic components, electrical parts for cars, ships and robots, smartphones on an EMS basis and solar modules, and also processes and coats semiconductor equipment parts and recycles silicon by-products. Founded in 1966, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988 and belongs to a group with 56 affiliates at home and abroad. In 2025 it bought stakes in two companies to enter chip by-products and expand its automotive electronics business.

004720.text: PharmGen Science is a healthcare company founded in 1966 whose drug business centers on digestive treatments, alongside health functional foods. It sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs through 6 wholesale branches and 9 branches nationwide and runs a global R&D center. In 2021 it set up a new drug division and is building a pipeline that includes a treatment for inflammatory bowel disease.

004770.text: Sunny Electronics makes quartz crystal resonators and related products as its single business. Founded in 1966 under a former name, it listed on the KOSPI in 1987. Quartz resonators use the piezoelectric effect to generate frequencies or filter signals and are core parts in electronics such as TVs, computers, mobile phones, cars and aircraft.

004780.text: DaeryukCan makes general cans, such as lubricant and paint cans, and portable butane gas canisters, and holds more than 60% of Korea's general can market. Founded in 1966, it diversified in 1995 through a merger and an acquisition. It developed C.R.V., Korea's first explosion-prevention technology for butane canisters, and newer technology such as TRIPLE SEAMED C.R.V. as it pursues overseas markets.

004800.text: Hyosung is the holding company of its group, managing and investing in stakes in subsidiaries. Founded in 1966 and listed in 1973, it became a holding company in 2019. In 2025 it took over a tank terminal business from a group chemical company, part of an effort to rely less on affiliate dividends and generate steadier cash flow.

004830.text: Dcksung was founded in 1966 to make synthetic leather and listed on the Korea Exchange in 1987. It runs synthetic leather, synthetic resin and materials businesses, with plants in Korea and subsidiaries in China, Vietnam and Indonesia. Its synthetic leather goes into sporting goods, furniture, car interiors, IT accessories and cosmetic puffs, and it makes its own resin to cut costs.

004840.text: DRB Holding is a pure holding company with 18 consolidated companies making rubber components such as vehicle sealing, construction materials and seismic isolation systems, industrial rubber products such as power transmission belts, conveyor belts and rubber tracks, automation solutions and medical devices. It started in 1945, went public in 1976 and became a holding company through a spin-off in 2022.

004870.text: Tway Holdings mainly makes and distributes PHC piles, concrete piles that transfer structural loads to the ground and are used in housing and large construction projects. Founded in 1966 and listed on the KOSPI in 1977, it reached its current structure after several changes of control and name. In 2013 it acquired an affiliated airline, which has since been renamed.

004890.text: Dongil Industries runs steel bar, ferroalloy and casting businesses, producing steel bars for auto parts, ferroalloys for steelmaking and parts for construction machinery. Founded in 1966 to make cast steel, special steel and ferroalloys, it absorbed a steel company in 1997 and listed on the KOSPI in 2005. Its subsidiary makes constant-velocity joint parts for vehicles.

004910.text: Chokwang Paint makes wood, architectural, industrial and powder coatings and is investing in electrical and electronic materials and adhesives. Founded in 1967 and listed on the KOSPI, it has a Vietnamese unit and a subsidiary in heat-dissipation materials. It is building its electronic materials capabilities through a subsidiary and pursuing global growth based on plants in the United States and Hungary.

004920.text: Citech develops, makes and sells information and communication devices, including premium network audio under its own brand, unmanned certificate-issuing machines and kiosks, and smart hospital solutions. Founded in 1967, it took its current name in 2015. It has 3 domestic affiliates including itself, and in 2026 it sold all its shares in one company and merged with a subsidiary.

004960.text: Hanshin Construction is a general construction company founded in 1950 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It works in building, civil engineering, plant and new businesses, targeting public contracts and expanding private, redevelopment and reconstruction housing under its apartment brand. It is also pursuing emerging markets such as Vietnam and Cambodia, running a parking business and seeking overseas infrastructure contracts.

004970.text: Silla is a distant-water fishing and seafood distribution company founded in 1967 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It operates 6 tuna purse seiners and 9 tuna longliners in the western and central Pacific, catching tuna for canning and sashimi, and sells tuna and canned tuna from overseas joint ventures. A subsidiary is a designated fruit and vegetable wholesaler at Korea's largest wholesale produce market.

004980.text: Sungshin Cement makes cement and supplies it nationwide under its own brand, with ready-mixed concrete and trading run through subsidiaries. Founded in 1967 and listed in 1976, it has 10 subsidiaries. Its trading arm, centered on JinSung International, imports and exports building materials and energy and mineral resources, helping to cut costs.

004990.text: Lotte is a holding company founded in 1967 that adopted its holding structure in 2017 by splitting off its confectionery business and merging in the investment businesses of three group companies. It owns 19 domestic subsidiaries, and its main income comes from dividends, trademark fees and rent. At the group level it is building an ESG management system and a roadmap for carbon neutrality by 2040.

005010.text: Husteel makes steel pipes, including piping, OCTG, structural pipes and electrical conduit, at four production sites. It was founded in 1967 and listed in 1973. In 2025 it completed a new plant for large-diameter pipes, and it is seeking new markets in green energy such as offshore wind and diversifying its exports.

005030.text: Pusan Cast Iron is a mid-sized maker of cast auto parts, founded in 1967 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975. Its plant has three casting lines with enough capacity for export and domestic orders. It is expanding a machining plant and adding equipment in an industrial complex to strengthen production of high-value products.

005070.text: Cosmo Advanced Materials & Technology makes cathode active materials for rechargeable batteries (67.14% of sales), release films for MLCCs (30.43%) and toner (2.43%), and exports account for 76.40% of sales. Founded in 1967 and listed in 1987, it entered the battery market in 2007 with LCO for small IT devices and is seeking a larger share with its single-crystal cathode technology.

005090.text: SGC Energy operates a combined heat and power plant and, in construction, carries out plant EPC, civil engineering and building projects across various industries. It was founded in 1967 as a glass maker, and in 2020 it absorbed an energy company, spun off its glass business and took its current name. It has several subsidiaries, including a logistics company.

005110.text: Hanchang is a small company whose main businesses are distribution and real estate development. Founded in 1967, it listed on the Korea Exchange in 1976. In 2014 it set up a subsidiary that developed a mixed-use residential project, and it now runs real estate development and, through another subsidiary, property management, investment and asset management.

005160.text: Dongkuk Industries makes cold-rolled steel sheets for auto and electronics parts and color-printed steel sheets for building interiors and exteriors and home appliances. Founded in 1967 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1999, it spun off its steel structure and refractories and ferrite businesses to focus on steel. Its renewable energy division sells WIND-TOWER products for wind turbines and makes offshore wind substructures.

005180.text: Binggrae is a dairy products company founded in 1967 under a different name and listed on the KOSPI in 1978. It operates a single dairy segment divided into chilled products and frozen and other products, and its brands include a banana-flavored milk. It has local units in China, the United States, Vietnam and Australia for importing, exporting and distributing food.

005250.text: GC is a healthcare holding company founded in 1967 that adopted its holding structure in 2001 and has 53 affiliates, including its main drugmaking subsidiary. The group makes and sells pharmaceuticals, mainly blood products and vaccines, and provides diagnostics, analysis and medical services. The company sets group strategy, manages its investments and invests selectively in digital healthcare.

005290.text: Dongjin Semichem makes electronic materials for semiconductors and displays, including photoresists, anti-reflective coatings, SOC and polishing materials, and exports blowing agents under the UNICELL brand. Incorporated in 1973, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1999 and has units in China, Taiwan, Sweden and the United States. In 2026 it spun off its blowing agent business into a new company.

005300.text: Lotte Chilsung Beverage makes and sells soft drinks, coffee and other beverages as well as soju, beer and other alcoholic drinks. Founded in 1950, it earns the most from carbonated drinks in beverages and from soju in liquor. Its main subsidiary, PCPPI, makes carbonated and energy drinks in the Philippines.

005320.text: Ontide is a knitwear exporter founded in 1967 and listed on the KOSPI in 1996, whose largest shareholder holds 42.94%. It makes clothing on an OEM basis for global brands such as FANATICS and H&M and runs a production unit in Indonesia. In 1999 it set up units in the United States and Mexico to enter the North American market.

005360.text: Monami is a stationery company founded in 1967 that sells writing instruments, including the BP153 and P-3000 pens and markers, as well as art supplies. Its computer supplies division provides printer ink cartridges and toner for a major electronics maker, and it also runs B2B, B2C and cosmetics OEM and ODM businesses. Its subsidiaries include Monami(Thailand) and ZENITH-MONAMI.

005380.text: Hyundai Motor is a global automaker founded in 1967 with 166 consolidated subsidiaries, including financial affiliates. Its vehicle segment makes, sells and services cars, its finance segment provides installment financing and payment processing, and its other segment covers rail vehicles and defense. It is adding production capacity, including HMGMA in the United States, a plant in India and an EV plant in Korea, toward sales targets for 2030.

005420.text: Cosmo Chemical produces cobalt sulfate and nickel sulfate, key raw materials for battery cathodes, through refining and recycling, and is the only titanium dioxide maker in Korea. Founded in 1968 and listed on the KOSPI in 1987, it has 4 segments: battery materials, titanium dioxide, new materials and catalysts. Its new materials business makes cathode active materials and MLCC release films, and it has two consolidated affiliates.

005430.text: Korea Airport Service provides aviation support services and was founded in 1968, listed on the KOSPI in 1976 and expanded through a merger in 1999. Ground handling, fueling and cargo handling for Korean and foreign airlines at major airports make up about 90% of its sales. A subsidiary handles passenger check-in, immigration support and flight operations at 14 domestic airports.

005440.text: Hyundai G.F. Holdings is a holding company of a department store group, founded in 1968 and listed on the KOSPI in 1989. Through a share swap it made a home shopping company a wholly owned subsidiary. Its businesses include food service, distribution, food ingredients, furniture, heavy equipment, home shopping, building materials, telecom and bio, apparel, employee welfare and mobile meal vouchers, and travel and leasing.

005490.text: POSCO Holdings is a holding company founded in 1968 that adopted its holding structure in 2022 and has 199 consolidated subsidiaries. Its main subsidiaries are in steel, infrastructure and battery materials, supplying steel products and running trading, energy, construction, logistics, IT and battery materials businesses. It sets group growth strategy, pursues new businesses including M&A and concentrates on decarbonization.

0054V0.text: NH Special Purpose Acquisition 32 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

005500.text: Samjin Pharmaceutical makes over-the-counter drugs, prescription drugs and active pharmaceutical ingredients, with products including an anti-inflammatory painkiller, an appetite stimulant, an antithrombotic and a brain function drug. Founded in 1968, it listed in 1988. It is focusing on new drugs for cancer, dementia and diabetes and expanding into health functional foods and medical devices.

005610.text: Samlip is a food company with bakery, food, distribution and logistics businesses, founded in 1968 and listed in 1975. It spun off SPC GFS in 2014 and absorbed three companies in 2018 to complete its vertical integration. It makes packaged bread, integrates premium ingredients and serves as its group's central kitchen while expanding at home and abroad.

005670.text: Foodwell is a mid-sized food and beverage maker founded in 1968 for agricultural storage and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1993. It makes syrups and beverages on an OEM basis for large companies and buys domestic chestnuts to make chestnut products exported to Japan and other markets. It has 5 unlisted affiliates, including a unit in China.

005680.text: Samyoung Electronics is a capacitor maker founded in 1968 and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It makes capacitors and capacitor materials used in home appliances, automotive electronics and AI data industries. It acquired a 68.04% stake in a capacitor company, made it a subsidiary and absorbed another subsidiary, and it has a unit in China.

005690.text: Pharmicell is a biotech company founded in 1968 under a different name and listed on the KOSPI in 1988. It developed Hearticellgram-AMI, the world's first stem cell therapy, and operates 2 divisions. The biomedical division makes and researches adult stem cell therapies and sells cosmetics made with stem cell culture media, while the biochemical division makes electronic materials, pharmaceutical intermediates and eco-friendly phosphorus flame retardants.

005710.text: Daewon Sanup makes car seats as its single business, supplying a domestic automaker for several of its models. It was founded in 1968 to make seats and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1993. It has subsidiaries in China, Russia and Vietnam that make car seats locally.

005720.text: Nexen is the parent of its group, a business holding company that makes rubber products such as tire tubes and runs logistics. Founded in 1968, it made a tire company a subsidiary in 2018 and has set up a new unit in Mexico to expand global production. Its segments are rubber, including tire manufacturing, sales and rental, logistics, leasing, machinery and a golf course.

005740.text: Crownhaitai Holdings is a pure holding company set up in 2017 when a confectionery company split off its food business, and it has 9 subsidiaries. Its income comes from CROWN brand fees, outsourced service fees and dividends. Its subsidiaries make and sell confectionery, frozen foods and ice cream.

005750.text: Daelim Bath is a bathroom building materials company that traces its origins to a government-affiliated ceramics center set up in 1966 and listed on the KOSPI in 1992. It sells sanitary ware, faucets, bidets, filters, kitchen remodeling, home interiors and appliance rentals through builders, agencies and online and offline channels. Its subsidiaries run a designer living brand and a healthcare and beauty business.

005800.text: Shinyoung Wacoal is a women's underwear maker that was founded in 1954, pioneered Korea's lingerie market and listed on the KOSPI in 1976. It sews and sells garments under several brands and also leases real estate. It has 8 affiliates, and its products are made at a subsidiary in China.

005810.text: Poongsan Holdings was founded in 1968, listed on the KOSPI in 1988 and became a holding company in 2008. Its holding operations provide IT maintenance, brand management and management consulting, while its manufacturing operations make tools, machine parts and packaging and process non-ferrous metals. Its main subsidiary has 12 subsidiaries with production and sales lines in the United States, Thailand and China.

005820.text: Wonlim makes and wholesales packaging materials and has 4 subsidiaries. Its sales come from industrial packaging (50.3%), a medical business (43.1%), financial investment (5.1%) and leasing (1.5%). Founded in 1968 and listed in 1990, it invests selectively in bio and medical, electrical and mechanical, and ICT manufacturing companies, while its leasing business focuses on stable income.

005830.text: DB Insurance is a non-life insurer selling general, long-term and auto insurance and managing investment assets. It began in 1962 as a monopoly auto insurer, relaunched under a new name in 1968, came under its current group's control in 1983 and took its current name in 2017. Its main subsidiaries include a life insurer, a capital company and The Fortegra Group.

005850.text: SL is a global auto parts maker founded in 1954 with 21 affiliates in Korea, China, North America, India and elsewhere. It makes vehicle lamps, electrification parts, mirrors and electronics for global carmakers, including Korean automakers, GM and Ford. It is expanding into electrification products such as BMS and SBCM and into robotics, while working to cut greenhouse gas emissions.

005860.text: Hanil Feed is a mid-sized company founded in 1968 to produce compound animal feed and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994. Its feed business makes poultry and cattle feed, and its meat distribution business sells beef and pork imported from the United States, Europe and elsewhere through a nationwide network. Its main subsidiary is an imported meat distributor with 7 subsidiaries of its own.

005870.text: Huneed Technologies makes tactical communications equipment and systems for defense and exports and trades avionics through partnerships with companies such as Boeing and GA-ASI. Founded in 1968 under a different name, it was designated a defense contractor in 1973 and listed on the KOSPI in 1991. Using its multi-channel radio technology, it completed development of HCTRS, a core part of TICN, and is developing P5G and MANET/FANET.

005880.text: Korea Line is a shipping company that carries iron ore, natural gas and crude oil on bulk carriers, LNG carriers and tankers, with shipping making up 93% of sales. Founded in 1968 and listed on the KOSPI in 1992, it has 6 subsidiaries. It secures steady income through long-term contracts with cargo owners and is diversifying into trading, mining and construction.

005930.text: Samsung Electronics is a global electronics company founded in 1969 with 309 subsidiaries. Its DX division makes TVs, refrigerators and smartphones, its DS division makes semiconductors such as DRAM and NAND Flash, SDC makes OLED panels, and Harman makes automotive electronics and audio products. It is adopting AI and focusing on energy-efficient technology and higher-value solutions.

005940.text: NH Investment & Securities began in 1969 and, after several changes of name, took its current form through a merger with another securities firm in 2014. Licensed for dealing, brokerage and trust business, it offers retail and institutional clients securities brokerage, financial product sales, corporate finance and principal investment. It has 80 consolidated subsidiaries, including futures and hedge fund firms and overseas units.

005950.text: Isu Chemical, founded in 1969, makes raw materials for synthetic detergents and other petrochemicals. Its petrochemical division is the only producer of LAB and NP in Korea, its construction division builds housing under its own brand as well as civil and plant projects, and its pharmaceutical division sells biosimilars. It is working to commercialize higher-value chemicals and grow its drug pipeline.

005960.text: Dongbu was founded in 1969 for civil engineering, building and machinery installation and listed in 1978. The parent runs a construction business, and its subsidiaries provide engineering services and real estate development. In 2026 it set up a Vietnamese unit to enter overseas infrastructure markets, and it is expanding its plant division.

005990.text: Maeil Holdings is a pure holding company that was founded in 1969 as a dairy processor and adopted its holding structure through a spin-off in 2017. It has 11 subsidiaries, including its main dairy company, and provides them with funding and operational support, management consulting, and intellectual property management and licensing. Each subsidiary is run independently under a performance evaluation system.

006040.text: Dongwon Industries is the holding company of its group, founded in 1969, listed on the KOSPI in 1989 and merged with a group company in 2022. It has 41 subsidiaries, including StarKist Co. Its fisheries business runs 37 distant-water vessels, including 19 purse seiners that form Korea's largest purse seine fleet, and it also makes branded processed foods and packaging materials and parts.

006050.text: Kuk Young G M is a glass processor founded in 1959 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994. It buys flat glass and processes it for construction, railways, vehicles and interiors, making special products such as high-insulation double glazing and bulletproof, heated and fire-rated glass. It focuses on building construction, is diversifying into transport and protective products, and researches BIPV, vacuum glass and electrochromic glass.

006060.text: HS Industries is a mid-sized company founded in 1969 under a different name and listed on the KOSPI in 1991, with 41 consolidated subsidiaries. Its ODM business makes shoes for a global sportswear brand at bases in Vietnam, Indonesia and China. Its chemical business makes shoe adhesives, automotive coatings and packaging films, and it also runs intermediary trade and logistics in Southeast Asia and new technology finance and private equity funds.

006090.text: Oyang makes crab sticks, ham, sausages, fish cakes and dumplings and also runs distant-water fishing. Founded in 1969, it joined its current group in 2007 and expanded food processing through a merger in 2015. One plant can produce about 14,000 tons of crab sticks a year, the largest capacity in Korea, and in 2025 it bought a vessel for trawling in Falklands waters.

006110.text: Sama Aluminium was founded in 1969 on the basis of producing aluminum foil domestically and listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in 1980; it now trades on the KOSPI. It operates rolling, processing and electronic parts sales divisions. Its rolling division makes aluminum foil for LIB cathode current collectors and pouches, and its processing division makes retort packaging and ALU-ALU packaging for pharmaceuticals.

006120.text: SK Discovery is a holding company founded in 1969 that took its current form in 2017 by splitting its investment and operating businesses. Its subsidiaries work in areas including chemicals, gas, plasma and bioscience. The company controls and guides its subsidiaries, provides funding and manages the brand to create synergies across the group.

006140.text: PJ Electronics is an electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company founded in 1969 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1993. It was the first in Korea to adopt the EMS concept in the mid-1990s and offers a full manufacturing system covering product planning and development. Its main businesses are medical devices, automotive electronics, robot controllers and SMD and SET processing.

006200.text: Kec Holdings was founded in 1969 to make semiconductor parts and became a pure holding company through a spin-off in 2006. Its subsidiaries include a semiconductor maker producing TR, IC, DIODE and automotive semiconductors and a service company running transport and warehousing, real estate leasing and plant businesses. It has units in Thailand, China, Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan.

006220.text: Jeju Bank is a regional bank founded in 1969 to support the local economy of Jeju and is a member of a Korean financial group. Besides deposits and loans, it offers cards, foreign exchange, bancassurance and trusts. Its 2026 priorities include an ERP banking model, a focus on SOHO clients, AX and DX initiatives, capital efficiency and stronger consumer protection governance.

006260.text: LS is a pure holding company that controls the businesses of its subsidiaries, whose operations form its core businesses. It was founded in 1962 as a cable maker and listed in 1977. As owner of the LS trademark, it works on brand value, and its main income comes from subsidiary dividends and brand fees.

006280.text: GC Biopharma is a drugmaker founded in 1969 that specializes in blood products and vaccines. It received FDA approval for an immunoglobulin product in 2023 and entered the US market in 2024. Through subsidiaries it also makes in vitro diagnostic reagents, blood glucose meters and cell therapies, and it has commercialized an ICV formulation of a Hunter syndrome treatment and won Chinese approval for a hemophilia treatment.

006340.text: Dawon Cable is a mid-sized maker of power cables and wires, founded in 1969 and listed in 1988, with several subsidiaries. In 2025 it acquired an aluminum wheel business by making a wheel maker its subsidiary. It aims to raise its share of insulated wire for buildings and to strengthen lightweighting technology for electric vehicle wiring and aluminum wheels.

006360.text: GS Engineering & Construction builds and operates buildings, apartments and refining and petrochemical plants through 4 divisions: building and housing, plant, infrastructure and new business development. Founded in 1969 under a different name, it listed on the KOSPI in 1981 and has 138 consolidated subsidiaries. It gained water and wastewater operations by acquiring Inima in 2012, and in 2025 it signed a share sale agreement with an Abu Dhabi state energy company pending regulatory approval.

006370.text: Daegu Department Store is a regional retailer founded in 1969 and listed in 1988. Its main business is department stores, and it also runs brand businesses and a supermarket chain with 105 franchise stores in its home region. A subsidiary leases real estate, and the company has sold assets to improve its financial stability.

006400.text: Samsung SDI makes lithium-ion rechargeable batteries in its energy solutions division, which provides 94% of sales, and semiconductor and display materials in its electronic materials division. Founded in 1970 and listed in 1979, it has 22 subsidiaries in countries including Hungary, the United States and Malaysia. It targets mass production of all-solid-state batteries in 2027, is developing sodium batteries and is expanding into robots and aerospace.

006490.text: FreeT runs an MVNO service using the wireless networks of Korea's 3 mobile carriers. Founded in 1970 and listed on the KOSPI in 1985, it also has smart grid, cosmetics and watch distribution businesses. In 2025 it signed an MVNO agreement with Telus to launch a service in Canada and introduced an AI-based customer center.

006570.text: Daelim Trading is a building materials company founded in 1970 and listed on the KOSPI in 1975, with 4 subsidiaries. It sells faucets, bidets, sensors and shower booths, and its other businesses include tableware in Indonesia, faucets in Canada and kitchen and household goods. It has been named a quality-competitive company 26 times, has won prizes at major international design awards and is developing eco-friendly energy-saving products.

006620.text: DongKoo Bio & Pharma was founded in 1983 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018, and it has 6 subsidiaries, one of which provides new technology finance. Drugs make up 98.4% of sales, including dermatology, urogenital and allergy treatments. Based on its MLE skin barrier technology and DDS, it ranks first in dermatology prescriptions, and it also runs cosmeceutical, medical device and medical food businesses.

006650.text: Korea Petro Chemical IND is a petrochemical company founded in 1970 and listed on the KOSPI in 1999. One of its plants uses naphtha to produce basic chemicals such as ethylene and propylene as well as EO/EG, and another makes polymers such as HDPE and PP. It has 4 affiliates, including producers of industrial gases and of utilities and refined salt.

006660.text: Samsung Climate Control makes radiators, oil coolers and HVAC systems for domestic automakers and makers of heavy equipment and farm machinery, and exports directly to the United States, Europe and Southeast Asia. Founded in 1970 to make engine radiators and auto parts, it listed on the KOSPI in 1987. It has 7 consolidated subsidiaries and operates 3 domestic sites and 5 auto parts sites in countries including Indonesia and Vietnam.

006730.text: Seobu T&D was founded in 1979 to run public truck terminals and listed on the KOSDAQ in 1995. It operates tourist hotels, a shopping mall and logistics facilities and makes and sells tableware, and it runs a 1,700-room hotel and a large shopping mall complex. Its consolidated subsidiaries include 5 real estate investment companies and 8 companies under a holding company it acquired in 2025.

006740.text: Blue Industrial Development is a paper maker founded in 1970 and listed on the KOSPI in 1996, with 6 subsidiaries. It produces paper for paper tubes (34%) and linerboard for corrugated boxes (66%), and it has vertically integrated through a packaging subsidiary. In 2025 it set up two recycling companies to secure raw materials, address ESG goals and earn new income from selling recyclables.

006800.text: Mirae Asset Securities is a financial investment company founded in 1970 and listed in 1975, with overseas units and offices in 11 regions. It provides dealing, brokerage and advisory services, with its business centered on Brokerage, WM, IB and Trading. It pursues globally diversified investment, is strengthening AI-based digital wealth management and is expanding corporate finance through new businesses such as IMA.

006840.text: AK Holdings is a pure holding company founded in 1970 that became a holding company in 2012 and has 5 subsidiaries, including a chemical company. It controls and guides its subsidiaries, manages and licenses intellectual property and provides consulting, with businesses divided into chemicals, air transport, real estate and IT services. In 2026 it sold all its shares in an affiliate to restructure its business.

006880.text: Singsong Holdings is a pure holding company with 5 subsidiaries whose businesses span investment, food, trading, investment property and materials. Founded in 1970, it moved to a pure holding company structure through a spin-off in 2009 and took its current name after a merger in 2010.

006890.text: Taekyung Chemical makes liquid carbon dioxide and dry ice for beverage and industrial use. Its environmental division produces magnesium hydroxide and liquid slaked lime used for flue-gas desulfurization and wastewater treatment, and a subsidiary builds vaporizers and sells industrial gases. Founded in 1970, it listed on the KOSPI in 2003.

0068Y0.text: BNK 3 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

006910.text: Bosung Power Technology develops, makes and sells power equipment for the domestic electricity market, including transmission and distribution materials and steel structures for power plants and substations. Its main products include gas switches, pole-mounted transformers and transmission towers, made at two domestic plants. Founded in 1970, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994.

006920.text: Mohenz makes and sells ready-mixed concrete. It holds a 55.50% stake in a subsidiary that also produces ready-mixed concrete and runs a hardfacing welding business. Founded in 1970, the company listed on the KOSDAQ in 1989.

006980.text: Woosung makes and sells compound feed for livestock, fish farming and pets. It runs production and sales operations at three domestic sites and in Vietnam and China, with subsidiaries including a feed company and Vietnamese and Chinese units. Founded in 1970, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988 and became the surviving entity of a spin-off in 2021.

007070.text: GS Retail combines retail and real estate development, operating the GS25 convenience stores, GS THE FRESH supermarkets and the GS SHOP home shopping channel. It absorbed its home shopping affiliate in 2021 to integrate online and offline sales, and uses a logistics subsidiary and private-label products to support the business. Founded in 1971, it took its current name in 2005.

007110.text: Ilshin Stone is a small building-materials company whose stone business covers quarrying, stone processing, sales, trade and stonework construction. Because stone is hard to transport, the business is closely tied to trade and logistics. It listed on the KOSPI in 1986, and its largest shareholder is a foundation.

007120.text: MiraeING runs a financial solutions business and a B&E business. The financial solutions unit supplies banks with SWIFT message management, compliance and foreign-exchange trading software, along with systems integration, and sells mainly to large domestic banks. Founded in 1971, it listed on the KOSPI in 1999 and has since changed its name.

007160.text: Sajo Industries is a diversified food company that grew out of deep-sea fishing, including tuna longline and purse-seine fishing. It also makes canned seafood, fermented sauces and seaweed, produces pork and processed meat, operates a golf course, and leases cold storage and buildings. Founded in 1971, it went public in 1989 and consolidates 10 subsidiaries.

0071M0.text: Samsung Special Purpose Acquisition 11 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

007210.text: Byuksan makes building materials, producing insulation, interior and exterior finishing materials. Through subsidiaries it also runs kitchen appliance and ventilation businesses and, since acquiring a fastener maker in 2025, construction fasteners and tools. It pursues energy-saving materials and a US unit for overseas expansion. Founded in 1971, it listed on the Korea Exchange in 1972.

007280.text: Korea Steel produces billets from steel scrap in electric arc furnaces, then heats, rolls and cools them into bar and section steel. Its products serve as basic materials for the construction, shipbuilding, automotive and machinery industries, and it focuses on small-batch, high-variety production. Founded in 1971, it listed in 1989.

0072Z0.text: KB No.33 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

007310.text: Otoki is a diversified food company making and selling dried foods, sauces and seasonings, edible oils and noodles. It runs 28 sites at home and abroad, including production and sales facilities in the US and Vietnam, and has 31 affiliates. It set up new North American and Japanese units in 2026. Founded in 1969, it listed on the KOSPI in 1994.

007330.text: Pureun Savings Bank is a savings bank offering deposit products such as demand and time deposits, and lending through discounted bills and secured loans. It serves ordinary households and small businesses, and relies on credit screening and risk management. Founded in 1971 and renamed after changes in ownership, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1996.

007340.text: DN Automotive makes automotive batteries, parts and tubes, and through a subsidiary manufactures and services machine tools. Founded in 1971 to make vehicle tubes and tires, it spun off its rubber business in 2017, took its current name in 2022 after acquiring a machine-tool maker, and absorbed a tire affiliate in 2024.

007370.text: Jin Yang Pharmaceutical makes and sells pharmaceuticals. It is working to strengthen research, including new drug development, and to launch new products through patents and technology partnerships. Founded in 1971, it incorporated in 1978 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2000.

007390.text: Naturecell researches treatments for rare and intractable diseases using stem cells derived from a patient's own fat tissue, runs overseas clinical trials, and offers stem cell storage. It took full ownership of its US subsidiary in 2022 and bought a research site in Maryland in 2025. Founded in 1971, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1992.

007460.text: Aprogen operates in metal surface hardfacing, pharmaceuticals, insulation and biopharmaceuticals, having absorbed a biopharmaceutical developer in 2022. Through subsidiaries it also makes semiconductor equipment parts and designs and installs geothermal heating and cooling and fuel cell systems. Founded in 1971, it listed on the KOSPI in 1995.

007530.text: YM makes fasteners and related parts, including bolts, screws and rivets, for vehicles including electric cars, electronics and buildings, with about 10,000 specialised products sold at home and abroad. Founded in 1971 to make bolts, nuts, machinery and tools, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994 and has 1 unlisted subsidiary.

007540.text: Sempio is a pure holding company that earns equity-method income, brand fees, rent and dividends from its subsidiaries. These include a fermented-sauce maker, a canned-food producer, a promotions agency and a contract tea producer. Founded in 1946, it listed on the KOSPI in 1976, split off its food business in 2016 and became a pure holding company in 2017.

007570.text: Ilyang Pharmaceutical makes and sells prescription drugs, including an anti-ulcer drug, a leukemia treatment and seasonal flu vaccines, as well as over-the-counter products such as a ginseng tonic drink. It is expanding its pipeline with a P-CAB acid blocker in phase 1 trials and a urology combination drug preparing for phase 3. Founded in 1946, it listed on the KOSPI in 1974.

007590.text: Dongbang Agro makes and sells crop protection chemicals and fertilizers in formulations such as emulsions, wettable powders and granules. Its products target moths, aphids, mites and plant diseases, and its main buyers are the national agricultural cooperative federation and retail dealers. Founded in 1971, it listed on the KOSPI in 1977 and has one subsidiary.

007610.text: Seondo Electric makes heavy electrical equipment for industrial plant power systems, including gas-insulated switchgear (GIS), switchboards, vacuum circuit breakers and protective relays. Its main customers include a major chipmaker and the national power utility, and it has two subsidiaries. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989.

007660.text: Isupetasys makes high-layer-count multilayer (MLB) printed circuit boards, supplying data-center boards for AI accelerators, servers and network switches to large global companies. Exports make up more than 97% of sales. It is expanding capacity with a fifth plant and units in China and Thailand. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSPI in 2003.

007680.text: Daewon runs construction and textile businesses in Korea and Vietnam. Its construction arm builds and sells apartments under the Cantavil brand and handles industrial complexes, road and civil works, and commercial buildings. Founded in 1972 as a wool spinning and trading company, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 and has 9 unlisted subsidiaries.

007690.text: Kukdo Chemical makes epoxy resins, polyamide resins and polyurethanes. Its epoxy resins are used in coatings for ships, cars and containers, in electrical and electronic materials, and in wind turbine blades. It has plants at four domestic sites and 10 subsidiaries, including units in China and India. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989.

007700.text: F&F Holdings is a holding company that manages and invests in its subsidiaries, earning dividends, brand royalties and building rent. It split off its fashion business in 2021 and became a holding company after acquiring a 30.54% stake in that business. It has 21 affiliates, including 16 subsidiaries. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSPI in 1984.

007720.text: Sono Square supplies materials and operating solutions to the hospitality industry, such as hotels and resorts, through its MRO business. It also runs resort shops and digital advertising under the GOOD&GOODS brand and rents mattresses and other home products online and offline. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994 and has a Singapore subsidiary.

007770.text: Hanil Chemical IND makes zinc oxide, used as a raw material for tires, automotive rubber products and ferrites. It also makes specialty paints and turns waste plastic into recycled raw material. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1992 and has 3 unlisted subsidiaries.

007810.text: Korea Circuit makes printed circuit boards, supplying HDI boards for smartphones and memory module products. It runs an HDI business focused on communications devices and a package substrate business focused on semiconductors, and absorbed a subsidiary's PCB unit in 2026. Founded in 1972, it listed in 1985 and holds stakes in three affiliates.

007820.text: MX Robotics builds and installs automated logistics systems, control systems and operating information systems for a range of industries. It offers turnkey automation and is adding robotics and AI to its logistics solutions. Founded in 1972, it joined SK Group in 2017 and took its current name in 2026.

007860.text: Seoyon is a holding company with stakes in 12 companies in Korea and abroad, whose main subsidiaries make interior and exterior automotive parts. Through one subsidiary it also makes automotive molds and heavy equipment parts. Founded in 1972, it listed in 1989 and became a holding company through a spin-off in 2014.

007980.text: TP makes apparel, with overseas production units in Vietnam, Indonesia and Myanmar. It has 5 business segments: apparel manufacturing and sales, down processing, rice flour processing, bedding, and property leasing, and consolidates 26 subsidiaries. Founded in 1972, it listed on the KOSPI in 1994 and adopted its current name in 2024.

008040.text: Sajodongaone runs a flour milling business that imports and processes wheat, and a feed business making feed for livestock and farmed fish. Founded in 1972 as a compound feed maker, it gained two flour mills through a 2008 merger and absorbed two more companies in 2017 and 2018.

008060.text: Daeduck is a holding company with 2 domestic subsidiaries whose main businesses are printed circuit boards and SAW filters and RF modules. Founded in 1972 to make PCBs, it spun off that business and became a holding company in 2020. In 2026 a subsidiary set up a Canadian unit.

008250.text: Eagon Industrial makes and sells plywood and wood flooring and trades timber, and is one of the few producers that dominate Korean construction plywood. Through subsidiaries in Chile and the Solomon Islands and an energy unit, it also runs forestry and district energy businesses. Founded in 1972, it listed in 1988.

008260.text: Ni Steel makes composite steel beams and columns for buildings and leases steel products. Its composite beams and columns combine steel and concrete and can cut steel use by 20% or more. The leasing unit offers sheet piles, H-beams, struts, scaffolding and supports. It listed on the KOSPI in 1975.

0082N0.text: Kanaph Therapeutics develops new drugs based on human genome data, analysing disease-specific biological signatures to find new targets for cancer and eye disease treatments. It has 7 pipeline programs and seeks early licensing deals and joint development at the preclinical and early clinical stages. Founded in 2019, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026 as a technology growth company.

008350.text: Namsun Aluminium is an SM Group affiliate in aluminium, automotive parts and construction. Its aluminium business sells window systems under the WINDART and X-WIDE brands, its automotive unit supplies parts to a domestic carmaker, and it added general construction through a 2025 merger. Founded in 1947, it is also developing blast-resistant windows and plant EPC capabilities.

008370.text: Wonpoong makes industrial tarpaulins and flex fabrics for advertising, using hot-melt coating and its own SIGNFLEX products. It runs a 5,500mm-wide production line and supplies more than 60 countries. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1992; it has one affiliate, and an overseas unit was liquidated in 2025.

008420.text: Moonbae Steel makes and distributes steel and acts as a hot-rolled steel sales agent for a major domestic steelmaker, processing flat steel at three domestic sites. It also leases and invests in real estate. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1994 and is pursuing automation, quality development and a wider sales network.

008470.text: Booster makes industrial boilers, with once-through boilers as its main product alongside vacuum hot-water and non-pressurised boilers. It provides after-sales service through 35 offices and about 200 service staff, and its own research lab develops low-NOx burners and high-efficiency boilers. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

008490.text: Suheung makes hard capsules and produces soft-capsule drugs on contract as well as health supplements. It also makes gelatin and collagen and provides OEM/ODM manufacturing of skincare cosmetics. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1990 and has 13 affiliates, including units in the US, Vietnam, Japan and Europe.

008600.text: The Willbes runs textile and education businesses. Its textile arm makes clothing on an OEM basis for export to global buyers such as Gap and Hanesbrands, with production bases in Indonesia, Cambodia, the Dominican Republic and Haiti. Founded in 1973 as a clothing maker, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989 and has 14 unlisted subsidiaries.

008700.text: Anam Electronics makes audio equipment, including home audio and AV devices, soundbars and speakers, drawing on about 53 years in the AV field. Founded in 1973 to make televisions, it listed on the KOSPI in 1984. It has 6 affiliates, with main subsidiaries in Hong Kong and Vietnam.

008730.text: Youlchon Chemical makes film-based packaging and electronic materials. Its packaging unit produces OPP, CPP and shrink films and food packaging, while its electronic materials unit makes optical films for IT, automotive and semiconductor uses and LiBP pouch film for rechargeable batteries. It spends about 2% of sales on R&D. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988.

008770.text: Hotel Shilla is a Samsung Group affiliate in duty-free retail and hotels. Its travel retail unit runs downtown duty-free stores in Korea and airport stores in Korea, Singapore and Hong Kong. Its hotel and leisure unit directly operates two hotels and runs 3 hotel brands in all. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1991.

008830.text: DaedongGear makes power transmission parts and transmissions for cars, farm machinery and industrial machinery, and says it is the only Korean company devoted solely to power transmission devices. It is automating production to cut costs and developing high-precision products. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1991 and has 15 affiliates.

008870.text: Kumbi has four businesses: glass bottles for the liquor, beverage, pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries, tax-stamped bottle caps sold at home and abroad, plastic cosmetic containers, and cosmetics wholesale and retail. Founded in 1973 as a glass maker, it listed on the KOSPI in 1990 and has two subsidiaries.

0088D0.text: Meritz No.1 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

0088M0.text: Mezoo develops wearable patch-type patient monitors based on biomedical telemetry. Its HiCardi series, SmartView and LiveStudio provide mobile remote patient monitoring across inpatient, outpatient and remote settings. It is also developing AI-based digital biomarkers and early prediction for high-risk patients. It was founded in 2018.

008930.text: Hanmi Science is an operating holding company whose subsidiaries include a pharmaceutical maker. Besides its holding business, it runs a healthcare segment covering medical devices, food, beauty and IT solutions, added through a 2022 merger, and distributes drugs and health supplements through its HMP Mall. Founded in 1973, it was approved as a holding company in 2011.

008970.text: Kbi Dong Yang Steel Pipe makes steel pipes, including structural pipes, pipes for wind turbine foundations, gas and oil pipelines, steel pipe piles, coated water pipes and earthquake-resistant square tubes. It also runs a copper alloy business through a wholly owned subsidiary. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1977.

009070.text: KCTC is an integrated logistics company that began by running a container terminal. It handles port stevedoring, inland container transport, bonded warehouses, heavy cargo, parcel storage and delivery, and international multimodal transport, with facilities at major Korean ports and cities. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1978 and has 17 unlisted subsidiaries.

009140.text: Kie makes remote controls, thermostats and switches, and its main customers include a US TV company and large Korean electronics and car makers. It has subsidiaries in China and recently added another consolidated subsidiary through a share acquisition. Founded in 1973, it took its current name in 1974 and listed on the KOSPI in 1989.

009150.text: Samsung Electro-Mechanics is a Samsung Group electronic components maker with three businesses: passive components, semiconductor package substrates and camera modules. It supplies parts for smartphones, PCs, AI servers and cars through production and sales units in Korea and abroad, and is expanding products for AI, servers and automotive electronics. It was founded in 1973.

009160.text: Simpacinc runs press, ferroalloy, roll and trading businesses. Its press unit makes metal-forming machines and related equipment, and its ferroalloy unit has made ferroalloys since 1959, the first in Korea. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989 and took its current name in 2001 after separating from its former business group.

009180.text: Hansol Logistics provides third-party logistics for companies in Korea and abroad, including international freight, trucking and container transport. It has 13 consolidated subsidiaries, 11 of them overseas, and recently set up Logismile USA, INC. It was founded in 1994, acquired another company in 1996 and adopted its current name in 2014.

009190.text: Daiyang Metal makes and sells cold-rolled stainless steel, buying in stainless hot coil and processing it on its own cold-rolling lines. It has made only stainless steel for 53 years. Its subsidiaries include a lending company and a special-purpose company for bank borrowing. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1994.

0091W0.text: Shinyoung HappyTomorrow No.11 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

009200.text: Moorim Paper makes printing paper and bleached chemical pulp, and also operates in finance, steam and power generation, and golf courses. Its group includes a pulp maker, US and European units, a power company, a capital firm and a resort operator. Founded in 1973, it began printing-paper production in 1979 and listed on the KOSPI in 1990.

009240.text: Hanssem is a home interior company. It remodels kitchens and bathrooms, sells furniture online and offline, and supplies kitchen and storage furniture to housing developments. It launched an integrated shopping app in 2023 and has moved into office furniture for businesses. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 2002.

009270.text: Shinwon makes knitwear and sweaters on an OEM/ODM basis for export to about 20 regular buyers such as GAP and WAL-MART, using 9 overseas production bases including Guatemala and Vietnam. A main subsidiary runs logistics and property leasing. Founded in 1973 for textile manufacturing, apparel sales and trade, it listed on the Korea Exchange in 1988.

009290.text: Kwangdong Pharmaceutical sells herbal tonics and other pharmacy products, prescription drugs including a cancer treatment and a vascular drug, and beverages such as vitamin drinks, corn silk tea and bottled water. Its subsidiaries handle MRO purchasing, health supplement OEM/ODM and in-vitro diagnostic devices. Founded in 1963, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989 and has 21 subsidiaries.

009300.text: Sam-A Pharm makes and sells pharmaceuticals, including respiratory drugs, antibiotics, dermatological products, digestive drugs, fever and pain relievers, and circulatory and endocrine drugs. It also sells over-the-counter medicines and health supplements. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2000.

009310.text: Charm Engineering runs recycling and flat-panel display (FPD) businesses. Its recycling unit buys non-ferrous materials such as copper foil, recycles them and supplies domestic companies, while its FPD unit makes repair equipment for display panel production using laser, optical and software technology. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1987 and owns a savings bank.

009320.text: Ajin Electronic Components makes automotive electronic parts, including heaters and radar, as a second-tier supplier, and since 2023 has supplied electric vehicle heaters directly to carmakers. It switched from electronic components to automotive electronics after being acquired in 2010. Founded in 1973, it listed in 1989 and is building capabilities for electric and self-driving vehicles.

0093G0.text: Mirae Asset Vision Special Purpose Acquisition 8 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

009410.text: Taeyoung Engineering & Construction is a general builder ranked 24th in the 2026 construction capability ratings. It carries out civil, environmental, plant, building and housing work, and also runs a motor racing track, a hotel and housing and retail leasing. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989 and has 16 consolidated subsidiaries.

009420.text: Hanall Biopharma makes and sells about 160 drugs, including endocrine and cardiovascular medicines, and researches synthetic and biologic drugs. It is focused on developing new biologic drugs, running global clinical trials with partners, and uses a US unit for overseas trials and licensing. Founded in 1973, it listed in 1989.

009440.text: KC Green Holdings is a holding company in environmental engineering, environmental services, resource recycling and energy, with 16 companies in Korea and 17 overseas. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1994 and became a holding company in 2010. It set up three new companies through a 2024 spin-off and sold one of them in 2025.

009450.text: Kyung Dong Navien makes heating and cooling equipment, focusing on gas boilers, oil boilers and gas water heaters, and is expanding overseas through a global sales network. In 2025 it acquired a maker of smart-home, video phone and home network products. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1993 and has 16 subsidiaries.

009460.text: Hanchang Paper makes and sells manila board and white board. Using Korea's first line dedicated to all-pulp board, it supplies cigarette packaging, premium packaging and food packaging paper, and is developing specialty industrial papers. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSPI in 1987.

009470.text: Samwha Electric researches, makes and sells capacitors, including electrolytic, electric double-layer, chip electrolytic and hybrid types. They are used in home appliances, vehicle electronics, industrial equipment, renewable energy and ESS, and 5G products. It was founded in 1973 and has 3 unlisted subsidiaries.

009520.text: POSCO M-tech packages steel products and supplies aluminium deoxidizers for steelmaking. Its packaging unit wraps coils at POSCO's hot-rolled, cold-rolled and stainless steel plants and maintains equipment, and since 2012 it has also run a ferromanganese plant on contract. Founded in 1973, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1997.

009540.text: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering is the HD Hyundai Group holding company for shipbuilding, offshore plants, engines and machinery, and green energy, with 26 subsidiaries. Its shipyards build merchant ships, gas carriers, offshore vessels and naval ships and are developing hydrogen- and ammonia-powered carriers. Founded in 1973, it became a holding company in 2019.

009580.text: Moorim P&P is Korea's only producer of bleached chemical pulp and also makes printing papers such as art paper and woodfree paper at an integrated pulp and paper mill completed in 2011. It is part of a paper-focused business group. Founded in 1974 to supply pulp to domestic paper makers, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989.

009620.text: Sambo Industrial recycles used aluminium into aluminium alloys for auto parts and for the electronics and steel industries. Its subsidiaries make die-cast auto parts and run a broadcast channel business that operates PlayboyTV. Founded in 1974, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1993.

009680.text: Motonic is a tier-one supplier of vehicle parts to domestic carmakers, producing LPI systems, OPUs and FCEV parts on an OEM basis. It has a head office and two plants in Korea, and an Indian subsidiary is being liquidated. Founded in 1974 to make carburettors, it listed on the KOSPI in 1994 and took its current name in 2002.

0096B0.text: Samsung Special Purpose Acquisition 12 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

0096D0.text: Mirae Asset Vision Special Purpose Acquisition 9 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

009730.text: IREM makes stainless steel pipes and integrated deck plates used in construction, shipbuilding, cars, energy and buildings. It holds KC, KS and JIS quality certifications and KR, LR and DNV-GL classification approvals. Founded in 1974, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1990 and bought another company's deck plate business in 2024.

009770.text: Sam Jung Pulp makes and sells toilet paper, jumbo rolls, kitchen towels and other paper products, and is one of 5 large Korean tissue makers with integrated processing lines. In 2025 it halted one plant and reorganised production around two others to improve costs. Founded in 1974, it listed on the KOSPI in 2006.

009780.text: MSC supplies food additives. Its affiliates include an agar maker described as the largest in Asia and a producer of small-pack foods. It has run a research institute since 1987, bought an agar plant in 2023, and is building an extraction line for functional ingredients and pursuing the halal market. It was founded in 1974.

0097F0.text: Mirae Asset Vision Special Purpose Acquisition 10 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

009810.text: MDSsphere runs MRO and video content businesses, and through subsidiaries offers embedded software development and system software, industrial and office automation, and a virtual-asset derivatives exchange. It has 20 consolidated subsidiaries, 2 listed and 18 unlisted. Founded in 1974, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988 and took its current name in 2026.

009830.text: Hanwha Solutions is a Hanwha Group energy and chemicals company. It makes basic materials such as PE, PVC, CA and TDI, solar cells and modules, and builds solar plants, with further units in lightweight composites, electronic materials and property development. It is also developing AEM water electrolysis for clean hydrogen. Its origins date to 1965, and it listed in 1974.

0098T0.text: Kyobo 19 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

009900.text: Myoung Shin Industry makes lightweight car body parts using hot stamping, supplying tier-one suppliers with floor, moving and side body-frame and closure parts, as well as press dies. Its main subsidiaries in the US and China are tier-one suppliers to a global electric vehicle maker, and a Brazilian unit joined in 2025. It was founded in 1982.

009970.text: Youngone Holdings is a pure holding company. Through its subsidiaries it makes clothing, footwear and bags on an OEM basis for export and retails a global outdoor brand in Korea. It entered the global bicycle market by taking a stake in SCOTT in 2015 and is expanding production in Bangladesh and elsewhere. Founded in 1974 as an apparel maker, it became a holding company in 2009.

0099W0.text: Mirae Asset Vision Special Purpose Acquisition 11 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

0099X0.text: IBKS No.25 Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

010040.text: Korea Refractories makes, sells and installs shaped, unshaped and basic refractories and non-metallic fine powders. Its main markets are iron and steelmaking, cement, glass, heavy industry and power plants, and a main subsidiary runs a construction business. Founded in 1973, it listed on the Korea Exchange in 2000.

010060.text: OCI Holdings is a holding company that manages and invests in its subsidiaries, which include OCI, a basic chemicals maker, and OCI TerraSus, a producer of polysilicon for solar power. It has 128 subsidiaries. Founded in 1959, it listed in 1976 and became a holding company through a 2023 spin-off.

010100.text: Korea Movenex runs auto parts, flange and industrial machinery divisions, with half shafts and axles as its main auto parts. It has domestic manufacturing sites and 3 overseas production units in the US, China and Mexico. Founded in 1974 to make auto parts, flanges, machinery, steel structures, tanks and heat exchangers, it listed on the KOSPI in 1987.

010120.text: LS Electric makes, sells and maintains electrical, electronic, measurement, information and automation equipment. Its power business covers power equipment, systems and renewable energy, and its automation business supplies PLCs, inverters and HMIs. Founded in 1974, it listed in 1994 and has 42 consolidated subsidiaries, including a US unit.

010130.text: Korea Zinc is a non-ferrous metals smelter with 94 consolidated subsidiaries. Through subsidiaries it also trades non-ferrous metals, recycles steelmaking dust and is moving into electrolytic copper foil for rechargeable batteries. Abroad it makes and sells non-ferrous metals through an Australian unit and works in e-waste recycling, renewable energy and hydrogen. Founded in 1974, it listed in 1990.

010140.text: Samsung Heavy Industries is a Samsung Group shipbuilding and offshore company. It runs a shipyard and two R&D centers in Korea, and 10 overseas subsidiaries build ships and ship blocks and design offshore facilities. It recently set up two US units to expand in that market. Founded in 1974, it listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in 1994.

010170.text: Taihan Fiberoptics makes optical fiber and optical cable and is the only Korean company that produces both in one integrated process. It has sales units in the Americas and Europe and a telecommunications construction subsidiary, and acquired INCAB AMERICA LLC in 2026. Founded in 1974, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1994.

0101C0.text: Hana Thirty-six Special Purpose Acquisition is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

010240.text: Heungkuk Metaltech makes undercarriage drive parts for construction machinery, such as track rollers, carrier rollers and idlers, and counts JOHN DEERE among its main customers. It set up local units in China in 2005, Japan in 2018, India in 2019 and the US in 2022. Founded in 1974 as a steel forging company, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

010280.text: Itcenentec provides IT services in digital engineering (DE), IT outsourcing (ITO) and customer experience (CX) for the public, defense, manufacturing, logistics, service and financial sectors. Its consolidated subsidiaries include ITCEN Japan. Founded in 1981, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2000 and took its current name in 2024.

010400.text: Woojin I&S makes and installs building systems. Its high-tech unit supplies fluoropolymer-coated ducts and hook-up piping for semiconductor and display plants, while its general unit handles water supply and drainage, heating and cooling, air conditioning and fire protection. Founded in 1975, it listed in 2018, has 1 unlisted subsidiary and set up an R&D center in 2020.

010470.text: Oricom runs advertising and magazine businesses. It provides advertising, public relations, promotion and market research services, and publishes magazines in Korea under licences for global media brands such as Vogue and GQ. Founded in 1975, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2000 and acquired 100% of another advertising agency in 2015.

010580.text: SM Bexel makes auto parts and batteries. Its automotive unit supplies engine and transmission products such as water pumps and oil pumps to domestic carmakers, and its battery unit makes primary and rechargeable batteries, ESS and special batteries for defense, and is expanding into drone battery packs. Founded in 1961, it listed in 1994.

0105P0.text: Eugene Special Purpose Acquisition 12 is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) listed on the KOSDAQ. It was set up to merge with an unlisted company and has no operating business of its own until a merger is completed.

010640.text: Chinyang Poly Urethane makes flexible polyurethane slab foam, used as a material in cars, furniture and beds for cushioning, sound absorption and insulation. It holds about 15% of the market among 6 domestic polyurethane foam makers and sources more than 95% of its main raw materials in Korea. Founded in 1975, it listed in 1989.

010660.text: Hwacheon Machinery makes and sells machine tools that cut and grind metal into machine parts and molds, and in 2000 entered the machining of engine cylinder blocks for cars. It has moved from general-purpose machine tools to dedicated machines. Founded in 1975, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988.

010690.text: Hwashin makes chassis and body parts and electrification parts for cars, with affiliates of a major domestic car group as customers. It has units in the US, India and China, set up a new Indian unit in 2024, completed an EV parts plant in the US state of Georgia in 2025 and is building a new domestic plant for battery pack cases. Founded in 1975, it listed in 1994.

010770.text: Pyung Hwa Holdings is a holding company with 10 domestic and 5 overseas affiliates. Its subsidiaries make automotive and industrial parts, including anti-vibration parts, hoses, oil seals, O-rings, molds and jigs, and supply domestic carmakers. Founded in 1950, it listed on the KOSPI in 1986 and became a holding company through a spin-off in 2006.

010780.text: IS Dongseo runs concrete, construction and environmental businesses: it makes precast concrete and PHC piles, builds apartments, retail and civil projects, and recycles construction waste, cars and used batteries. It was founded in 1975 as a spin-off from a construction company's civil engineering division. It has 32 consolidated subsidiaries and set up BTS Technology GmbH in 2024.

010820.text: Firstec is a defense company that develops and produces fire control equipment and drive systems, and has taken part in programs such as the T-50 and the K-9 self-propelled howitzer. It ranks within the top 20 Korean defense firms by sales. Founded in 1975 and later designated a defense contractor, it listed on the KOSPI in 1989.

010950.text: S-Oil is an oil refiner that also makes lube base oils and petrochemicals, including aromatics and olefins. Refining makes up 79.5% of its sales. Its largest shareholder, AOC, holds 63.4% of the shares. It was founded in 1976.

010960.text: Samho Development is a civil engineering contractor that builds roads, subways and port facilities in Korea and abroad, and has expanded into building and civil works after obtaining a general construction licence. It also owns a venture capital firm and 2 venture funds that invest in small and venture companies. Founded in 1976, it listed on the KOSPI in 2005.

011000.text: GeneOne Life Science runs pharmaceutical and textile businesses. Its pharmaceutical arm offers CDMO production of nucleic acid materials, mainly plasmid DNA, and develops DNA medicines using its AIMX DNA platform. Its textile arm holds 20~30% of the domestic market. Founded in 1976 to make clothing interlinings, it listed in 1987 and has wholly owned subsidiaries in the US and Vietnam.

011040.text: Kyungdong Pharm makes prescription drugs, mainly cardiovascular, digestive and blood pressure medicines. Pharmaceuticals account for about 96% of sales, with own-product sales about 66% and resold goods about 27%, and it also has a leasing business. Founded in 1976, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 1992.

011070.text: LG Innotek is an LG Group electronic components maker with three divisions: optical solutions, package solutions and mobility solutions. It makes camera modules, semiconductor substrates, photomasks and communication modules, with domestic plants and production units in China, Indonesia, Poland, Mexico and Vietnam. Founded in 1970, it listed on the KOSPI in 2008 and merged with an affiliate in 2009.

011080.text: Hyungji Innovation and Creative makes and sells apparel under its own brands, including the YEZAC shirt brand, BON menswear and Carries Note and BON:E womenswear, through offline and online channels. It is focusing on online sales, with a new online-only brand in 2026 and expansion into Asian markets such as China and Japan. Founded in 1976, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2004.

011090.text: Enex makes and sells kitchen furniture, built-in wardrobes and interior furniture. It supplies large builders directly and sells to consumers through about 90 dealers, online stores and home shopping channels. It has a Vietnamese unit and a domestic subsidiary. Founded in 1971, it listed on the KOSPI in 1995.

011150.text: CJ Seafood makes processed seafood, including fish cakes, seaweed, grilled fish and fried tofu, and says it launched Korea's first hygienic premium fish cakes in 1985. Founded in 1976 as a seafood processor and exporter, it listed on the KOSPI in 1988, expanded into seaweed through a 2012 merger and bought 100% of a producer from an affiliate in 2023.

011170.text: Lotte Chemical is a Lotte Group petrochemical company with production facilities in Korea's petrochemical complexes. With its affiliates it works in 5 areas: basic chemicals, advanced materials, fine chemicals, battery materials and hydrogen energy. It produces PE and PP from naphtha crackers and high-performance ABS and PC for appliances, IT and cars. It was founded in 1976.

011200.text: HMM is a shipping and logistics company with container, bulk (tanker and dry bulk) and terminal businesses. Its fleet ranges from small ships to very large container ships and VLCCs, serving routes worldwide. In 2023 it ordered methanol-fuelled container ships and trialled biofuel. Founded in 1976, it listed on the KOSPI in 1995 and has 34 subsidiaries.

011210.text: Hyundai Wia is a Hyundai Motor Group auto parts maker with 13 production sites in 7 countries. It supplies engines, modules, constant-velocity joints, 4WD and thermal management parts to carmakers including GM, and also works in mobility solutions and defense, including factory automation and future weapon systems. It was founded in 1976.
