It bought an auto electronics company in 2019 and moved fully into the business from 2020, and has a phone parts subsidiary in Vietnam. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

101360.text: Eco & Dream makes secondary battery materials and catalyst materials based on its own environmental materials technology, and its NCM precursors are used in electric vehicle and other batteries. It completed a precursor plant in 2025. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KONEX in 2013, moved to the KOSDAQ in 2020 and took its current name in 2022.

101400.text: N Citron makes and sells fully digital audio amplifier chips for flat-panel TVs. It has 6 subsidiaries covering marketing in China, restaurant brands and beauty device sales, and acquired restaurant companies in 2024 and 2025 to build a portfolio from premium global dining to mid-priced brands. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

101490.text: S&S Tech makes blank masks for semiconductors and displays. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009, became a mid-sized company in April 2026 and set up S&S MATERIAL PTE. LTD. in Singapore that month to expand abroad. Its 4 consolidated subsidiaries work in new technology financing and bio and science services.

101530.text: Haitai Confectionery and Foods makes biscuits, gum, candy, chocolate, snacks and pies, supplying its main brands nationwide. Its frozen food business holds a share of the dumpling market with its own brand, and it is stabilizing a new plant and improving purchasing to raise productivity. Founded in 2001, it was acquired by a consortium in 2005.

101670.text: Hydro Lithium makes ultra-high-purity battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate, anhydrous lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate, while gradually scaling back its original civil engineering business. Founded in 1995 to make civil engineering materials, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2008. It took its current name and entered battery materials in 2022 after a change of largest shareholder.

101680.text: HNK Machine Tool makes machine tools, which cut and grind metal workpieces, and industrial machinery. It develops large machine tools with its own technology that were previously imported from Europe and Japan, serving industries such as plants, aircraft and power generation, and says it alone has independent design capability in large machine tools. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

101730.text: Wemade Max develops and supplies games as its single business segment, running mobile and PC online games and a licensing business for its titles. Founded in 1997 to develop and supply software, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009 and has 8 consolidated subsidiaries.

101930.text: Inhwa Precision makes large parts for ship engines, power generation equipment and machinery. Using an integrated production system, it makes cylinder covers, bed plates and frame boxes for Korean engine makers. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010 and diversified by acquiring companies in 2012 and 2013.

101970.text: Wooyang HC designs, makes and delivers plant equipment for large construction and engineering firms, including reactors and heat exchangers for chemical plants and high-efficiency condensers for energy plants. It also works in water treatment and environmental businesses and takes part in national CCUS projects. It was founded in 1993 to make chemical products and became a corporation in 1996.

102120.text: ABOV Semiconductor is a fabless company whose main products are 8-bit and 32-bit MCUs for home appliances, supplied to Korean electronics makers. It also supplies sensor and power semiconductor products, has analog IP design capability and is developing AI MCUs. Founded in 2006 to develop non-memory chips, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

102260.text: Dongsung Chemical is a non-financial holding company, spun off in 2008, that also makes products after absorbing affiliates in 2015 and 2021. It produces polyurethane resins for shoe soles and synthetic leather, TPU and the melamine foam VIXUM, and built a polyurethane production hub in Indonesia in 2025. Its main subsidiaries make cryogenic insulation and medical devices.

102370.text: K Auction runs four businesses: art sales, art auctions, art brokerage and other services, with auctions making up 76% of sales. Founded in 2005 to run art auctions, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022. It added a subsidiary in 2023 and completed small-scale mergers with three companies in 2024.

102460.text: Reyon Pharmaceutical makes and sells prescription drugs, original drugs and active pharmaceutical ingredients, and sells contrast agents under an exclusive contract with ISK. It is building a biologics production platform at its bio plant and developing new drugs through open innovation. Founded in 1964 to localize drug ingredients, it listed in 2010 and has an investment company affiliate.

102710.text: ENF Technology makes process chemicals for semiconductors and displays, along with fine chemicals, color paste and CMP slurry for chips, from three plants including one in Ulsan. Its subsidiaries include investment units in China and the United States, a slurry company and an electronic materials company. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

102940.text: Kolon Life Science has a chemical division that makes active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates and eco-friendly antimicrobials for personal care and marine paints. Its bio division's pipeline includes the osteoarthritis treatment TG-C, the AAV-based neuropathic pain treatment KLS-2031 and the vaccinia virus-based cancer therapy KLS-3021. It was founded in 2000.

103140.text: Poongsan makes copper and copper alloy sheets and strips and lead frame materials, while its defense business produces military and sporting ammunition and precision forgings. It has production and sales operations in the United States, China and Southeast Asia, and is developing new alloys, researching combat drones and expanding defense exports. It was spun off in 2008 from Poongsan Holdings, which was founded in 1968.

103230.text: S&W makes ship engine parts, industrial parts and forgings, supplying Korean shipbuilders and engine makers. Founded in 1967 and incorporated in 1990, it entered special-material industrial bolts through a 2003 merger and later expanded into precision machining and forgings for engines. It is developing locally made engine parts and attends overseas trade shows to grow abroad.

103590.text: Iljin Electric makes heavy electrical equipment, including power cables, transformers and circuit breakers for voltages from low to extra-high, and offers total solutions for power grids. After entering Western Europe and North America in the early 2000s, it has reached about 80 countries and is pursuing turnkey orders to raise overseas sales. It was spun off from Iljin Holdings in 2008.

103840.text: Wooyang makes, imports and exports processed farm, livestock, fishery and forest products, canned fruit and ready-to-eat foods, supplying ingredients and contract-made products to business customers such as food companies and coffee chains. Founded in 1992, it is expanding its own brands for the cafe and home meal replacement markets and pursuing overseas sales.

104040.text: DSM runs a mobility division that makes auto parts using its mold technology and also works in solar power and supercapacitors, and a leisure division that operates a theme park built on robotics and AI. Founded in 2000 to make auto parts, molds and machine tools, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009 and changed its name after merging with a leisure platform developer in 2025.

104200.text: NHN Bugs is an NHN affiliate that runs a digital music streaming and distribution service through its music portal, along with a music broadcasting service. Its business-to-business arm invests in music production and distributes music under exclusive rights. Founded in 2002 for online music services and distribution, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

104460.text: Dypnf designs, builds, installs and commissions powder conveying systems, supplying integrated solutions to petrochemical and other industries. It has localized equipment in fields that relied on imports and is working to expand overseas. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009 and has 3 subsidiaries, including DY P&F USA Corp.

104480.text: TK Chemical has three divisions: chemicals, which makes and sells PET chips; construction, which develops and builds housing; and electronics, which makes touchscreens. Founded in 2007 to make synthetic fibers and chemicals, it took over a trading company's chemical business in 2008 and added construction through a 2015 merger.

104540.text: Corentec makes artificial joints, with hip and knee implants making up more than 85% of sales, and has added spinal fixation devices and shoulder and ankle implants. The company says it was founded in 2000 as Korea's first specialist artificial joint maker. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013, markets abroad through its US unit Corentec America and runs health checkup services and an ASC hospital through a subsidiary.

104620.text: Yellow Balloon Tour sells domestic and overseas package tours and air tickets to Korean and foreign customers, and also runs city sightseeing tours and travel information services. It serves travelers abroad through its Japan unit, Yellow Balloon Japan, and has diversified by buying stakes in two companies. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019.

104700.text: KISCO makes steel rebar with a 120-ton electric arc furnace and rolling mills, selling to builders, distributors and a government procurement agency, with a sales network centred on Busan and two other regions. It is cutting costs, diversifying customers and adopting digital technology amid a weak domestic construction market. It was spun off in 2008 and listed on the KOSPI the same year.

104830.text: Wonik Materials produces high-purity specialty gases used in semiconductor and display manufacturing, such as N2O, NH3, F2 mix, C4F8, Xe and PF3, supplying major global chip and display companies. Founded in 2006 to make industrial gases, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011 and has three subsidiaries, one in the United States and two in China.

105330.text: KNW makes materials for electronic components, auto parts and semiconductors, with production sites in Ulsan and another Korean city as well as China and Vietnam. A subsidiary is building an anhydrous hydrofluoric acid plant, targeted for completion in 2026, to strengthen its chip materials business. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009 and has subsidiaries including K.N.W Vietnam.

105550.text: Edge Foundry is a sensor company with printed electronics, electromagnetic and thermal infrared imaging technology, developing and supplying automotive pedal sensors and infrared thermal sensors and camera modules. It localized automotive sensors that had relied on imports and supplies tier-1 auto suppliers, global parts makers and carmakers. Founded in 2006 to make automotive displacement sensors, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

105560.text: KB Financial Group is a financial holding company that controls subsidiaries through share ownership, covering banking, financial investment, insurance and credit cards. Its units provide retail and corporate banking, brokerage and investment services, property and casualty insurance, and card services. It was formed in 2008 through a comprehensive share transfer involving 8 companies, including its bank.

105630.text: Hansae makes knitwear, activewear and casual clothing on an OEM and ODM basis for US buyers such as TARGET, OLD NAVY and GAP, with production units in 8 countries. In 2024 it entered El Salvador and acquired the US company TEXOLLINI to add higher-priced products and cut logistics costs. It was spun off in 2009 and relisted on the KOSPI the same year.

105740.text: DK-Lok makes instrumentation fittings and valves sold under its own DK-Lok brand to the shipbuilding, offshore plant, power generation, semiconductor, CNG and hydrogen vehicle industries. Exports make up 71% of sales, and it is expanding into aerospace and defense parts. Founded in 1986, it adopted its current name and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

105760.text: Posbank develops and makes PC-based POS systems and self-order kiosks running on various operating systems, used in restaurants and retail. In 2025 it expanded a plant to build an automated production line with capacity of up to 283,000 units a year, and it is widening its global distribution channels. Founded in 2003, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024.

105840.text: Woojin applies its measuring instrument technology mainly to instruments for nuclear power plants, and also makes temperature sensors for semiconductors and industry, automation equipment for steelmaking and equipment condition monitoring systems (CMS), and maintains plant instruments. Its main subsidiary maintains nuclear and thermal power plants. Founded in 1980 to make industrial measuring instruments, it listed on the Korea Exchange in 2010.

106080.text: KEM Tech makes IR filters, a key part of smartphone camera modules, and secondary battery sub-materials, and runs a food and beverage business that supplies food, drinks and daily goods through large-company retail channels. It is developing battery parts as a new business and, after signing a main ESS contract in 2025, is preparing for mass production. It was founded in 2001.

106190.text: High Tech Pharm makes active pharmaceutical ingredients for injectable antibiotics, focusing on carbapenems such as imipenem and ertapenem, which the company says command high prices because of their strong antibacterial effect. Exports make up its sales, with Europe at 78.81% and Asia and other regions at 21.19% at mid-2026. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

106240.text: Fine Technix makes and sells a full range of LED lighting, including indoor lights, street and security lights and floodlights, for public-sector, private business, consumer and overseas markets. It has 8 unlisted subsidiaries and overseas units. It was created through a spin-off in 2009 and focused on LED lighting after a further spin-off in 2022.

107590.text: Miwon Holdings is a holding company whose main subsidiaries make energy-curable resins, inkjet and printed electronics products, and surfactants. Its resin subsidiary produces UV and EB curing monomers and oligomers for coatings, inks, adhesives and electronic materials. It was spun off in 2009 and converted to a holding company structure in 2017.

107600.text: Sebitchem is a waste recycling company that grew by recycling waste acid from semiconductor and display plants. Its main business now recovers nickel, cobalt and manganese, precursor solutions and high-purity lithium compounds from waste cathode material and battery scrap, using multi-stage leaching and solvent extraction. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022.

107640.text: HanJungNCS makes parts for energy storage systems and electric vehicles, including liquid cooling systems that control heat from battery charging and discharging, a field where it says it holds a leading position. It supplies EV cooling fan modules to global auto electronics suppliers and runs joint R&D with global battery makers. Founded in 1995, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024.

108230.text: Toptec supplies factory automation equipment, including battery cell module assembly lines, EV motor automation equipment and AGV and AMR-based smart logistics systems. Its product sales business covers nanofiber membrane materials and health and beauty goods, and it is applying physical AI and robotics to smart manufacturing. Founded in 1996, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009 and has a nanomaterials subsidiary and overseas units.

108320.text: LX Semicon is a fabless company that designs and sells system chips for display panels, home appliances and cars, including DDI, T-Con and PMIC products for driving panels. It is developing automotive MCUs and heat dissipation solutions as new growth businesses and preparing to enter the automotive and server markets. Founded in 1999, it moved its listing to the KOSPI in 2022.

108380.text: Daeyang Electric serves the shipbuilding, defense, rail and automotive industries with lighting, electronic and electrical systems, underwater robots and pressure sensors. A subsidiary makes batteries for defense use, and it added another company as a consolidated subsidiary during the year. Founded in 1988 to make industrial lighting, electronic systems and switchboards, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

108490.text: Robotis develops, makes and sells actuator-based humanoid robot products, including smart actuators, precision reducers, humanoid robot platforms, physical AI software and autonomous delivery robots. It combines in-house hardware with AI control algorithms and is expanding sales abroad through a US unit. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

108670.text: LX Hausys makes building materials such as windows, flooring, wallpaper and PF board insulation, as well as automotive fabrics and parts and functional films for appliances and furniture. It has plants in Korea, including in Ulsan, and production and sales units in the United States, China, Russia and Germany. It was spun off in 2009 from the industrial materials division of a chemical company.

108860.text: Selvas Ai develops deep learning-based speech recognition, speech synthesis, handwriting recognition and image recognition technology, and says it was Korea's first AI specialist company and ranks first in the Korean speech synthesis market. It is combining large language models and generative AI with its speech engines to build AI agents and platforms, and is pursuing AI medical products. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

109070.text: Joosung runs telecom network, customer and logistics businesses, developing and producing ICS and RF repeaters, 5G antenna combiners, optical communication solutions, car dashcams and window film. It was spun off in 2009, moved into optical parts through a 2017 merger and diversified by absorbing another company in 2021. It has 4 unlisted affiliates.

109080.text: Opticis makes digital optical links for video signals, providing long-distance video transmission products that meet various interface standards, and says it developed the world's first digital optical link. It designs and makes the key optical materials and parts itself and offers transmission solutions for 4K and 8K video and AR and VR platforms. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

109610.text: SY makes prefabricated sandwich panels and has subsidiaries in Korea and several units abroad in countries including Vietnam, Nepal and Cambodia. In 2024 it set up a UPVC window profile maker in Nepal and domestic units for solar power and cosmetics wholesale, and in 2025 it absorbed two affiliates. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

109670.text: C-site makes knitwear mainly on an OEM basis with some ODM production, operating plants in Guatemala and Indonesia. It chose Guatemala as a production base for its access to the US market during the fast fashion boom of the 1990s and has worked with global brands since 2000. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2023.

109740.text: DSK makes precision systems in four groups: secondary battery equipment, camera module equipment, bonding and in-line systems for flat panel displays, and mechatronics. It is using its mechatronics manufacturing capability to diversify within factory automation. Founded in 1995 to make display equipment and mechatronic systems, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

109820.text: Genematrix develops and sells molecular diagnostics and medical diagnostic reagents based on its own technologies, including C-Tag, Encleap, TriO and RFMP, and is developing vaccines and immuno-oncology treatments. Founded in 2000 for biotech drug and genetic diagnostics development, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009. It bought stakes in an affiliate in 2011 and 2017 and absorbed it in 2019.

109860.text: Dongil Metal is a steel castings maker incorporated in 1984 that listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009. Its affiliates include listed companies and unlisted units such as PT. DONGIL METAL INDONESIA and PT. DONGIL CASTING. In February 2024 it acquired a company to diversify and grow sales, and in September that year it absorbed a subsidiary.

109960.text: Aptocrom distributes and sells medicines, including skin treatments, digestive drugs, tonics and antibiotics, and runs real estate and equipment rental businesses. One of its 3 subsidiaries designs, makes and installs special insulation for nuclear power plants and forms and installs foam glass insulation. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

110020.text: Jeonjinbio makes products from naturally derived materials, including household goods such as capsule detergents, air fresheners and deodorizers, agents that reduce damage from pest animals, and pet products and biotech feed. Its capsule detergents use plant-derived surfactants with 5-in-1 technology, and its repellents draw on a library of more than 700 active substances. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

110790.text: Creas F&C makes and sells golfwear through a portfolio of brands ranging from masstige to luxury. Its subsidiaries run a golf course and an online shopping mall, and include Hydrogen S.R.L, which makes and sells sportswear. Founded in 1998 to make and sell clothing, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

110990.text: DIT makes AOI, LASER and VISION AI Solution equipment used in the semiconductor, display, secondary battery and automotive industries. Its AOI systems use machine vision to inspect defects, and its laser systems improve wafer yields and serve SiC power semiconductors. Founded in 2005 to make chip and display equipment, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

111110.text: Hojeon makes and exports sportswear and high-performance outdoor clothing, supplying about 20 global brands on an OEM basis. It buys materials abroad, manufactures finished goods at its production unit in Indonesia and exports them to buyers. Founded in 1985, it listed on the KOSPI in 2017 and has 9 unlisted subsidiaries.

111380.text: Dong IN Entech makes outdoor backpacks and outdoor gear on an ODM basis for about 40 brands worldwide, combining ultra-light, high-strength aluminum technology with ergonomic sewing. Since opening its first plant in the Philippines in 1996, it has built up 12 units there and 1 in Vietnam. Founded in 1992, it listed on the KOSPI in 2023.

111710.text: Namhwa Industrial runs a 54-hole public golf course in the Gwangju region, which it says was the area's first public course and is the third largest in Korea, earning green fees, food and beverage, cart rental and golftel lodging income. Ahead of a KTX station opening in 2027, it is building a resort and more golftels. Founded in 1990, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

111770.text: Youngone is an outdoor and sports company that makes clothing and footwear on an OEM basis at overseas factories for about 40 global brands, and it expanded into brand distribution by acquiring SCOTT and OR. It runs 47MW of solar power capacity at its sites worldwide and aims to reach 100MW. It was spun off in 2009.

112040.text: Wemade develops, distributes and sells PC online and mobile games, runs a licensing business based on its long-running game IP and operates a blockchain platform. Founded in 2000 to develop and sell online games and software, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009 and has 39 subsidiaries, including WEMIX PTE. LTD.

112290.text: Ycchem makes semiconductor process materials, including a commercialized solution that prevents pattern collapse in ArF processes using special surfactants and polymers. In 2016 it developed pattern collapse prevention solutions and developers for EUV processes, and it also produces photomask developers and capacitor cleaning solutions. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022.

112610.text: CS Wind makes wind towers, with production units in Vietnam, the United States and elsewhere, and counts global wind turbine makers and renewable power companies as its main customers. It entered offshore wind substructures by acquiring a European maker in 2023 and is pursuing orders based on long-term supply contracts. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSPI in 2014.

113810.text: Dgenx develops and makes mufflers, key parts of automotive exhaust systems that clean exhaust gas and reduce noise and vibration, and runs this as a single business segment. It was created in 2006 by splitting off a company's auto parts manufacturing arm and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012. Its subsidiaries are DH HONGKONG CO.,LIMITED, a holding company, and a hydrogen production company.

114090.text: Grand Korea Leisure runs three casinos for foreigners only, two in Seoul and one in Busan, open 24 hours a day all year. Its main markets are Asian countries such as Japan, China, Mongolia, Hong Kong and Taiwan, and it offers tiered complimentary services to affluent customers. It was founded in 2005 to attract foreign tourists and earn foreign currency, and listed on the KOSPI in 2009.

114190.text: Kangwon Energy has three segments: secondary batteries, making battery materials and equipment; plants, making industrial steam generators and chemical and environmental energy equipment; and new businesses, including AI data center infrastructure. Founded in 1976 as a boiler maker, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009, took its current name in 2021 and has one subsidiary.

114450.text: Green Lifescience is a KPX group fine chemicals company that develops and makes active pharmaceutical ingredients, drug intermediates, electronic materials and crop protection products for global drugmakers. The company says it has Korea's only phosgene reaction process and largest hydrogenation facilities, which it uses to pursue contract manufacturing, and it is adding materials for electronic substrates and AI chips. Founded in 2005, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2009.

114630.text: Polaris Uno makes synthetic fiber for wigs, and its chemical division produces monomers and photochromic dyes for corrective plastic eyeglass lenses and adhesives for wigs. It has subsidiaries in South Africa and Indonesia and belongs to a group of 11 companies. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

114810.text: Hansol Iones provides precision machining, cleaning and coating for parts used in front-end semiconductor and display manufacturing equipment, offering integrated service from machining to coating. It is expanding by localizing import-dependent equipment parts and developing new materials. Founded in 1993 and incorporated in 2005, it joined the Hansol group in 2022 and took its current name.

114840.text: iFamilySC is a branding company built around beauty brands, having entered cosmetics in 2016 with a color cosmetics brand aimed at 18 to 24 year olds. It began in 2000 as an online wedding hall business and changed its name in 2012 to add other family event services and expand abroad. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2021.

115160.text: Humax makes video and audio equipment and runs gateway, automotive electronics and EV charging businesses. As a set-top box maker it supplies pay TV operators with solutions covering digital broadcasting from transmission to devices. It was spun off from Humax Holdings in 2009 and belongs to the Humax group, which has 14 domestic affiliates.

115180.text: Qurient develops drugs, with a pipeline that includes a CDK7-inhibiting cancer drug, the dual-payload ADC QP101 and an Axl, Mer and CSF1R triple-inhibitor cancer drug. Through strategic alliances with research institutes in France and Germany, it holds first-look rights to early cancer and autoimmune disease projects. Founded in 2008, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016.

115310.text: INFOvine mainly runs a mobile certificate storage service that keeps digital certificates on phones for use on any PC, which the company says it was the first in Korea to develop and commercialize. It partners with Korea's 3 mobile carriers to serve banks, brokerages, card companies, insurers, e-commerce firms and public agencies. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

115440.text: Woori-Net makes transmission equipment, including packet-optical transport systems (POTN), access gateways and cellular IoT products, and also supplies organic materials for OLED displays. In 2025 it added a defense company, with a 74.48% stake, and a wholly owned communications device developer as subsidiaries. It was founded in 2000 by researchers from a large electronics company's network division and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

115450.text: HLB Therapeutics runs three core divisions: bio, cold chain and electronics. Founded in 2000 to develop embedded graphics software, it expanded into cold chain and electronics through mergers and entered biotech in 2014 through a drug co-development deal with RegeneRX. It is running global clinical trials through its US joint venture ReGenTree and its subsidiary Oblato.

115480.text: Cu Medical Systems makes emergency medical devices, including automated external defibrillators (AED), and says it was the first in Asia to develop an AED. It also makes fetal and neonatal devices and patient monitors for customers in Korea and abroad, and added a consolidated subsidiary during the year. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

115500.text: Korea Computer & Systems provides fault-tolerant, non-stop systems and solutions to finance, telecom and public-sector clients, along with NonStop SI, transport infrastructure and kiosk businesses. It is targeting new markets with enterprise virtualization, cloud and security solutions and device encryption technology. It was spun off in 2002 from a company founded in 1974 and merged with a research lab in 2007.

115530.text: Cnplus makes electronic components and automation equipment, and entered renewable energy by acquiring and merging with a wind power company in 2021. Its 4 subsidiaries are CNPLUS VINA, an overseas manufacturing unit, a Korean chip maker, a renewable energy developer and a car dealership. Founded in 2003, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

115570.text: Starflex makes FLEX and banner fabrics for advertising signs and exports to about 100 countries. The company says it holds about 60% or more of the Korean FLEX sign market, and it is adding eco-friendly and recycled products. Founded in 1985 and incorporated in 1996, it adopted its current name in 2006 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

115610.text: Imagis is a fabless chip design company founded in 2004 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010. It develops touch controller ICs, haptic driver ICs, MST ICs and SAR sensor ICs used in a range of IT devices. Building on its touch, SAR sensor and power and haptic ICs, it is working to diversify its products and widen its target markets.

117580.text: Daesung Energy supplies city gas for cooking, heating, air conditioning, commercial and industrial use, using natural gas bought from its wholesale supplier. It also runs 11 natural gas filling stations and a combined heat and power plant, and city gas makes up more than 97% of sales. It was created in 2009 through a spin-off of its parent holding company's city gas business and listed on the KOSPI in 2010.

117670.text: Alphachips designs system semiconductors, providing RTL design and SoC chip implementation in its DS division and developing IR receiver and key scan ICs in its MS division. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010. The company says it became the first design house for a Korean chipmaker's foundry in 2003, and it was made an official design solution partner of that foundry in 2019.

117730.text: T-Robotics develops and makes vacuum robots for semiconductor and display production and autonomous logistics robots. Its products include vacuum robots that move OLED glass and semiconductor wafers, AGV and AMR robots for smart factories, and gait rehabilitation robots. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018, and the company says it was the first in Korea to develop vacuum robots for OLED.

118000.text: Metacare was created in 2009 when a drugmaker spun off its medical business. It now runs medical and pharmaceutical products, real estate development, hair transplant clinic consulting and an internet advertising agency. It fully acquired one unlisted subsidiary in 2024 to expand its healthcare infrastructure and consolidated another in 2026 to move into advertising, and it has three unlisted subsidiaries.

118990.text: Motrex develops and produces in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) products and automotive electronics based on its automotive HMI capabilities, supplying global carmakers. Building on its display technology, it is expanding into vehicle convenience devices, camera systems, and EV and PBV solutions. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 and has 20 consolidated subsidiaries.

119500.text: Formetal makes forged precision machine parts, supplying about 800 types of parts to about 150 customers in industrial machinery, automobiles, robots and wind power, defense and agricultural machinery. Designated an excellent technology research center by the trade and industry ministry, it is developing key parts for aircraft landing gear. Founded in 1969, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

119610.text: Interojo makes and sells contact lenses. In Korea it mainly sells its own Clalen series, while overseas it focuses on OEM/ODM sales. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010, it has 3 subsidiaries, including one set up to develop smart lenses.

119650.text: KC Cottrell is an environmental engineering company spun off from a holding company in 2010. It supplies dust and gas treatment equipment for coal-fired power plants, steelworks, cement plants and petrochemical sites in Korea and abroad, and has carried out about 6,000 projects, with entities and offices in 5 countries. It is commercializing CCUS and tunnel dust collectors and developing climate technologies such as semiconductor F-gas treatment.

119830.text: ITEK provides wafer and package testing for non-memory semiconductors, sorting good chips from defective ones. It also makes and sells composite materials and runs semiconductor infrastructure operations, cold chain solutions and battery safety management systems. Founded in 2005 to test system semiconductors, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010 and has 3 unlisted consolidated subsidiaries.

119850.text: GnCenergy designs, builds, delivers and installs emergency and commercial generators, and is expanding into biogas, fuel cell and overseas power generation. It bought 100% of a heavy fuel oil power plant operator in Papua New Guinea in 2024 and 100% of a hydrogen fuel cell power company in 2025. Founded in 1989 and incorporated in 1993, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013.

120030.text: Chosun Welding Pohang makes coated welding materials used to join metals in construction, automobiles, shipbuilding and other industries. It sells through dealers in Korea and abroad and directly to large end users. It was created in 2010 through a spin-off from a holding company and listed on the KOSPI the same year.

120110.text: Kolon Industries was formed in 2010 when Kolon's manufacturing business was split off. Its businesses cover industrial materials such as tire cord, airbags and aramid; chemicals including petroleum, phenolic and epoxy resins; fashion including outdoor, golf and casual wear; and golf course operation and venture investment. It has 36 subsidiaries in Korea and abroad and absorbed an affiliate in 2026.

120240.text: Daejung Chemicals & Metals produces reagents for general, analytical, diagnostic and specialty testing, electronic-grade solvents and active pharmaceutical ingredients, selling them in Korea and abroad. Main products include alcohols, acetonitrile, tetrahydrofuran and ethyl acetate, and its main customers are chemical and pharmaceutical companies. Founded in 1968, it incorporated in 1986 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

121440.text: Golfzon Holdings is a holding company whose main subsidiaries run screen golf, golf course operation and golf equipment distribution businesses. Its revenue comes mainly from brand royalties, management advisory fees, rental income and equity-method income. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011 and became a holding company in 2015.

121600.text: Advanced Nano Products makes advanced materials from ultrafine nano powders, including CNT conductive additives for secondary batteries, TCO targets for displays and CMP slurry for semiconductors. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011, it has production facilities in the United States, Poland and China. It is expanding its European and U.S. production bases and commercializing CMP slurry for chips such as HBM.

121800.text: Vidente develops, makes and sells displays for HD digital broadcasting. It supplies high-performance HD video equipment to broadcasters including BBC, CNN, NBC, ABC, Disney and FOX TV through a worldwide distributor network, and has released products using S3D, 360-degree VR and HDR. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

121890.text: SD system develops, makes, sells and maintains intelligent transport systems (ITS), including highway toll collection systems (TCS/ETCS), electronic toll on-board units (OBU), fire information systems, integrated control center systems and smart parking systems. It is expanding into next-generation transport and safety infrastructure such as C-ITS and multi-lane electronic tolling. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010.

122310.text: Genoray makes medical X-ray imaging equipment for both medical and dental use. Its medical products include C-arm and mammography systems, and its dental line covers panoramic, CT and portable units. Founded in 2001 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018, it has sales subsidiaries in the United States, Germany, Japan, Türkiye and China.

122350.text: Samkee is an aluminum die-casting company founded in 1978, with alloy, casting and machining divisions that make engine, transmission and electric vehicle parts. It has production sites in Korea, including Incheon, and in the United States, and handles everything from alloy production to shipment. It is expanding battery and chassis parts for global EV brands, and the company says it built Korea's first die-casting clean room.

122450.text: KX Innovation runs three businesses: broadcasting, where it transmits programs and operates channels for program providers; leisure, where it runs public golf courses in Korea and abroad; and semiconductor materials for chips and SSDs. The company says its in-house transmission technology keeps it first in Korea's transmission market. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011, it is diversifying into golf course data and VPN security monitoring.

122640.text: YEST develops, makes and sells heat treatment and pressure process equipment for semiconductors and displays, such as chillers, furnaces and pressure cure systems. Through subsidiaries it also supplies chip fab infrastructure parts including heating jackets and clean hoods. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015, it has 5 subsidiaries and production sites in Korea, including Incheon, and in Vietnam.

122690.text: Seojin Automotive produces drivetrain parts such as hybrid dampers, clutches and flywheels, while its subsidiaries make interior and exterior parts including plastic bumpers and consoles. Founded in 1990 to make and sell auto parts, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012 through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company. It has 29 subsidiaries.

122870.text: YG Entertainment runs record and digital music, concert, and management and advertising businesses, and also sells content and merchandise featuring its artists. Founded in 1998 for music publishing and the training and management of new artists, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. During the current fiscal year it set up 5 new subsidiaries to widen its investment portfolio.

122900.text: iMarketKorea runs a B2B e-commerce and MRO purchasing agency business covering a broad range of industrial goods, and has expanded into wholesale of medicines and medical supplies. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSPI in 2010, it has 5 overseas entities in Vietnam, China, the United States and Hungary, and its U.S. unit is pursuing a high-tech industrial complex there.

122990.text: WiSoL focuses on RF front-end products, producing SAW filters, duplexers and RF modules for mobile phones. It mass-produces components for 2G, 3G and 4G as well as filters and modules for 5G. Founded in 2008 to develop and sell RF products such as SAW filters, duplexers and Bluetooth modules, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010 and has 5 affiliates, 3 overseas and 2 in Korea.

123010.text: MSDI was founded in 2003 on patented image sensor packaging technology and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016 as a technology growth company. In image sensor packaging it provides photo sensor CSP packaging and testing using its own NeoPAC® technology. Its other businesses are contract processing of automotive air conditioning parts, coating of mobile camera module parts, and IT and robot automation systems.

123040.text: MS Autotech was founded in 1990 to make and sell car body parts and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010. In August 2024 it split off its operating business into a new company and became a holding company. It earns mainly dividends, rental income and management fees, and runs its car body parts business through subsidiaries.

123330.text: Genic researches, develops, produces and sells face mask packs based on its patented water-soluble hydrogel technology. It sells through its own brand online and offline and supplies OEM/ODM products to Korean and global brands. Founded in 2001 for cosmetics and pharmaceutical R&D, manufacturing and sales, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011 and wholly owns a subsidiary in China.

123410.text: Korea Fuel-tech makes auto parts, including fuel system components such as carbon canisters and plastic filler necks, and interior and exterior trim parts including sunshades. Founded in 1996, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012. It has 7 consolidated subsidiaries in China, India, Poland, Slovakia and the United States.

123420.text: Wemade Play is a KOSDAQ-listed game software company founded in 2010 that owns one subsidiary. It releases mobile games on app markets, earning revenue from game sales and advertising. It is developing services using AI processes and game engine technology, and is pursuing new titles based on its main game series and expansion into global markets.

123570.text: Emnet is a digital marketing company founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011, with three subsidiaries. In 2021 it sold part of its stake in eMnet Japan, turning it into an associate, and it continues its overseas business centered on Asia through a partnership. In 2025 it added a digital marketing firm serving small and mid-sized advertisers as a subsidiary.

123690.text: Hankook Cosmetics sells about 700 kinds of skincare and color cosmetics through channels such as online, home shopping and distributors, and through door-to-door sales. It was created in 2010 when a cosmetics manufacturer spun off its sales and property leasing businesses. Through subsidiaries it also runs brand-shop cosmetics sales and online sales.

123700.text: SJM was created in 2010 through a spin-off from a holding company and makes flexible couplings for vehicle exhaust systems and expansion joints for buildings and plants. It acquired control of SJM ECS to make cooling system parts for electrified vehicles. It is also expanding into aerospace by developing a domestically made gimbal joint for the KF-21 fighter jet.

123750.text: Alton makes and sells bicycles and bicycle parts, including electric, shared, everyday, and leisure and racing bicycles. Founded in 1994 as a trading company, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011 through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company. It adopted its current name at its 2024 annual shareholders' meeting.

123840.text: Nuon mainly sells health functional foods such as cissus and boswellia, along with household goods under its own brand. It was set up in 2010 as a special purpose acquisition company listed on the KOSDAQ and entered the vacuum equipment business through a 2013 merger. After a merger in 2024 it took its current name, and it discontinued its vacuum deposition equipment business in 2025.

123860.text: Anapass is a fabless maker of system semiconductors for displays, founded in 2002 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010. Its main products, T-Con and TED ICs, are core chips for display panel production, and it develops custom chips to panel makers' requirements. It has supplied T-Con chips for large displays since 2008 and TED ICs for smartphone OLED panels since 2018.

123890.text: Korea Asset IN Trust is a real estate trust company founded in 2001 and licensed for the trust business by financial regulators. It offers land trusts, collateral trusts and other real estate trust products, along with agency services, PFV asset management and REIT asset management. Since 2012 it has set up financial subsidiaries to provide trust, REIT, lending, investment and asset management services.

124500.text: Itcen Global, founded in 2005 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014, is the controlling company of the Itcen group and oversees sustainability management and new business development. It operates in management and investment, a Web3 business based on metal manufacturing and distribution, and IT services. It has invested in a digital asset exchange in Busan, set up a venture capital joint venture, acquired a generative AI company and runs a TIPS startup program.

124560.text: Taewoong Logistics is a third-party logistics company founded in 1996 that provides sea, air and rail freight, customs clearance, insurance and inland transport for exports and imports worldwide. It runs 17 overseas local subsidiaries and has affiliates including a logistics center operator. It secures steady volumes through long-standing business with large companies and a network with major shipping lines.

125020.text: TC Materials is a copper materials company founded in 1995 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025. It uses copper to make materials for power infrastructure, automotive electronics and home appliances, as well as motor-related products, including winding wires for power equipment such as enameled copper wire, CTC and rectangular copper wire. The company says it was the first in Korea to develop enameled copper wire technology for submarine and extra-high-voltage power cables.

125210.text: Amogreentech was founded in 2004 to make and sell new materials and applied products, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019 as a technology growth company. Its advanced materials division covers high-efficiency magnetic materials and heat dissipation and nano membrane materials, alongside functional components and energy and environmental systems divisions. Its group has 8 affiliates, both listed and unlisted.

125490.text: Hallacast makes precision parts from aluminum, magnesium and zinc. Its direct customers are large Korean companies, with global carmakers as end customers. Founded in 2005 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025, it focuses on parts for AI-based autonomous driving and eco-friendly vehicles, and it is working with a global AI carmaker and has won orders for humanoid robot parts.

126340.text: Vina Tech researches, develops and mass-produces core materials and components for supercapacitors and hydrogen fuel cells. It is expanding from supplying single cells to system-level products, and in fuel cells is building a global supply chain based on its carbon materials technology. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020 and has 5 unlisted subsidiaries.

126560.text: Hyundai Futurenet is an ICT company running digital signage, immersive content, enterprise messaging and IT services, including system operation and integrated AI solutions. Founded in 1992, it started out in cable broadcasting and value-added telecom services and took on its current businesses after a split in 2020. In 2024 it acquired and merged an IT company to strengthen its IT expertise, and it has one subsidiary.

126600.text: BGFecomaterials was founded in 1997 to make high-performance polymer chips and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010. It produces high-performance polymer compounds such as PA66, PA6 and PP, optical films, specialty gases and electrolyte additives for secondary batteries. Its businesses span engineering plastics and chemicals, electronic component materials, auto parts materials and semiconductor materials, and it has 9 subsidiaries in Korea and abroad.

126640.text: Hwashin Precision makes chassis parts, precision-machined parts and replacement parts, supplying them as modules or individual parts to Korean carmakers and their affiliates. Its raw material processing division sells slitted products to tier-1 suppliers. Founded in 2010, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

126700.text: HyVISION SYSTEM develops and makes automation equipment for phone camera modules and smart components, operating in four segments: IT and mobile, secondary batteries, automotive electronics and 3D printers. Its main subsidiaries handle autonomous driving electronics equipment and 3D printers and robotics. Founded in 2002 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012, it has 6 subsidiaries, including a unit in India.

126720.text: Soosan Industries provides maintenance services for power plants in Korea and abroad, including routine and planned preventive maintenance at nuclear, thermal and renewable energy plants. Founded in 1983 for routine maintenance of construction works, it shifted to power plant maintenance in 2001 under a policy to foster private maintenance firms. Its subsidiaries make MMIS, maintain instrumentation and control equipment, and run an overseas solar power business.

126730.text: Korchip makes electric and electronic components, mainly small secondary batteries, and also distributes MLCCs and passive components as a partner of a components maker. Founded in 1994, it gained its core technology in 2002 by acquiring that company's DLC business. It has raised its own products to 70% of sales through R&D and equipment investment, and is shifting coin-type products to SMD types.

126880.text: JNK Global designs, makes and installs industrial heaters for oil refineries and petrochemical plants, and also runs hydrogen extractor and hydrogen refueling station businesses using its own technology. Founded in 1998 as a spin-off from an engineering company, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011; the company says it is Korea's only industrial heater specialist. It works with LHT of the United States and is expanding in the Middle East through a Saudi Arabian unit.

127120.text: JS Link is a personalized medicine healthcare company founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011; it adopted its current name in 2025. Its businesses include genome analysis services, personal genome analysis, molecular diagnostics and personal identification. It is also entering production of sintered permanent magnets for electric vehicles, robots and UAM, building raw material supply partnerships as it prepares production.

127710.text: The Asia Business Daily is an online and offline business news media company founded in 2005 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015, with 8 consolidated subsidiaries. Its main businesses are advertising, content and finance, and it also runs job training programs on behalf of government ministries and universities. It focuses on online content for mobile and smart platforms and is pursuing growth in paid content.

127980.text: Finecircuit was founded in 1991 to make and sell printed circuit boards (PCBs) and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2023. It mainly produces rigid PCBs for home appliances such as refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners, and double-sided PCBs account for 94% of sales. Its main subsidiary makes and sells zirconia blocks for dental use.

128540.text: Ecocab makes electrical and electronic auto parts, mainly automotive wires. Its Mexican plant produces wiring harnesses and LED modules for export to North America, and it set up a Polish subsidiary to build a supply base for Europe. It began making auto parts in 2007, listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018, and has 5 overseas subsidiaries and 1 in Korea.

128660.text: PJ Metal is a non-ferrous metals company created in 2010 through a spin-off and listed on the KOSDAQ in December 2010. It supplies deoxidizers, an additive used in steelmaking, to two major Korean steelworks, and sells all of its billets, an intermediate material for aluminum extrusion, to aluminum extruders. A subsidiary set up in 2023 runs a recycled lead business.

128820.text: Daesung Industrial traces its roots to 1947 and took its current form through a split in 2010; it merged with its holding company in 2017. Its oil and gas division runs gas stations and charging stations as, the company says, the largest general dealer of a major oil refiner, and its power division supplies electricity, heat and steam from an LNG-based district energy plant. It is based in Seoul and has 20 unlisted subsidiaries.

128940.text: Hanmi Pharm makes and sells pharmaceuticals and was created in 2010 when its parent spun off its drug manufacturing and sales business. It has 5 consolidated subsidiaries, 1 in Korea and 4 overseas, grouped into pharmaceuticals, active pharmaceutical ingredients and overseas pharmaceuticals. It recently made Aptose Biosciences Inc., a listed overseas company, a consolidated subsidiary after acquiring additional shares.

129260.text: Intergis was founded in 1956 mainly for port cargo handling and freight transport, and listed on the KOSPI in 2011. It has domestic subsidiaries that run port terminals and logistics centers, and overseas units in Vietnam, Mexico, Japan, the United States, Thailand and Poland. It set up the Polish unit in the first quarter of 2026 to expand its overseas network.

129890.text: Abko is a PC gaming company founded in 2001 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020, with one subsidiary. It sells gaming gear, PC parts and small appliances, and runs public-sector projects such as IoT charging storage boxes and fire prevention control boxes. Through brands including ABKO, HACKER and COX it is strengthening its product lines, and it runs its own service centers.

129920.text: Daesung Hi-Tech makes and sells precision parts, Swiss-type automatic lathes and compact machining centers, and is widening its end markets to defense, robots, AI data center cooling and medical devices. Founded in 1995 and incorporated in 2001, it gained Swiss-type lathe technology by acquiring NOMURA DS of Japan in 2014. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022 and set up a Romanian unit in 2025 as a base for Europe's defense market.

130500.text: GH Advanced Materials makes nonwoven fabrics for car interiors, such as floor carpets, ISO dash and seat backs, and also produces yarn. Founded in 1979 and incorporated in 2001, it took its current name in 2016. It set up an Indian subsidiary in 2009, began producing its own yarn after acquiring a yarn business in 2018, and set up a U.S. unit in 2021 that runs a pallet business.

130580.text: Nice D&B was set up in 2002 through a partnership between a Korean credit information company, Dun&Bradstreet of the United States and Tokyo Shoko Research of Japan. The company says it is the only Korean member of the D&B WorldWide Network, and it provides global company information, credit certification and business partner management services. It also offers business support for small and mid-sized firms and research services.

130660.text: Korea Electronic Power Industrial Development runs and maintains equipment at thermal and nuclear plants across Korea, serving a power generation company and private power producers. The company says it handles more than 70% of fuel and environmental equipment operation at Korea's thermal power plants. Founded in 1990 and listed on the KOSPI in 2010, it has entered turbine and boiler maintenance and operates water treatment facilities at nuclear plants and liquefied carbon dioxide facilities.

130740.text: TPC makes auto parts including precision steel tubes, anti-vibration parts, fuel filler systems and cooling system parts, supplying Korean and global carmakers including GM. Founded in 1998 to make drawn tubes and fuel and coolant tubes, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. A consolidated subsidiary makes and sells PVC pipes for water supply, sewage and fire protection.

131030.text: Optus Pharmaceutical develops, produces and sells treatments for eye diseases such as dry eye, with a product range that includes preservative-free eye drops. Founded in 2010, it merged with another company in 2013 and took its current name in 2022. It began building a new plant in 2024 to add single-use eye drop capacity, and uses an AOA training platform and KAM to manage its accounts.

131090.text: Secuve is a security company founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. Its system security products include Secuve TOS, a secure operating system based on digital signature authentication, along with iGRIFFIN and LogGRIFFIN. The company says it was the first in Korea to commercialize such a system and holds the largest domestic share in secure operating systems, and it is investing in mobile authentication and multi-modal biometrics R&D.

131100.text: TN entertainment runs entertainment and food and beverage businesses. Its entertainment arm holds exclusive and agency contracts with 57 artists, handling management, broadcast and advertising appearances and digital content production, while its F&B arm franchises a fried chicken brand and directly runs Western-style restaurants. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

131180.text: Dilli Illustrate develops and makes industrial digital printers and UV digital printers based on its own inkjet technology, with UV curing that allows instant printing on a variety of materials. Its main printer series sells in North America and Europe, and it is developing next-generation high-end solutions with global partners. Founded in 1996, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

131220.text: Daihan Scientific distributes, manufactures and services laboratory equipment for research, supplying products from about 270 manufacturers in Korea and abroad. The company says it is Korea's largest business of this kind. Founded in 1980, it incorporated in 1993 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011, and its subsidiaries include a unit in Vietnam.

131290.text: TSE supplies semiconductor and display test products, including probe cards, interface boards, test sockets and OLED inspection equipment. Founded in 1995 to make and sell chip test equipment and peripherals, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. Its main subsidiaries make PCBs and probe pins and provide semiconductor testing services.

131370.text: Rsupport develops remote support and remote control software, supplying products such as a remote support solution and a video conferencing platform to telecom operators, financial firms and public institutions. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013 through a SPAC merger. It has subsidiaries in Japan and China, and exports make up more than 60% of its business.

131400.text: EV Advanced Material makes flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs) used in advanced IT products and electric vehicle batteries, and also runs a transparent display business. Founded in 2004 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2010, it took its current name in 2021 to expand into the electric vehicle business. It has run a wholly owned Vietnamese unit, EVAM VINA, since 2019.

131760.text: Finetek makes display equipment, secondary battery manufacturing equipment, touch systems and digitizers, and is expanding into mobile, home appliance and automotive electronics products. Its components division produces in Vietnam and its equipment division in Korea. Founded in 2008 for display parts and equipment and battery manufacturing equipment, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

131970.text: Doosan Tesna specializes in testing, a back-end process for system semiconductors, providing wafer testing, package testing and die preparation (DP). Its main product groups are SoC, CIS, MCU and smartcard ICs, and it is moving into automotive power semiconductors such as SiC. Founded in 2002 for chip testing and engineering services, it took its current name in 2022.

133750.text: MegaMD is an education company for university students and adults, offering online and offline courses through several brands. It covers professional exam preparation, such as the LEET and the bar and patent attorney exams, and certification courses such as social worker and licensed real estate agent. Founded in 2004 for online education information and private academies, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

133820.text: Finebesteel makes and sells steel sections, including inverted angles used in shipbuilding to add structural strength and stability, and general sections such as track shoes and sheet piles. Using hot rolling technology, it produces shipbuilding sections in various sizes and low-temperature steel for major shipbuilders. Founded in 2007 and listed in 2014, it runs smart factory, robot automation and energy IT businesses through subsidiaries.

134060.text: e-future develops English language teaching (ELT) content and publishes books, having entered the ELT market with EFL Phonics in 2003. It develops English content for preschool and elementary learners worldwide and supplies AI-based ELT content and SMARTREE. Founded in 2000 to develop internet education content and software, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

134380.text: Miwon Chemicals produces and supplies chemicals, including sulfur products such as lump and powdered sulfur, sulfuric acid, oleum and refined sulfuric acid; rubber additives; and detergent raw materials such as sulfonic acid, alcohol sulfates and ethanolamine. It also trades chemical goods including EOA. It was created in 2011 through a spin-off and listed on the KOSPI the same year.

134580.text: Topco Media restructured in 2025 through a merger with a webtoon company, becoming an IP and AI business built on webtoon platforms and content. It runs webtoon platforms in Korea, Japan, Taiwan and North America, earning revenue mainly from platforms and content distribution. In September 2026 it changed its name and added business purposes to expand into AX, combining IP and AI.

134790.text: Sidiz mainly makes and sells chairs, with divisions for its Sidiz chairs, sofas and Alloso, along with research and production units. It was spun off from a furniture maker in 2010 as an educational furniture company, listed on the KOSPI in 2011, and in 2018 took over an affiliate's chair business along with its current name. It has 2 unlisted subsidiaries.

136150.text: Woniltni develops and makes key equipment for the hydrogen, LNG and nuclear energy industries, and the company says it was the first in Korea to domestically produce combustion-type vaporizers (SCV) and reliquefaction units for natural gas. In hydrogen it stores hydrogen with storage alloys and produces it with reformers, and it supplies systems for a class of Korean submarines. It was incorporated in 1998.

136410.text: Assems makes solvent-free hot-melt film adhesives and offers one-stop services including lamination, coating and development of adhesive functional coated yarn. Its main product, hot-melt adhesive film for shoes, goes to global brands, and it also supplies films for clothing and car headliners. Founded in 2003, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022.

136480.text: Harim is a vertically integrated chicken producer covering feed, breeding and hatching, slaughtering and processing, and meat processing. It produces whole chickens, cut parts and home meal replacement products at its processing plants under HACCP standards, and supplies feed to farms from its own feed mills. Founded in 1990, it was re-established through a spin-off in 2011, and a subsidiary handles slaughtering of spent hens and exports.

136490.text: Sunjin is an integrated livestock and food company making compound feed for pigs, cattle and poultry, raising hogs, and selling fresh meat and processed meats such as sausages and patties. Founded in 1979 to make compound feed, it was split into operating and holding companies in 2011 and is listed on the KOSPI. It has 21 subsidiaries, 7 in Korea and 14 across 5 other countries, and a holding company is its largest shareholder.

136540.text: WINS Technet develops and supplies information security systems and related services. Its roots go back to 1996, and the current company was created in 2011 when the network security business was split off and listed on the KOSDAQ. Since 2024 it has entered the zero trust market, expanded its lifelong education business and launched Sniper AIVAX, an AI security solution, and it has two subsidiaries.

137080.text: Narae Nanotech develops and makes equipment including FPD equipment for OLED, electrode process equipment for secondary batteries, logistics automation equipment and PLP process equipment for semiconductors. Founded in 1995 as a display equipment maker, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022. In 2026 it set up NARAENANOTECH USA INC to serve customers more efficiently and liquidated its earlier U.S. entity.

137310.text: SD Biosensor is an in vitro diagnostics company with a portfolio spanning immunodiagnostics, molecular diagnostics, point-of-care testing (POCT), clinical chemistry, self-testing and chronic disease management. Backed by approvals such as WHO PQ, CE-IVD and FDA, it sells in more than 100 countries. It was created in 2010 through a spin-off of its parent's biosensor business and listed on the KOSPI in 2021.

137400.text: People & Technology makes roll-to-roll production equipment for secondary battery electrodes, battery foil and IT materials, a business it began in 2003. Its battery division supplies electrode manufacturing equipment for electric vehicles, ESS and mobile devices, and its materials division supplies equipment for battery foil, optical films and other electronic materials. It is pursuing LFP battery and cathode material production through a subsidiary and bringing copper foil in-house through a Chinese unit.

137940.text: NextEye mainly makes and sells LCD visual inspection equipment using machine vision, along with polarizing film, BLU and glass edge chipping inspection equipment. Founded in 1998 to make automatic measurement and control equipment for industrial processes, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. It has 8 subsidiaries, including an image processing hardware maker, a cosmetics company in China and a bio and cosmetics distributor in the United States.

137950.text: JC Chemical was founded in 2006 to make and sell biodiesel and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. It runs biofuel and palm plantation businesses, supplying biodiesel and bio heavy oil to refiners and power companies and producing and selling CPO and PK in Indonesia. It wholly owns JC ENERGY SINGAPORE PTE. LTD. and runs its oil palm business through two Indonesian companies.

138040.text: Meritz Financial Group is a financial holding company that manages subsidiaries in three core businesses: non-life insurance, financial investment and specialized credit finance. Its insurance arm sells long-term, auto and general insurance, its securities arm runs a comprehensive investment banking business, and its capital arm offers leasing, installment finance and new technology finance. The company says it was set up in 2011 as Korea's first insurance holding company.

138070.text: Sinjin SM mainly produces standard plates, a basic component for the machinery industry, using precision machining equipment built with its own technology. Founded in 2001 to sell cutting machines and standard and non-standard plates, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011. Its subsidiaries include a Korean company and units in Thailand, Japan, Singapore, Taiwan and Malaysia.

138080.text: OE Solutions mainly makes and sells optical transceivers and laser diodes (LD), a key optical component, and the company says it has the largest share of the Korean market. Beyond 5G, it is diversifying into FTTH, CATV/MSO, telecom and data center networks and expanding overseas. Founded in 2003, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

138360.text: NRobotics operates in three segments: automation (meat processing and food equipment), robots (industrial robots, control systems and process automation) and infrastructure (robots, kiosks, autonomous robots and access control systems for public institutions). It is developing robot systems that combine food automation equipment with robot control technology. Founded in 2001 to make cosmetic ingredients, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013 and completed a merger with a robotics company in 2026.

138610.text: Nibec develops peptide drugs, biomaterials for tissue regeneration and oral health products using its peptide-based drug delivery and biomaterial technology. Its dental regenerative biomaterials hold overseas approvals including from the FDA and are sold through global implant companies, and it is also developing new peptide drugs. Founded in 2004 to commercialize research from a biointerface engineering research center, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011.

138930.text: BNK Financial Group is a financial holding company set up in 2011 through a comprehensive share transfer by a bank and BNK's securities, credit information and capital units. It later set up systems and savings bank units, and added a second bank in 2014, an asset manager in 2015 and a venture capital firm in 2019. Through its subsidiaries it provides banking, specialized credit, financial investment, savings banking and venture investment services.

139130.text: iM Financial Group is a financial holding company set up in 2011 through a comprehensive share transfer involving a bank based in Daegu, a credit information company and a card network company. It manages and funds its subsidiaries, which provide banking, securities trading and brokerage, and life and annuity insurance. It is pursuing a nationwide network through conversion to a commercial bank, along with digital finance and overseas expansion, to diversify its revenue.

139480.text: E-mart was created in 2011 when a retailer spun off its hypermarket business. It runs 7 business segments, including retail and real estate, and operates 156 hypermarkets, 241 supermarkets and 5,493 convenience stores in Korea. Overseas it runs premium grocery stores and a winery.

139670.text: KineMaster is a mobile software company founded in 2002 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2011, with one unlisted subsidiary. Its main products are two video editing apps used worldwide, one of which carries the company's name. It continues to invest in building out its platforms and is using AI technology to meet demand for mobile video editing.

139990.text: Ajusteel makes and sells color-coated steel sheets with surfaces processed in various ways, used in premium video appliances, home appliances, building materials and auto parts. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSPI in 2021. It runs subsidiaries in the United States, China and Poland to follow global appliance makers' localization strategies, and moved into B2C business through a merger in 2025.

140070.text: Surplus GLOBAL buys and sells used equipment for front-end and back-end semiconductor processes, running a platform business that trades thousands of used tools a year through a worldwide network. The company says it is the world's largest distributor of used chip equipment. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017, it has 11 unlisted subsidiaries and recently set up EQ GLOBAL USA.

140410.text: Mezzion Pharma was founded in 2002 to make and sell pharmaceuticals, listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012, and focuses on new drug development for global markets. Its pipeline covers erectile dysfunction, benign prostatic hyperplasia, portal hypertension, pulmonary arterial hypertension, single ventricle heart disease and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. After filing a new drug application with the U.S. FDA for its single ventricle treatment, it is running an additional clinical trial.

140430.text: Catis is a spatial-awareness security platform company founded in 2006 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024. It develops platforms that process status data on secured spaces and moving objects, supplying government agencies, nuclear power plants, airports and data centers. It supplies perimeter intrusion detection platforms (PIDS) to more than 500 national key facilities and is upgrading its quantum security and Edge AI platforms linked with robots and drones.

140520.text: DaeChang Steel was founded in 1980 to process, make and sell steel and building materials, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014. In January 2024 it merged two main subsidiaries, adding aluminum and steel divisions, and took on a real estate subsidiary. It now runs 4 divisions: steel, raised access floors, aluminum and real estate.

140670.text: RS Automation specializes in robot motion control and energy control devices. Its motion control division develops and produces servo drives and servo motors, and its energy control division supplies PCS products for solar and fuel cell power. Founded in 2009 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017, it is developing next-generation controllers for physical AI and expanding globally through a contract with Rockwell Automation of the United States.

140860.text: Park Systems develops and produces atomic force microscopes (AFM) and sells them worldwide, mainly for industrial and research use. In the latest half-year, industrial systems made up 65% of sales, research systems 28% and other items 7%. Founded in 1997 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015, it strengthened its optical metrology capabilities by acquiring Accurion of Germany in 2022 and Lyncee tec SA of Switzerland in 2025.

141000.text: Viatron Technologies develops, makes and sells heat treatment equipment for display TFT backplane processes, including pre-compaction, hydrogenation and dehydrogenation, activation and annealing. Founded in 2001 to make machinery for semiconductor and flat panel display production, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012. Its subsidiaries are a venture capital firm and a semiconductor equipment maker.

141080.text: LigaChem Biosciences is a research-focused drug developer founded in 2006 to develop synthetic new drugs and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013. Using its own next-generation ADC platform, ConjuALL, and open innovation, it researches cancer drugs and pursues global commercialization through technology transfers. It is focused on new ADC technologies such as novel-mechanism and dual payloads, bispecific antibody ADCs and next-generation immuno-oncology drugs.

142210.text: Unitrontech distributes semiconductors and displays from overseas vendors in Korea and abroad, supplying DRAM, NAND flash, MCUs and display products to a range of manufacturers. Founded in 1996, it has two subsidiaries: a chip and display distributor and a secondary battery equipment maker, which it consolidated in 2026 after acquiring shares under a shareholders' agreement.

142280.text: GC Medical Science makes in vitro diagnostic reagents for immunodiagnostics, clinical chemistry and molecular diagnostics, medical devices such as blood glucose meters and HbA1c tests, and dialysis solutions for chronic kidney failure patients. Founded in 2003 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014, it entered the blood glucose business through an acquisition in 2015. It develops products quickly with outside partners and relies on long-term supply contracts.

142760.text: MOA Life Plus was founded in 1999 on its HumaMAX and MucoMAX patents and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016 as a technology growth company. It supplies poly-gamma-glutamic acid ingredients, sells health functional foods and functional cosmetics, develops new drugs with its platform technology and distributes pharmaceuticals. It has received U.S. FDA NDI approval and supplies the European market.

143160.text: Intelligent Digital Integrated Security develops, produces and sells video recorders, IP cameras and VMS, running an ODM business in Korea and selling its own brand through 55 overseas partners. It was created in 2011 when its parent, founded in 1997, split off its development, manufacturing and sales business, and it relisted on the KOSDAQ. It has 21 affiliates, including IDIS Europe, IDIS Americas and IDIS Japan.

143210.text: Hands supplies aluminum wheels to carmakers on an OEM basis, with global carmakers including GM among its main customers. Founded in 1972 as a plywood maker, it began making aluminum wheels in 1984. It has 6 unlisted subsidiaries, one of which specializes in large, high-end wheels.

143240.text: Saramin runs online HR services built on two-way matching between job seekers and employers. Its career platform business makes up 54.5% of sales, outsourcing 29.6% and recruitment consulting 15.9%. Founded in 2005 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012, it has one unlisted consolidated subsidiary and absorbed another company during the current fiscal year.

143540.text: YoungWoo DSP makes and sells inspection equipment for displays, semiconductors and secondary batteries, as well as smart logistics automation systems. Its main products, OLED cell and module inspection systems, go to major display makers in Korea and abroad, and it is expanding into semiconductor wafer bump inspection using its optics and image processing technology. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

144510.text: GC Cell develops cell therapies and runs cell therapy, specimen testing, cord blood banking, bio logistics and CDMO businesses. It was set up in 2011 by taking over a cell therapy business from a group company and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016. A merger in 2021 with an affiliate brought it an immune cell therapy product and a CDMO business, and its group has 53 affiliates.

144960.text: New Power Plasma supplies key components for semiconductor and display thin-film and etch equipment, making remote plasma generators (RPG), RF generators and matchers. Founded in 1993, the company says it was the second in the world to develop a remote plasma generator for semiconductor and FPD CVD processes. It is expanding in global markets, pushing into RF generators and pursuing new businesses such as eco-friendly exhaust treatment equipment.

145020.text: Hugel is a medical aesthetics company that researches, makes and sells a type A botulinum toxin biopharmaceutical derived from Clostridium botulinum, along with hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers. Its main subsidiary focuses on HA filler research and manufacturing. Founded in 2001 to develop, make, sell and export biomedical products, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

145170.text: Nobland International is an apparel ODM company that designs and exports mainly knit and woven clothing for about 40 global fashion brands, from mass-market to premium and online and social media-based labels. Founded in 1994, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024. Acquisitions in 2024 and 2026 gave it production capacity across all apparel categories.
