145210.text: Dynamic Design makes tire molds and 3D-sintered sipes, supplying three Korean tire makers and top-tier global tire companies. The company says it was the first in Korea to develop a segmented mold manufacturing method, which improved quality and enabled mass production. Founded in 1999 and listed on the KOSPI in 2015, it is pursuing new business through 3D printer development.

145270.text: K-top Reits is a real estate investment company listed on the KOSPI. It invests in property and pays shareholders dividends from the income, rather than running an operating business.

145720.text: Dentium develops, produces and sells dental medical devices and biomaterials, mainly implants, which make up 75% of sales, with digital equipment at 12% and biopharmaceuticals at 13%. About 80% of its sales come from overseas, where it runs 23 subsidiaries and sells in about 70 countries. Founded in 2000, it says it ranks second in Korea with a market share of about 20%.

145990.text: Samyang was created in 2011 through a spin-off from Samyang Holdings. Its food business makes sugar, flour, starch sugars and oils and fats, and its chemicals business makes engineering plastics, PET containers, ion exchange resins and polymers for personal care. Its subsidiaries include a packaging company and units in Hungary and Vietnam, and in 2026 it set up new units in the United States and Japan.

146060.text: YulChon makes steel tubes through pipe forming and precision drawing for use in automobiles, heavy equipment and heat exchangers. It supplies global carmakers including GM through their vendors, and can design drawing processes for small to large diameters. Founded in 1986, it has production subsidiaries in Mexico and Poland and is building a Polish plant to expand in Europe.

146320.text: BCnC makes quartz, silicon and ceramic consumable parts used in semiconductor etch and thin-film deposition processes. It has developed and mass-produced the synthetic quartz QD9+ and the new material CD9, and has localized silicon ingot production. Founded in 2003 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022, it is developing import-replacing materials such as ST-T1 and BC-T1 for front-end and back-end chip processes.

147760.text: Protec Mems Technology makes probe cards, custom consumable interface devices that test the function of chips on a wafer after front-end processing. It commercialized MEMS-based 3D probe cards in 2006 and has developed and supplied 2D MEMS probe cards since 2023. Founded in 2004 to make and sell semiconductor inspection equipment, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016.

147830.text: Cheryong Industrial makes and sells electrical equipment for transmission, distribution and underground lines, along with telecom equipment and railway materials. It supplies mainly metal and synthetic resin products to public institutions and private customers, with its head office in Seoul and an R&D center in Daejeon. Created through a spin-off in 2011, it makes products in small, order-based batches and is developing power equipment for HVDC and smart grids.

148150.text: Se Gyung Hi Tech makes functional films used in the displays and housings of small and mid-sized IT devices. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019. It set up a Vietnamese production subsidiary in 2013, runs a Japanese unit (SGJ) and a design center in China for R&D, and holds 55% of an ultra-precision pattern developer and 73% of a secondary battery safety solutions company.

148250.text: RN2 Technologies makes ceramic components based on its LTCC materials technology, including MLC, MCP and ceramic heat-dissipation substrates for power semiconductor packaging, as well as parts for mobile base stations and medical devices. The company says it supplies the world's 5 largest wireless equipment makers, including Ericsson. Founded in 2002 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016, it is developing ceramic substrates for 6G communications and EV inverters.

148780.text: Becu Ai is an AI data infrastructure company that collects, refines and supplies many kinds of data and offers AI technology and data platform services. Its main services include AISURFER, RDPLINE and JCopilot, and its customers include LG, SKT and KT. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022 as a technology growth company.

148930.text: Hytc makes ultra-precision parts for secondary battery manufacturing equipment used in electrode and assembly processes, including PX-SHAFT, KNIFE UNIT, winding cores, CUTTER and ultrasonic horns. Founded in 2005, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022. It has overseas units in China, Poland, the United States and Indonesia, and 6 unlisted subsidiaries.

149950.text: Avatec uses coating and etching technology to supply parts and materials for displays in phones, TVs and tablet PCs and for home appliances. Its main products include glass slimming and ITO and metal coating, and it also supplies MLCCs for electronics, IT, automotive electronics and renewable energy. Founded in 2000 to make vacuum thin-film coating products for displays, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012.

149980.text: Hironic develops and makes medical aesthetic devices based on energy sources such as HIFU, RF and lasers, supplying hospitals and clinics in Korea and abroad. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014. Its 3 consolidated subsidiaries handle domestic B2B sales, B2C home-care beauty devices and service in Japan.

150900.text: Fasoo Ai is an information security company founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013. It spun off its application security business into a subsidiary in 2018 and entered CPS security in 2024 by acquiring another company's business. In 2026 it set up a new company, Symbologic, to build ties with the U.S. AX consulting firm Konsilix, and brought Fasoo Inc. and Konsilix in as subsidiaries.

151860.text: KG Eco Solution runs bioenergy, steel, port, and SUV and electric bus manufacturing and sales businesses. Founded in 1999 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013, its main subsidiaries are KG group steel and mobility companies. It brought the mobility company into the group in 2022, merged with a steel holding company in 2024 and has invested in KG STEEL EUROPE B.V.

153460.text: Nable was founded in 2003 to develop and supply wired-wireless converged communication and security solutions, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012. Its businesses are 4G and 5G smart networks, MCPTT core solutions for disaster safety networks, enterprise VoIP and AIoT. The company says it became the first small or mid-sized firm to register as a private 5G network operator in 2022, and it built and tested such a network at a hospital.

153490.text: Wooree E&L Haroutine makes LED packages and health functional foods. Its LED business supplies BLUs for displays, lighting and automotive modules, and its health food business runs nutrition, oriental and diet lines under its own brand. Founded in 2008 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013, it has production bases in China and Vietnam and vertically integrated its health food business by adding a subsidiary in 2025.

153710.text: Optipharm is an animal health company whose businesses include animal disease diagnosis, veterinary drugs, bacteriophage feed additives and laboratory animal supply. Designated a livestock disease diagnostic institution in 2006, it has provided diagnostic services for 20 years, and the company says it is the only one in Korea with drug efficacy testing, animal testing, disease diagnosis and research all in-house. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

153890.text: Justek makes ultra-precision motion systems for semiconductors, displays, industrial automation and space, combining nanometer-level precision with high-speed transfer. Building on linear motor technology it developed in-house, which the company says was a first in Korea, it is vertically integrated from motors, sensors, drivers and controllers to full systems. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2026 as a technology growth company.

154030.text: Asia Seed handles seed research and development, production, processing, distribution and sales, offering 1,147 varieties of 96 vegetable crops such as peppers, radishes, napa cabbages and watermelons, plus 243 other varieties. The company says it holds a unique position in breeding cabbage and broccoli using male sterility, and it exports to 260 companies in 53 countries. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018 as a technology growth company and has 2 unlisted subsidiaries.

154040.text: Dasan Solueta makes and sells electromagnetic shielding materials such as conductive tapes and conductive cushions, supplying global companies including Apple. Founded in 2003, it joined the Dasan group in 2015, and its largest shareholder changed in 2021. After selling an auto parts subsidiary in 2024, it now runs electromagnetic shielding materials as its single business.

155650.text: YMC develops and produces targets and backing plates for display deposition processes and parts for semiconductor and display process equipment, running target and bonding and surface treatment businesses. Founded in 2008 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2012, the company says it was the first in Korea to localize backing plates. It draws on bonding know-how and analysis infrastructure to meet customer needs.

155660.text: DSR makes and sells synthetic fiber ropes, stainless steel wire and carbon steel wire ropes, supplied for fish farming, ship mooring, automobiles, electrical and electronics products and medical device materials. Founded in 1965, it listed on the KOSPI in 2013. From its Korean headquarters it runs a production and sales network with subsidiaries in China, Vietnam and the United States.

156100.text: L&K Biomed makes spinal fixation devices and surgical products used mainly in orthopedics and neurosurgery, including cervical and thoracolumbar cages, screws and plates. It has obtained U.S. FDA certification and supplies U.S. university hospitals, and it has finished developing an implant for correcting chest wall deformities as it expands globally. Founded in 2008, it has 6 unlisted subsidiaries.

158430.text: ATON provides fintech authentication and security solutions and fintech platform services to financial institutions, public agencies, telecom operators and companies. Its main solutions include Quantum SafeGuard and Quantum SafeOTP, and it offers simple authentication, electronic signature and identity verification services centered on the PASS certificate. Founded in 1999 to develop and supply system software, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019.

159010.text: Asflow makes ultra-clean pipes, fittings, valves and other parts for semiconductor process gas supply, selling to Korean chipmakers and to equipment makers such as AMAT and LAM Research. The company says it was the first in Korea to localize high-purity tubes for chip process gas. Founded in 2001 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2021, it is diversifying into corrosion-resistant special alloy materials and precision-machined parts.

159580.text: Zero to Seven makes and sells skincare for babies and children and POE, after starting out in customer relationship management (CRM) services for pregnancy, childbirth and childcare companies. Founded in 2000, it took its current name in 2007 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013. Its two segments are packaging and its infant skincare brand, which it sells in Korea and abroad.

159910.text: EcoGlow runs beauty, merchandise distribution and advertising and marketing divisions, and holds CGMP and ISO 22716 certifications for global markets. Founded in 2006 to develop and sell OLED materials and sublimation purification equipment, it changed its business in 2016 by merging with a cosmetics OEM subsidiary and took its current name in 2025. Its subsidiaries handle financial investment and consulting and cosmetics distribution.

160190.text: Higen RNM runs industrial motor, servo and robot, and mobility businesses, and the company says it holds the third-largest share of Korea's industrial motor market. It began in 2007 by acquiring an elevator company's industrial motor business in Korea, and bought a plant in China in 2010 to build a cost- and technology-competitive production system. It has chosen permanent magnet drive modules for robots and mobility as a core technology.

160550.text: Next Entertainment World is a content media group founded in 2008 mainly to invest in and distribute films. Its 6 unlisted subsidiaries handle TV program production and distribution, global rights distribution, music, a digital platform, cinemas and content production. It has expanded into 7 business segments, including film investment and distribution, drama and music.

160980.text: Cymechs makes semiconductor equipment, chiefly wafer transfer systems such as CTS, EFEM and LPM units. A second business carries out EPC work on energy efficiency, water quality and air pollution control facilities. Founded in 2005, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

161000.text: Aekyung Chemical produces basic chemicals, synthetic resins and household chemicals, including phthalic anhydride, plasticisers, unsaturated polyester resins and surfactants. It says it holds the top share of Korea's phthalic anhydride market and is the exclusive supplier of isocyanate curing agents. Founded in 2012, it absorbed two affiliates in 2021, has 11 subsidiaries and is developing eco-friendly plasticisers and next-generation battery materials.

161390.text: Hankook Tire & Technology makes and sells tyres, along with thermal energy management parts for vehicles and, in a smaller segment, general machinery, moulds and prototypes. It was created in 2012 when its former parent's tyre business was split off. The company says it holds the top share of the Korean tyre market, ranks within the global top 10, and leads the domestic market for vehicle climate-control products.

161580.text: Philoptics develops and makes process equipment for OLED displays, secondary batteries, semiconductors and solar power, building on its optical technology. It was founded in 2008 to make equipment and parts for printed circuit boards and flat panel displays, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. A key subsidiary became a KOSDAQ-listed company in 2023.

161890.text: Kolmar Korea develops and manufactures cosmetics for client brands on an ODM basis. Through subsidiaries it also sells prescription drugs, including infusion solutions, runs a health and beauty business and makes cosmetics containers. It was split off from its former parent in 2012, and in the first half of 2026 it bought a 99.46% stake in another company, making it a consolidated subsidiary.

162300.text: Shin Steel is a steel service centre that cuts and shears colour-coated steel sheet and other steel products to customer specifications. Its main customers are Korean and overseas home appliance makers, and it also trades, distributes and stores steel. Founded in 2008, it has 3 subsidiaries in Korea and runs units in Thailand and Mexico.

163280.text: Airrane develops, makes and sells polymer-based gas separation membranes that separate nitrogen, methane and carbon dioxide at high purity. Its products are used for nitrogen generation, biogas upgrading and carbon capture, and the company says it is the only gas separation solutions specialist in Korea. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024 as a technology growth company.

163560.text: DRB Industrial makes industrial rubber products, including power transmission belts, conveyor belts and rubber tracks for construction and farm machinery. Other businesses supply medical devices, civil engineering and building materials, and seismic isolation and damping systems. It was split off from its predecessor in 2012 and relisted on the KOSPI the same year.

163730.text: Finger builds financial software, running smart finance platforms, data scraping solutions and a mobile app development platform based on fintech and banking know-how. It is expanding into payment services outside the financial sector and researching AI, blockchain and cloud technology. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2021 and has 4 consolidated subsidiaries.

166090.text: Hana Materials makes and sells silicon and silicon carbide electrodes and rings used in the semiconductor etching process. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. It set up a subsidiary in 2023 to provide new technology business financing and in 2024 invested as a limited partner in a related investment fund.

166480.text: Corestemchemon develops, produces and sells stem cell-based cell therapies for rare and intractable diseases. A second division is a non-clinical contract research organisation that tests the toxicity and efficacy of drug candidates, a business it gained by absorbing a CRO in 2022. Founded in 2003, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and is pursuing overseas licensing and second-generation stem cell therapies.

168330.text: Naturalendo Tech develops natural ingredients and sells inner beauty and skincare products under the NEEDIN and NEEDLY brands. Through a subsidiary it also runs a microneedle patch business, and it is working to commercialise microneedle-based transdermal drug delivery and personalised health solutions using AI and big data. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013.

168360.text: Pemtron makes machine vision-based 3D inspection equipment for precision manufacturing, including SMT, semiconductor and FC-BGA PCB inspection systems. Its main products are 3D SPI, 3D AOI, and wafer bump and wire bonding inspection tools, and it exports more than 400 units a year to some 300 companies in about 20 countries. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022 and has units in Hong Kong, the United States, Vietnam and Malaysia.

169330.text: Macromill Embrain runs online and offline market research and a deep data business based on its research panel, which the company says is the largest in Korea. It was founded in 1998, took investment from a listed Japanese company in 2012 and merged with that company's Korean unit, adopting its current name. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020 and has 5 subsidiaries.

170030.text: Hyundai Industrial makes interior seat parts for cars, such as seat pads, armrests and headrests, and sells mainly to Korean carmakers and large parts assemblers. It was founded in 1969, incorporated in 1978 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013. Headquartered in Ulsan, it has production sites in Korea, the United States and China, and set up a US subsidiary in 2021.

170790.text: Piolink develops application networking and web security products, including cloud data centre optimisation products, ADC, security switches, web application firewalls and HCI. It also provides 24-hour information security services and took over a security consulting business in 2018. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013, and it says it launched Korea's first cloud switch in 2015.

170900.text: Dong-a ST makes and sells prescription drugs, including new drugs it developed itself, and has a portfolio that includes biologics. It was created in 2013 through a spin-off from its former parent and belongs to a holding company group. Production takes place at three sites, including one in Daegu, and it invests in research on treatments for metabolic diseases.

170920.text: LTC develops and makes photoresist strippers used in display and semiconductor manufacturing, supplying TFT-process strippers and cleaning solutions to Korean display makers. Through subsidiaries it also supplies wet chemicals for chipmaking and C.C.S.S, and delivers wafer cleaning equipment. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013 and has 8 affiliates.

171010.text: Ram Technology makes chemical materials for semiconductor processes, such as etchants and strippers, and has extended their use to displays and secondary batteries. It develops materials tailored to customers and works with semiconductor and electronics companies around the world. It was founded in 2001 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013.

171090.text: Sunic System makes and sells OLED deposition equipment and semiconductor equipment, and also makes communications electronics and runs an import-export business. Founded in 1990, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. It has 4 consolidated subsidiaries, including a newly established US unit, Sunic System America Corp.

171120.text: Lion Chemtech makes artificial marble for interior and exterior building finishes and synthetic waxes that improve the properties of plastics. Its main products are acrylic and E-Stone artificial marble and waxes made by breaking down PE and PP. It was founded in 1973 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2013.

172670.text: ALT provides back-end services for non-memory chips, testing wafers and packages for system semiconductors such as DDI, CIS, PMIC and MCU. It also offers CIS reconstruct, rim-cut and COG pick-and-place services, and is widening its SoC testing and developing SiC dicing technology. Founded in 2003, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2023.

173130.text: Opasnet provides network and system integration services to large corporations, IT services firms including LG CNS, and government bodies. It is a Cisco Preferred Partner and is expanding into solution-based business and digital healthcare platforms. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018 and became classified as a mid-sized company in 2025.

173940.text: FNC Entertainment plans and produces music, runs music services, concerts, merchandise distribution and artist management, and also produces media content, runs fan clubs and offers education services. It manages singers, including the group SF9, as well as actors. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and has 5 subsidiaries, including units in Japan and the United States.

174900.text: AbClon develops antibody drugs and cell therapies using its NEST, AffiMab and CAR-T platforms. It was founded in 2010 by a group of Korean and Swedish scientists and has built a network with Swedish partners, including Atlas Therapeutics AB, Affibody AB and Alligator Bioscience AB. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017.

175140.text: AGOS makes and sells communication devices such as AI speakers, mobile routers and wearables. It acquired a video content company in 2022 and merged it in 2023 to expand into video content and distribution, and it is preparing an anti-drone solutions business. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

175250.text: Icure Pharmaceutical uses transdermal drug delivery technology to develop and make patch-type medicines, alongside ODM and CDMO work on patches and oral solid drugs. Its cosmetics arm develops and contract-makes skincare items such as hydrogel masks. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018 as a technology growth company and has 6 unlisted subsidiaries.

175330.text: JB Financial Group is a financial holding company that owns two banks, a capital company, an asset manager and an investment firm. It also holds overseas units, including PPCBank in Cambodia and JBSV in Vietnam, as second-tier subsidiaries. Established in 2013, it added its second bank in 2014 and is pursuing further expansion in Southeast Asia and partnerships with fintech firms.

176750.text: DuChemBio develops, makes and sells radiopharmaceuticals for diagnosing cancer and brain diseases. The company says it holds 8 radiopharmaceutical products, the most of any company in Korea, and it runs 12 manufacturing sites, including GMP-certified ones. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024 and sources drug candidates through open innovation, with Asia as its base market.

177350.text: Vessel makes display manufacturing equipment and industrial film materials. Its materials division applies adhesives and functional coatings to PVC, PET and PP films, while its systems division designs in-line systems and high-temperature ovens for LCD and OLED panel makers, focusing mainly on maintaining equipment already delivered. It was founded in 2004 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

177830.text: Pavonine uses precision aluminium machining and anodising to make parts for premium TVs, digital signage, medical devices and cars. Its main customers are a Korean electronics maker and GE. Founded in 1997, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and has set up units in Vietnam, the United States and Mexico to enter the North and Central American market.

177900.text: 3ALogics designs short-range wireless communication chips, producing NFC reader chips and commercialising NFC dynamic tag chips used in smartphones, wearables, payments and ticketing. The company says it was the first in Korea to localise a 13.56MHz RFID reader chip, in 2006. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024 as a technology growth company.

178320.text: Seojin System supplies metal platform products, manufacturing ESS equipment, semiconductor equipment, and parts for electric vehicles and batteries. Its main production base is in Vietnam, and it keeps parts and equipment in-house through vertical integration of its manufacturing. Founded in 2007, it has 28 affiliates, 5 in Korea and 23 overseas.

178780.text: Ilwoul GML distributes seasonal home appliances, mainly electric and hot-water heating mats and electric fans. It started in 2006 as a mould developer and maker and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. After its largest shareholder changed in 2023, it began selling that company's heating mats in Korea and set up a US unit to grow overseas.

178920.text: PI Advanced Materials makes and sells PI film, varnish, and powder and moulded products. It was formed in 2008 when two Korean companies combined their PI film divisions, and the company says it is Korea's only PI film maker. It listed on the KOSPI in 2021, and its largest shareholder changed in 2023.

179290.text: Mitech makes non-vascular stents, mainly for the digestive tract, and has about 3,000 designs, of which more than 300 products are commercialised and exported. The company says it was the first in Korea to develop non-vascular stents, and it is extending their use from malignant tumours to benign conditions. Founded in 1991, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

179530.text: Adbiotech develops immune antibody products for livestock, aquaculture and people that can replace vaccines and antibiotics. Its VHH technology was selected in 2021 as one of 10 next-generation bio technologies, and it is researching antibodies against PRRS in pigs, EMS and WSSV in shrimp, and AI. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ as a technology growth company and has 3 unlisted subsidiaries.

179900.text: Uti makes camera modules and tempered glass that protects touch panels in smartphones, tablets and laptops, with camera window cover glass for smartphones as its main product. It runs two production units in Vietnam, UTI VINA Co.,Ltd and UTI VINA VINH PHUC Co.,Ltd. Founded in 2010 to make touch panel parts, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017.

180400.text: Dx&Vx is a bio healthcare company that works with its subsidiaries on research, production and distribution. Its drug development arm is pursuing KRNA, an oral GLP-1RA obesity treatment and immuno-oncology drugs, while its diagnostics arm offers genetic testing and in vitro diagnostic services. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

180640.text: Hanjin KAL is a holding company whose main subsidiaries are an airline with 165 aircraft, which also runs an aerospace business, and a logistics firm handling parcel delivery, global logistics and energy. Other subsidiaries run hotels and manage buildings. It was split off from the airline in 2013 and listed on the KOSPI the same year.

181710.text: NHN runs online and mobile games, PG and VAN payment services, the PAYCO simple payment service, cloud technology, ticketing, e-commerce and webtoons. It was created in 2013 by splitting off its predecessor's game business and listed on the KOSPI. It has 58 consolidated subsidiaries and operates overseas through units in Japan such as NHN PlayArt and NHN Techorus.

182360.text: Cube Entertainment is an entertainment company that plans and produces its artists' albums and handles promotion, concerts, management and merchandise sales. It develops new artists and earns royalties from merchandise based on its intellectual property and from collaborations with outside companies, and it also exclusively imports and distributes a Thai juice brand. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

182400.text: NKGen Biotech Korea develops NK cell-based immune cell therapies on its SuperNK platform, with a pipeline that includes SNK01, SNK02 and SNK03. It was founded in 2002 to make and develop research reagents and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. A 2019 merger was followed by court-led rehabilitation proceedings, which ended in 2025.

183190.text: Asia Cement makes and sells cement, ready-mixed concrete and dry mortar. Its subsidiaries are also in the cement business, and others work in venture capital and theme park operation. The company was established in 2013 and develops products through partnerships with universities and research institutes.

183300.text: KoMiCo cleans and coats parts for semiconductor process equipment and makes ceramic components, serving customers such as Samsung, Intel and TSMC in 8 countries. It was created in 2013 by splitting off its former parent's cleaning and coating business. Its ceramics subsidiary was set up in 2020 through a similar split, and it has units in the Czech Republic and Ireland to serve Europe.

183490.text: Enzychem Lifesciences develops new drugs globally based on its compound EC-18, and also sells active pharmaceutical ingredients and health supplements. Through subsidiaries it supplies bioenergy feedstock for HVO and SAF, works on graphene and secondary batteries, and runs global clinical trials through ENZYCHEM LIFESCIENCES USA. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

184230.text: SGA Solutions provides information security solutions. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company. It bought a system access control specialist in 2022 and absorbed two affiliates in 2026 to strengthen its business.

185490.text: EyeGene is a biotech company that develops mRNA vaccines, including an mRNA cancer vaccine, and AAV gene therapies while also running revenue-generating businesses. It started out in proteomics and immunology research and invests in promising start-ups to secure key technologies. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and has an Australian unit, EyeGene Australia.

185750.text: Chong Kun Dang Pharmaceutical makes prescription and over-the-counter drugs, including a Korean-developed anticancer drug, a diabetes treatment and biosimilars. It was created in 2013 when its holding company's pharmaceutical business was split off, and the business has more than 80 years of history. It is increasing research spending on new drugs, improved drugs and biologics, and expanding into overseas markets such as Vietnam and Indonesia.

186230.text: Green Plus has an aluminium division that extrudes and processes aluminium into materials for electronics, vehicles, aviation and defence, and a smart farm division. It was founded in 1997 to make aluminium products and greenhouse materials, and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019. It has 4 subsidiaries, including Green Plus KT and Green Plus AUS, and 1 associate.

187220.text: Dt&C tests and certifies products for electromagnetic compatibility, electrical safety, specific absorption rate and telecommunications standards. It was founded in 2000 for electromagnetic testing and certification and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014. Its subsidiaries include DCJ, Dt&C Vina and Dt&C China.

187270.text: Shin Hwa Contech makes connectors used in telecommunications equipment, home appliances, automotive electronics, defence and medical devices. It has taken part in developing a digital microphone for a Korean carmaker's infotainment platform and produces in Vietnam. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and has 6 unlisted subsidiaries.

187420.text: HLB Genex develops and makes custom enzymes and bio healthcare materials, including industrial specialty enzymes and microbiome-enzyme products, using microbial display and recombinant protein secretion technology. It was founded in 2000 as a spin-off from a Korean biotech research institute and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 under a special listing track. A subsidiary develops treatments for brain and nervous system diseases.

187660.text: Penetrium Bioscience develops cancer treatments centred on its Penetrium technology and also works as a CRO, providing clinical trial design, operation, data management and pharmacovigilance services. Founded in 2003, it was acquired in 2024 by another biotech company and gained exclusive rights to a drug delivery technology. It is pursuing clinical development of its own pipeline and building an AI-based analysis system.

187790.text: NANO makes SCR catalysts that reduce nitrogen oxides, and the company says it is the only firm in the world with its own technology for SCR catalyst raw materials, catalysts, testing and regeneration. It was founded in 1999 on technology for making titanium dioxide for nanoparticle catalysts and merged with a special purpose acquisition company in 2015. In 2025 it completed a new automated plant for high-density catalysts.

187870.text: Device supplies contamination control equipment used in cleaning processes, mainly FM MASK cleaning and optical inspection systems for OLED displays and FOUP cleaning systems for semiconductors. It is also expanding into materials and parts for chip and display production. Founded in 2002 to make semiconductor and display equipment, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017.

188040.text: Bio Port Korea makes and sells snacks, liquid teas and other beverages, supplying major retailers. It runs three of its own plants in and around Busan, making ODM and private-label products for retailers as well as brand collaboration products. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025 by merging with a special purpose acquisition company.

188260.text: Sanigen provides food safety products, including PCR and NGS-based diagnostic kits, microbial genome analysis services, sanitising products and the ForLabs brand. The company says its PCR kits reach close to 100% sensitivity and specificity and that it developed the world's first NGS panel product. Founded in 2005, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2023 through a SPAC merger and is expanding into cosmetics and microbiome markets.

189300.text: Intellian Technologies develops, makes and sells satellite communication antennas for moving platforms, and has more than 600 networks in about 60 countries. Its range covers LEO and MEO antennas, gateways, and aviation and defence antennas, and it says it holds the top position in the GEO VSAT antenna market. Founded in 2004, it works with OneWeb, SES and Telesat on LEO services and electronic flat-panel antennas.

189330.text: XIIlab is an AI company that runs 5 solutions across 3 divisions: AI Infra, Vision AI and Digital Twin. Its AI Infra business offers GPU orchestration software and works with global partners, while its Vision AI and Digital Twin products are used across a range of industries. It was founded in 2010 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2021.

189690.text: Forcs develops and supplies electronic document software, including an e-form development tool, an enterprise reporting tool and a cloud AI-based e-signature service. It was founded in 2008 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. It has 4 affiliates, including FORCS Japan and companies in food service, electronics retail and used-car trading.

189860.text: Seojeon Electric Machinery makes power distribution equipment that carries electricity to consumers, including high- and low-voltage switchgear, motor control centres, distribution panels and GIS. It was founded in 1988 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014. It set up a research lab in 2009, has earned NEP certification, and is launching seismic-resistant and smart switchgear and a 170kV GIS.

189980.text: Hyungkuk F&B makes fruit and vegetable drinks such as fruit concentrates, smoothies and fresh-pressed juices, working as an ODM supplier for cafes. It sells through coffee and restaurant franchises, wholesalers and online channels. Founded in 2008, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and has 5 consolidated subsidiaries.

190510.text: Namuga makes camera modules for smartphones and tablets, along with 3D depth-sensing modules, through a subsidiary in Vietnam. Camera modules make up about 99% of sales, and a Korean electronics maker is its main customer. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and is developing OIS modules and technology for cars and XR devices.

190650.text: Korea Asset Investment Securities is a securities firm offering brokerage, proprietary trading, bond underwriting, financial advisory and fund management. Proprietary trading is its core business, accounting for about 85% of operating revenue. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019, and its affiliates include its largest shareholder and an investment company.

191410.text: Ryuk-il C&S makes PVC stabilisers and ultraviolet absorbers in its fine chemicals business, which serves many products and customers in small volumes, and also runs an edtech business. It shifted its focus from tempered glass after selling its Vietnam production unit in 2025. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and has 2 subsidiaries in Korea.

191420.text: Tego Science develops and produces cell therapies using cell culture technology. The company says it holds 3 of the 16 cell therapy products approved in Korea. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and made another company a subsidiary in 2025 by acquiring a stake.

192080.text: DoubleUGames develops and runs online games. Through its main subsidiary it offers social casino games and casual games on web and mobile, and it runs an iGaming business centred on SuprNation AB, acquired in 2023. Founded in 2012, it completed the acquisition of Paxie Games and WHOW Games in 2025 to strengthen its casual and social casino lines.

192250.text: Ksign supplies information security products for database security, encryption and authentication, access control and account management, and system security to financial institutions, public bodies and companies. It earns revenue from installation, licences and maintenance, and researches AI-based threat detection and XAI. Founded in 1999, it is listed on the KOSDAQ and has two subsidiaries.

192390.text: Winhitech makes, installs and sells steel structures, mainly deck plates, metal assemblies that replace plywood formwork when building floor slabs. Its range includes integrated, removable, long-span, non-dismantling and insulated deck products. It was split off from another company in 2011, listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and has 6 consolidated subsidiaries.

192400.text: Cuckoo Holdings is a holding company that earns brand royalties, management advisory fees and dividends from its subsidiaries. Its main subsidiary makes kitchen and household appliances, chiefly electric rice cookers, along with IH and hot-plate pressure cookers, induction ranges and multicookers. Founded in 1978, it became a holding company in 2017 after creating two companies through a spin-off and a split.

192410.text: Oneul E&M has an antenna division that makes and sells base station antennas and a robot division that makes indoor autonomous mobile robots and smart actuators. Founded in 1997 for electronics and telecoms manufacturing and services, it changed its name in 2025. It has 4 game-related subsidiaries, including units in the United States and China and One Crane Holdings Limited, set up in 2025.

192440.text: Spigen Korea sells smartphone cases, screen protectors and other mobile accessories under the Spigen brand, mainly through a major online marketplace. It started in North America and now sells in more than 52 countries, including in Europe, India and Japan, and is adding foldable cases and wearable accessories based on its own patents. Founded in 2009, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and has 6 unlisted subsidiaries.

192650.text: Dreamtech is an EMS and ODM company whose main production is in Vietnam. Its businesses include IMC, which supplies PBA modules for IT devices, BHC, which supplies biometric modules and convergence products, and CCM, which supplies camera modules. Founded in 1998, it runs an R&D organisation and holds intellectual property for fingerprint sensor modules and ECG measurement patches.

192820.text: Cosmax develops and makes cosmetics for other brands, with ODM supply making up more than 90% of sales. It covers skincare, colour cosmetics and sheet masks for about 4,000 brand companies in Korea and abroad, with factories in China, the United States, Indonesia and Thailand. It was split off from its former parent in 2014, is listed on the KOSPI and has 34 subsidiaries.

193250.text: Linked makes vibration motors for smartphones, e-cigarettes and beauty devices, and electric motors for car parts, at its headquarters and overseas plants. Its main customers are Korea's largest smartphone maker and global auto parts suppliers. Founded in 2004, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and is also pursuing homewear distribution using character licences, AX/DX projects, and expansion into cars, appliances and robotics.

194370.text: JS makes handbags and clothing, supplying handbags on an ODM basis to global brands such as MICHAEL KORS and Guess, and also runs a hotel through a subsidiary. Its clothing is produced in Indonesia, Vietnam and Cambodia. Founded in 1987, it acquired a company in 2024 that gave it production units in the United States, Mexico and Indonesia.

194480.text: Devsisters develops and runs mobile games built on its own game franchise, and is expanding the franchise's intellectual property business and moving onto PC and console platforms. It also runs a venture capital business through a subsidiary. It was founded in 2007 to develop software and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

194700.text: Novarex develops and makes health supplements for other brands on an ODM and OEM basis, handling everything from product planning to shipment, with omega-3 products among its main sellers. The company says it holds 49 individually approved functional ingredients, the most in Korea. Founded in 2008, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018, runs a smart factory and cGMP-certified facilities, and is growing exports to China and Asia.

195500.text: Maniker F&G processes chicken, pork and beef into 7 product groups, including fried items, patties and grilled products. It sells to restaurant franchises and to consumers through large supermarkets and convenience stores. Founded in 2004, it acquired a plant in 2008 with investment from Maniker, and it says it began Korea's first exports of chicken soup to the United States in 2014.

195870.text: Haesung DS makes substrates for semiconductor packaging, including lead frames and package substrates. Its lead frame customers include IDMs such as Infineon and ST Micro and OSATs such as ASE and Amkor, while two Korean chipmakers are its main package substrate customers. Founded in 2014 and listed in 2016, it says it leads the global market in PPF plating and is developing automotive lead frames and graphene.

195940.text: HK inno.N runs a prescription drug business and a health and beauty business, making and distributing a range of medicines led by a Korean-developed new drug. Its research pipeline covers cancer, digestive disease, diabetes and autoimmune disease, with a focus on finding its next major drug. It was created in 2014 by splitting off another company's pharmaceutical division and was acquired by a cosmetics maker in 2018.

195990.text: RootK makes metal-cutting machines, specialising in small machining centres used to produce IT and car parts. It was founded in Daegu in 2004 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. In 2019 it signed an agreement with Abpro Holdings of the United States to develop bispecific antibody drugs in Asia, and in 2023 it entered the battery and chip equipment business by acquiring a subsidiary.

196170.text: Alteogen develops and sells biopharmaceuticals based on platform technologies: Hybrozyme, which turns intravenous drugs into subcutaneous injections, NexP fusion for long-acting biologics, and NexMab for next-generation antibody-drug conjugates. It has licensing deals with global drugmakers such as MSD, AstraZeneca, Sanofi and GSK, earning upfront payments, milestones and royalties. Founded in 2008, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

196300.text: HLB Pep develops peptide biomaterials and drug candidates, with most sales coming from peptide materials for medicines and research. It makes drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredients and quasi-drugs, and offers CDMO services from ingredients to finished drugs at two GMP plants. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016 as a technology growth company.

196450.text: CoAsia CM makes smartphone camera lenses and modules, using mass production technology for aspheric optical lenses and handling design, parts and modules in-house. It was split off from another company in 2014 and in 2021 brought CoAsia CM KR and a Vietnam unit under one structure to focus on camera modules. Using its Vietnam production base, it is expanding into robotics, automotive electronics and 3D cameras.

196490.text: DA Technology makes automation equipment for secondary battery production, covering the assembly and formation stages. Besides individual machines it offers turnkey solutions, and it has supplied large Korean and overseas battery makers for more than 20 years. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and has unlisted subsidiaries.

196700.text: WAPS develops and makes polymer materials, including functional materials for golf balls and lithium-ion battery separators, artificial leather and other car interior materials, and exterior building materials such as synthetic wood and aluminium composites. It was founded in Busan in 2001 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. Its head office and research centre are in Busan, with two plants in Korea and a production unit in Vietnam.

197140.text: DigiCAP develops software for video security, video AI, metaverse, digital twin and content, along with digital broadcasting solutions. It is widening its customer base beyond broadcasting and media to games, film, OTT, and architecture and design. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018 and absorbed a subsidiary in 2024.

198080.text: CAP has two businesses: an SMT division that uses surface-mount technology to produce FPCA for smartphone OLED panels, and a division that makes wiper blades for cars. It was founded in 2010 to make electronic products and parts and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020. It has 10 affiliates, with units in China, Vietnam, the United States and Japan.

198440.text: Kangdong C&L makes and sells cement and also runs a leisure business. The company says it is the only Portland cement producer in Korea's southwestern region, which is its main market, and its location near major sources of demand keeps logistics costs low. It was founded in 2014 and listed on the KOSDAQ the same year.

198940.text: Hanjoo Light Metal makes aluminium parts for vehicles, including EV and lightweight components and engine parts, which make up more than 90% of sales. It uses electromagnetic stirring casting and rheocasting technology to develop parts for eco-friendly cars and robot body housings. Founded in 1987, it set up a subsidiary in Slovakia in 2022 and went public in 2023.

199430.text: KNR Systems builds hydraulic and electric precision control systems, running test equipment, robot, and test and evaluation service businesses. It serves the car, rail and energy industries as well as aerospace, nuclear and defence, and says it has led the replacement of imported test equipment in Korea with domestic products. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024 as a technology growth company.

199480.text: Bankware Global makes software for banks and other financial companies, selling financial and platform software licences and providing maintenance, SaaS services and core system consulting. It supplies about 100 financial institutions in 7 Asian countries and is starting AI and blockchain businesses. Founded in 2010, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024 as a technology growth company.

199550.text: Laseroptek develops and makes laser-based medical devices for skin aesthetics and treating skin conditions, after starting with lasers for chip and car manufacturing. The company says its LOTUS and HELIOS devices, launched in 2005, were the first made with Korean technology, and that PALLAS, developed in 2016, was the world's first titanium sapphire-based UVB laser, used for vitiligo. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024.

199730.text: BioInfra is a contract research organisation that runs bioequivalence studies for generic drugs, early clinical trials for improved drugs, and Phase I to III trials for new drug approvals. It also carries out pharmacokinetic and toxicokinetic studies for biologics, biomarker analysis, quality testing of finished drugs, comparative dissolution tests and long-term stability tests. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2023.

199800.text: ToolGen develops gene editing products and services, having built ZFN and TALEN tools before developing CRISPR/Cas9 in 2012. The company says it is the only firm in the world to have developed all three types of gene scissors itself, and the first to show CRISPR working inside eukaryotic cells. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KONEX in 2014 and moved to the KOSDAQ in 2021.

199820.text: Cheil Electric makes wiring devices and distribution panels, including IoT-based smart home wiring devices. It has done business with one partner since 1988, and it says it holds the highest market share in smart home network distribution equipment. Founded in 1980, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020 and has two subsidiaries, including JABEZ VINA.

200130.text: KolmarBNH develops health supplement and cosmetic ingredients, producing products from natural materials for immune, gut health and blood sugar support on an ODM and OEM basis. It works with immune function technology, high-purity green tea refining and herbal fermentation, and a subsidiary grows herbal raw materials. It was founded in 2004 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

200230.text: Telcon RF Pharmaceutical makes connectors and cables for wireless communications equipment and, in a separate pharmaceutical and bio division, produces and sells drugs while investing in new drug development. Its RF business offers 5G FTTA solutions and is expanding into Southeast Asia. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 and gained control of another company in 2026, adding several subsidiaries.

200350.text: Artist Studio plans and produces story-based dramas, entertainment shows and performances for broadcasters, media platforms and overseas markets. It also earns revenue from its content through NFTs, publishing, soundtracks and character goods, and develops content for channels such as Netflix, Disney+ and tving. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2021.

200470.text: Apact provides chip packaging and testing services to customers ranging from large IDMs to small and mid-sized fabless firms. It was founded in 2007 with joint investment from a group of chip industry suppliers and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014. It took over another company's packaging business in 2022 to offer a turnkey service and bought a stake in a materials and parts company in 2025.

200670.text: Humedix researches hyaluronic acid and PDRN and uses them to make fillers, arthritis treatments, eye drops and other medicines and medical devices for Korean and global markets. It was founded in 2003 to make functional foods and took its current name in 2010. It has 10 affiliates in Korea and 3 overseas.

200710.text: ADTechnology is a chip design house that designs and sells ASICs and provides mass production and development services to fabless and IT device companies. It started as a value chain partner of TSMC, became an official design partner of a Korean foundry in 2020, and was chosen as an Arm Total Design partner in 2023. Founded in 2002, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

200780.text: BC World Pharm makes and sells prescription drugs, including anaesthetic and pain medicines and antibiotics, at facilities built to EU GMP and cGMP levels under PIC/s rules. It is researching new and improved drugs. Founded in 1980, it adopted its current name in 2007 and has two subsidiaries.

200880.text: Seoyon E-hwa makes interior and exterior car parts, such as door trims, consoles, headliners and bumpers, as well as seats for commercial vehicles. Two Korean carmakers account for about 44% and 38% of sales, and it also supplies global carmakers. It was created in 2014 through a spin-off from its former parent and is a listed mid-sized company.

201490.text: Me2on was founded in 2010 to develop and run online and mobile games and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016. It acquired ACE Interactive Holdings Limited in 2012 to expand overseas and bought a game studio in 2017 to strengthen its presence in North America and Europe. Through its main subsidiaries it has made further acquisitions to diversify its business.

203400.text: Abion develops cancer drugs based on companion diagnostics. Its pipeline includes a targeted treatment for non-small cell lung cancer, the claudin-3 antibody platform ABN501, the antibody-cytokine fusion protein platform ABN202, and ABN101, an interferon-beta antiviral treatment. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2021 through the special listing track for technology growth companies.

203450.text: Union biometrics makes biometric access control and time-and-attendance systems that recognise fingerprints, faces, irises and veins, along with fingerprint modules, enrolment readers and card-based access controllers. All production is outsourced, and it holds 216 intellectual property rights, including patents and trademarks. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016 and has subsidiaries in Vietnam and the Middle East.

203650.text: Dream Security provides PKI-based encryption and authentication solutions for the public, financial, mobile telecoms and private sectors, with businesses in IT security, defence and rentals. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company. It has 15 consolidated subsidiaries.

204020.text: Gritee sells underwear and athleisure wear, including imported brands, licensed brands and its own brands. Through a subsidiary, it sources products made under contract at factories in Vietnam, Indonesia and China. It was founded in 1999 to make and sell underwear and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018.

204270.text: Jntc makes advanced materials and precision parts, including glass for mobile devices and cars and TGV glass substrates for semiconductors. It produces through its Vietnam unit, JNTC VINA, and is adding lines at a TGV glass substrate plant and its fourth Vietnam plant to serve the AI industry. Founded in 1996, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020.

204320.text: HL Mando develops and makes chassis parts, including braking, steering and suspension systems, at 19 production sites supported by 18 research centres. It is shifting toward electronically controlled chassis products and future mobility, building on an affiliate's ADAS technology. It was created in 2014 by splitting off the auto parts business of its holding company and has 27 consolidated subsidiaries.

204610.text: T3 Entertainment develops games and runs a game service business that operates titles globally, along with a solutions business that develops digital twin software. It was founded in 2000 to develop game software and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022. It has five subsidiaries and set up two new investment funds during the year.

204620.text: Global Tax Free handles domestic tax refunds for foreign tourists who buy goods at tax-refund shops, a system introduced by the government to attract more visitors. The company says it was the first tax refund agent in Asia. Founded in 2005, it merged with a special purpose acquisition company in 2017 and has 3 consolidated subsidiaries.

204840.text: GL Pharm Tech researches and develops drugs, focusing on improved versions of existing drugs that use DDS technology to raise their effect, and also handles sales and marketing. Its consolidated subsidiary makes and sells prescription and over-the-counter medicines and has hormone drug production facilities. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014 as a technology growth company.

205100.text: Exem provides IT performance management software, including database performance management and hybrid cloud IT monitoring. It also develops MLOps, big data and LLM-based AI platforms to help companies and public bodies adopt AI. Founded in 2001 to make database tuning software, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and has subsidiaries in the United States, Japan and China.

205470.text: Humasis researches and produces POCT immunoassay reagents for in vitro diagnostics. Through a main subsidiary it also runs rubber products, drama production and artist management businesses, and it merged a studio in 2026. It was founded in 2000 to make diagnostic devices and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 after a merger.

205500.text: Nexus develops and supplies game software and runs blockchain and AI-based global platforms, earning revenue from development work for overseas blockchain foundations and from platform and game content services. Founded in 2012, it merged with a special purpose acquisition company in 2015 and took its current name in 2025. In 2026 it acquired an 89.03% stake in another company, which became a main subsidiary.

206400.text: Beno TNR develops, designs and installs shading systems, eco-friendly raised floors and radiant heating and cooling systems for interiors, and also has wearable robot and duct manufacturing businesses. As the Korean agent of a German company, it supplies and installs access floors and other eco-friendly materials. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company.

206560.text: Dexter studios is a visual effects company that has brought content planning, production, sound and post-production under one group. It works on VFX and DI for films and dramas, immersive content and AI-based digital marketing. Founded in 2011, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and has 7 subsidiaries covering content production, sound, AI digital advertising and immersive media art.

206640.text: Boditech Med makes and sells in vitro diagnostic devices and test cartridges for point-of-care testing. Using lateral flow immunofluorescence technology, it offers more than 120 tests covering infections, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, cancer and hormones, organised into cartridge and instrument divisions. Founded in 1998, it runs production units in the United States and China and sells in about 130 countries.

206650.text: EuBiologics makes vaccines and researches and produces biopharmaceuticals, supplying oral cholera vaccine to international buyers including WHO and offering CRMO services. It is developing bacterial vaccines against typhoid and meningococcal disease and working on viral vaccines using adjuvants and its SNAP technology. Founded in 2010, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 and runs two plants and a research lab in Korea.

207760.text: Mr. Blue is an online content company offering digital comics, webtoons, web novels and games. It sells content to readers through its own Mr. Blue platform, supplies content to portals and other platforms, and runs PC and mobile games through a subsidiary set up in 2018. It listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015 and absorbed a web novel company in 2025.

207940.text: Samsung Biologics is a contract development and manufacturing organisation that provides CMO and CDO services to global pharmaceutical and biotech companies, with production capacity in Incheon and the United States. Founded in 2011, it listed on the KOSPI in 2016. It spun off a subsidiary in 2025 to focus purely on CDMO work and acquired a GSK subsidiary in 2026 to gain a US production base.

208140.text: Jungdawn is a duck meat company with fresh meat, processed meat, home meal replacement and down feather businesses. A subsidiary supplies more than 95% of its meat ducks, and it runs slaughtering, fresh meat, smoked meat, feather and HMR facilities in several regions of Korea. Founded in 2000, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2014.

208350.text: Jiran Security makes security software for email, documents and mobile devices, and the company says its products rank first in each of these fields. It was spun off from another software company's security division in 2014 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016. It bought an information security consulting firm in 2017, which absorbed another security company in 2026.

208370.text: Selvas Healthcare has two divisions: ACCUNIQ, which makes body composition analysers and automatic blood pressure monitors, and HIMS, which makes braille notetakers and reading magnifiers for visually impaired people. It was founded in 1999 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016. Its wholly owned subsidiaries HIMS, Inc. in the United States and Beijing SELVAS Healthcare in China serve overseas markets.

208640.text: Thumbage develops and runs games in genres such as MMORPG and RPG, serving them on mobile platforms. It currently operates three titles, and through a subsidiary studio it develops new games and updates existing ones. It was founded in 2013 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016.

208710.text: Photon makes parts for smartphone camera modules, including AF/OIS FPCB assemblies and F/Z FPCB assemblies used in camera actuators. It supplies them to first-tier vendors of a large Korean company. AF moves the lens to focus automatically, while OIS helps capture sharp images in low light. It was founded in 2012 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

208860.text: Dasan DMC supplies car parts such as suspension, powertrain and steering systems and weather strips, and also offers connected car solutions, an EV charging platform and an AI-equipped taxi mobility service. It is expanding from combustion engine parts into parts for electric and hydrogen vehicles. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016 and produces in China, Mexico, Uzbekistan and Brazil.

209640.text: Yjlink makes smart process equipment for SMT lines, including PCB conveyors, SMT back-end equipment and Smart Factory Solution products, and supplies equipment to Tesla, SpaceX and Apple. It is using Hermes Standard and digital twin technology to automate SMT lines and has production units in Mexico and India. Founded in 2009, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2024.

210120.text: Canvas N produces TV dramas, finding writers, casting actors and supplying finished shows to broadcasters or distribution platforms. It was founded in 2003, listed on the KONEX in 2014 and moved to the KOSDAQ in 2023. It changed its name in 2024 to broaden its business and raise its global profile.

210540.text: DY Power makes and sells hydraulic cylinders and other hydraulic and pneumatic equipment for construction machinery. Its customers include Korean and overseas construction equipment makers such as Caterpillar and HITACHI. It was split off from its former parent's hydraulics division in 2014, listed on the KOSPI in 2015, and has 2 overseas subsidiaries in China and India.

210980.text: SK D&D is a real estate developer and SK Group affiliate that develops and operates offices, housing, knowledge industry centres, hotels, retail facilities and logistics centres. Founded in 2004 for property development, it listed on the KOSPI in 2015. It split off its energy business into a new company in 2024, and a subsidiary absorbed another company in 2025.

211050.text: Incar Financial Service is an independent insurance agency founded in 2007 that listed on the KOSDAQ in 2022. It has 3 consolidated subsidiaries, which support remote sales through a financial platform, provide financial consulting, and broker loans under a contract with a Korean bank. It bought all of another company's shares and then absorbed it.

211270.text: Asia Pacific Satellite lnc develops and makes satellite communication terminals, including satellite phones, M2M terminals and broadband terminals, and also works on satellites and satellite parts. Its main customer is THURAYA of the United Arab Emirates, and it supplies terminals for mobile satellite services across Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Asia. Founded in 2011, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016.

212560.text: Neooto makes key transmission parts, including pinion gears and differential assemblies, as well as reduction gears for electric vehicles, selling mainly to Korean automotive companies. It has applied for a patent on a 2-speed EV transmission. It was created in 2010 through a split from its former parent and has affiliates in Korea and subsidiaries in Vietnam, the Czech Republic and India.

212710.text: ISTE makes semiconductor equipment, mainly FOUP cleaners along with sorters and EFEM units, for Korean and global chipmakers, and also runs a hydrogen energy business. It began by supplying vacuum transfer equipment for OLED, LCD and car production, and grew into a chip equipment maker after becoming a registered partner of a Korean chipmaker in 2016. Founded in 2013, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2025 as a technology growth company.

213420.text: Duk San Neolux develops and produces organic light-emitting materials for OLED displays, such as HTL, Red Host, R Prime and G Prime, as well as the non-emitting material Black PDL and conductive particles. It was split off from its former parent's chemical materials business in 2014 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. In 2025 it bought a 59.69% stake in a turbomachinery company spun off from another company.

213500.text: Hansol Paper makes and sells industrial, printing and specialty paper, exporting to North America and Europe through overseas sales units, and makes paper containers through a subsidiary. It was founded in 1965, left a large business group in 1993 and was re-established in 2015 through a split from its holding company. The company says it is Korea's largest paper maker, and it added plant construction and engineering after absorbing an affiliate in 2022.

214150.text: Classys makes aesthetic medical devices, including focused ultrasound systems, monopolar RF and microneedle RF devices, and lasers, sold in about 80 countries. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 through a SPAC merger. In 2024 it absorbed another device maker, set up a Japanese subsidiary and acquired units in Brazil, Colombia and Argentina to sell directly.

214180.text: Hecto Innovation provides secondary identity verification and security services focused on protecting personal data, and runs fintech and healthcare businesses through subsidiaries. It is developing a digital wallet business and partnering with global stablecoin issuers to build infrastructure for digital assets. It was founded in 2009 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

214260.text: Raphas researches, makes and sells dissolving microneedle patches based on its DEN technology, with most revenue from cosmetics and expansion into drug and vaccine patches. It has Korean regulatory approval for microneedle patches as functional cosmetics and is running clinical trials of a GLP-1 obesity patch. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2019 and has 12 unlisted subsidiaries.

214270.text: FSN is a digital marketing company offering planning, production, media operation and data analysis, with subsidiaries that broaden its marketing work. It also runs D2C commerce and healthcare platforms and grows with partners through revenue-sharing and equity investment models. Founded in 2007, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

214320.text: Innocean Worldwide is an integrated marketing communications company with a global network, providing strategy, ad production, media buying and digital marketing. It was founded in 2005 as the advertising agency of a carmaking group. It has pursued acquisitions of David & Goliath and Wellcom Group and is developing an AI-based GEO solution while building bases in growth markets.

214330.text: Kumho HT makes lighting parts for cars, such as LED modules and incandescent bulbs, and has subsidiaries in China, India and Vietnam. A biopharmaceutical division develops antibody-based treatments and diagnostics for technology licensing. It was founded in 1988 as a joint venture of two Korean firms and a Japanese lighting company, and listed on the KOSPI in 2015.

214370.text: Caregen develops and makes professional therapy products, functional cosmetics, health supplements and bio ingredients based on biomimetic peptides and growth factor proteins, supplying about 130 countries. It handles everything from peptide discovery to synthesis, formulation and mass production, and has a large peptide library that includes about 860 registered patents. Founded in 2001, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015.

214390.text: Kyongbo Pharmaceutical exports cephalosporin antibiotic and anticancer APIs to 16 countries and sells finished drugs such as cardiovascular medicines and inhaled anaesthetics. It has developed its own ADC conjugation and payload-linker technology and is building a dedicated ADC plant. It was founded in 1987 to make active ingredients, added finished drugs in 2002 and listed on the KOSPI in 2015.

214420.text: Tonymoly sells cosmetics mainly through its Tonymoly brand and a clean beauty brand, under the brand identity 'Be Uncommon'. It has 8 unlisted consolidated companies, including a cosmetics OEM and ODM maker, and bought a pet treat company in 2021. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSPI in 2015.

214430.text: i3system makes image sensors that turn electromagnetic energy, from X-ray to infrared bands, into visible images, along with related products such as infrared image sensors, X-ray image sensors and infrared simulators. Founded in 1998 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015, it says it is Korea's only supplier of military infrared image sensors, and it is expanding into civilian markets and space satellite work.

214450.text: PharmaResearch researches and sells medical devices, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals centred on PDRN and PN, based on regenerative medicine technology. Founded in 2001 as a drug and medical device development consultancy, it opened a GMP-certified plant in 2013 and completed a second plant in 2019. It runs a botulinum toxin business through a major subsidiary.

214610.text: RollingStone is an in vitro diagnostics company working across molecular, immunoassay and biochemical diagnostics, with PCR instruments, analysers, reagents and test strips. It has about 90 self-developed products for diagnosing diseases and viruses. Founded in 2009, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020 as a technology growth company.

214680.text: Drtech makes digital diagnostic imaging products, from X-ray systems to detectors and components, for human, veterinary, mammography and industrial use, and overseas sales make up about 80% of revenue. Founded in 2000 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016, it has 7 unlisted subsidiaries and says it is the only company in the world holding both direct and indirect detector technologies.

215000.text: Golfzon runs a screen golf simulator business and provides customer support such as after-sales service and store operation support. It was established in 2015 when the screen golf business was split off from its former holding company, and the group has 4 domestic and 13 overseas entities. It started a screen golf franchise business in 2017 and has run a GDR golf academy since 2018.

215090.text: SolDefense develops and produces components for guided weapons and avionics control units and supplies them to the military, while in the civilian sector it makes parts such as integrated monitoring and control systems for power plants. Founded in 1999, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018 and took its current name in 2025. More than 20% of its staff are specialist engineers.

215100.text: RoboRobo makes educational robots and a GUI programming tool called ROGIC. It was founded in 2000 as a developer of cleaning and security robots, moved into educational robots in 2005 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. Its subsidiaries provide contracted after-school education services and run coding academies.

215200.text: MegaStudyEdu is an education company formed in 2015 through a spin-off from its former parent, and it has 9 subsidiaries. Its divisions for younger students, high school, university and job seekers offer online and offline lectures and sell books under age-specific brands. It is expanding AI-based learning analysis, personalised study management, a subscription pass and a generative AI study assistant.

215360.text: Woory Industrial makes vehicle HVAC systems and electrical parts, with customers including domestic auto parts makers and, overseas, DENSO and MAHLE. It was formed in 2015 when the auto parts business of its holding company was split off. Since 2022 it has been registered as a tier-1 supplier to domestic carmakers, selling PTC and coolant heaters directly, and it is developing parts for eco-friendly vehicles.

215380.text: Kolmar BioTech runs a bio business and an infection control business, with the bio side offering efficacy and safety evaluation, analytical testing and vivarium operations through a bio cluster. Founded in 1989 for new drug research, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. It adopted its current name at a 2026 extraordinary shareholders' meeting and has resolved to absorb a newly acquired materials subsidiary.

215480.text: Toebox Korea specialises in children's shoes and clothing, distributing foreign brands, selling its own brands and making children's clothing through a subsidiary. It has exclusive contracts with about 30 premium kids' brands and sells through stores and an online mall. Founded in 2012 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017, it says it introduced Korea's first premium children's shoe select shop.

215600.text: SillaJen is a biotech company developing cancer treatments, including immuno-oncology therapies based on recombinant oncolytic viruses that multiply selectively in cancer cells, and mitotic checkpoint inhibitors. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016 as a technology growth company. It has 3 subsidiaries and holds global patent rights through its wholly owned subsidiary SillaJen Biotherapeutics.

215790.text: Inno Instrument makes and exports optical fibre fusion splicers and cleavers, supplying markets including China, North America, Europe and the Middle East. It is developing OTDR and power analyzer products and keeps costs down by producing both in-house and through its China unit. Founded in 2007 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017, it has 13 subsidiaries, including units in China, the US, Europe and India.

216050.text: Incross runs a digital advertising media representative business alongside a commerce business that offers one-stop services for commerce platforms. It has launched an AI-based content marketing platform that matches creators and automates performance reports. Founded in 2007 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016, it became a subsidiary of a new largest shareholder in 2026.

216080.text: Jetema is a biotech company that researches and develops hyaluronic acid fillers and botulinum toxin products. Founded in 2009, it entered medical aesthetics after a 2014 merger, won Korean approval for its toxin at the end of 2024 and launched the product in 2025. It has signed licensing deals with partners in China and Brazil and a toxin export contract with a partner in Thailand.

217190.text: Genesem develops, makes and sells automation equipment for back-end semiconductor processes, including HBM automation, EMI shielding, saw singulation and laser marking and cutting systems. Founded in 2000 to make chip manufacturing machinery, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015. It is headquartered in Incheon and is classified as a small and medium-sized venture company.

217270.text: Neptune develops and publishes mobile games, mainly casual titles, and runs the AD(X) and AdPie ad-tech platforms for advertising monetisation. It handles everything from user acquisition to ad monetisation in-house and is expanding in India and in its DSP business. Founded in 2012, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2016.

217330.text: Cytogen is a liquid biopsy company whose platform isolates, analyses and cultures circulating tumour cells (CTCs), with work in CTC research, anticancer drug evaluation, metastasis inhibitor research and Auto PRP-based regenerative medicine equipment. Founded in 2010 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2018, it has 4 unlisted subsidiaries. It set up Cytogen Japan in 2024 and has diversified through an acquisition.

217480.text: SD Biotechnologies sells mask packs and eye patches under its SNP cosmetics brand and also runs a food business under its own brand. It entered the cosmetics market in 2008 as a dermatology research institute and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017. It has 5 unlisted subsidiaries.

217500.text: Russell refurbishes semiconductor equipment, focusing on repair, modification and parts replacement for deposition tools. Through a subsidiary it also provides unmanned logistics solutions for smart factories. Founded in 2006, it listed on the KOSDAQ through a merger in 2018 and added the subsidiary in 2020.

217590.text: TMC makes cables, specialising in marine and optical communication cables, and also produces cables for nuclear power plants. It was established in 2012 through a spin-off, and its main customers are large Korean shipyards. The company says it holds more than about 50% of the Korean marine cable market, and it is expanding into power and telecom infrastructure.

217730.text: Kangstem Biotech works on stem cell therapies, cosmetics and new drugs. Its stem cell business isolates cord-blood-derived stem cells at high purity and cultures them in bulk, with a pipeline for atopic dermatitis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. Founded in 2010 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015, it has a subsidiary that develops exosome-based drugs.

217820.text: Wonik Pne makes equipment for secondary battery manufacturing, mainly formation and assembly process systems and cyclers for R&D, and also runs EV charging infrastructure and power plant power supply businesses. Founded in 1999 and listed on the KOSDAQ in 2015, it has 6 consolidated subsidiaries and set up a US unit in 2023 to expand overseas.

218150.text: Milae Bioresources makes feed and food products. Its feed division produces specially processed raw materials, functional ingredients and additives and makes pet health supplements under its own brand on an OEM/ODM basis, while its food division sells health supplements and produces beverages and HMR. Founded in 1998, it listed on the KOSDAQ in 2017 and has a contract with IFF.

218410.text: Rfhic is a semiconductor company whose main products are GaN transistors, power amplifiers and microwave generators, used in wireless communications infrastructure, defence and RF energy. The company says it has Korea's only mass-production technology for GaN transistors, which it uses to develop form-factor products for 5G SA networks.
